turned batman into nothing more complex then the punisher and an equally lazy back story for the same character, the joker was the star of the movie, while bruce wayne remained emotionless and stiff and batman basically operated in a gotham city that is so bizarre you fail to connect with it(or batman) on any level. it got worst with batman returns where they had penguins and clowns attacking gotham city, the penguim reduced to a sewer rat, rather then the sophisticated mob boss we know in the comics, c-grade romance between batman and the new villainess catwoman(but played exceptionally by michelle pfeifer) and bizarre sexual innuendo. it got worse when joel schumacher turned batman into a funny guy, turned gotham city from bizarre to outlandishly cartoony, introduced bat-nipples and bat credit cards. after i saw this movie, the first thing that popped into my mind was: wow! then i asked: is this the same company who released catwoman a couple of months ago? on the stop, i can say this was the best superhero movie of 2005, the best batman movie and one of the best, if not the best superhero movie of all times. ignoring the previous continuity of the original batman films, chris nolan and david goyer decided to re-invent batman by going back and for the first time recreating the origin story of batman. the movie tells the tale of one young boy named bruce wayne who's afraid of bats, he witnesses the murder of his parents by a small time thug named joe chill(just like in the comics), the movie narrates his coming of age and how he decided to become the violent creature of the night batman. the first of half of the film, is broken down in flashbacks that connect with the overall storyline. in the start of the movie, bruce is a nameless vagabond who finds himself locked up in a tibetan prison and out of focus, after getting involved in another prison fight, he gets sent to a private cell, where he is greeted by a man who seems to know his identity, a stranger known as ducard who works for an underground vigilante group called the league of shadows who offers bruce training to become what he's looking for: to be more then just a man. through the first half of the film we are guided through stages of bruce's early life. the latter half has bruce wayne returning to gotham to fight the crime and corruption of the city he wishes so much to defend and becoming the batman, while teaming up with some idealists. the movie delivers as a well-balanced action movie with drama that doesn't feel as awkward as say, spiderman 2. bruce wayne in the movie is someone you care about and his morals and his selflessness goes deeper then your average superhero. played by christian bale(now nobody has an excuse not to know this guy), he channels bruce's 3 personas with ease and you wonder if he was actually born to play this part. michael caine plays bruce's butler and father figure, alfred with competence, provides some clever sarcastic humor and connect well with he hero. gary oldman plays a different type of character, this time around a good guy, not only does he fit the part, he looks exactly like jim gordon. katie holmes is competent, but her role is rather disposable but thankfully her romantic involvement with the main character doesn't derail the movie. morgan freeman delivers as wayne's supplier of bad gadgets. villains in batman begins are no longer colorful and competing for most humorous performance and screen time, cillian murphy plays an impressive and creepy scarecrow, who breaths intelligence and cunning without falling into the typical villain stereotype, he's a sick person and filled with corruption, but he has real goals. the same could be said for ra's al ghul who's identity i won't reveal, a terrorist who tries to make a valid point for his actions(possibly better portrayed then most terrorists in action movies). batman himself as probably scarier then the villains, as nothing seems to stop him and he attacks his opponents viciously but with caution. for a character who has no super-powers, tricking your opponents into thinking you're some superhuman demonic creature is one amazing feat and the movie pulls this off quite well. other actors like rugter hauer and tom wilkison are also competent. the movie makes for good storytelling and character that feel true to life and camp free. and they finally made gotham city into something you can believe in, a city that looks pretty on the outside but on the inside it's rotten to the core, there's poverty, desperation,degradation, slums, corrupt city officials and corrupt police officers: all the elements for a crime movie(which is vital for the batman comics). the soundtrack is another high point in the film, deep, strong and moving. you can almost visualize the action just by hearing the songs. i'll be waiting for the sequel for sure, as batman is once again up there among the ranks of spiderman and the x-men.

christopher nolan is definitely one of today's most creative filmmakers, and one that has brought what is often considered "art-house" to the general eye, uniting all audiences effectively.

and whilst the dark knight is often considered perhaps his best film, batman begins, the first installment, is almost as good and an incredible film on its own.

the tone is mature, realistic and feels very close. it is more of a crime drama than a typical superhero story, and the inclusion of acclaimed dramatic actors such as morgan freeman and michael caine adds to it all. all of the cast overall do an incredible job.

overall, an incredible masterpiece with lots of breathtaking cinematography, cutting and editing, great action and beautiful messages.

definitely a film every lover of film should watch, whether you are into action or superhero movies or not!

batman has always been my favourite "superhero", eventhough he does not have any superpowers, which is also why he is so damn cool. he is not born with superpowers or anything, he just had a very tragic childhood with his parents getting killed in front of him, which is the main reason why he decides to become the protector of gotham. no superpowers, just his wits, combat training and gadgets! everything in this movie is perfection. the whole dark knight trilogy is perfection and it is one of my favourite trilogies of all time.

the cast is near perfect. everyone fit their role perfectly, except katie holmes as rachel dawes. she just looks way too young, like she is 16 years old. sorry katie, but that is just my opinion.

the story is so good. it is so interesting to see bruce wayne's training and what he went through before he became batman. the fights are amazing. the batsuit is so cool. it is also nice to see when he comes up with the ideas for everything when it comes to the gadgets, batcave, etc.

the chemistry and the jokes between bruce and alfred, and also between bruce and fox is so funny to watch.

the villains are so good as well. the only thing i would have wanted to be slightly different is ra's al ghul. he did not feel that super powerful as i would have wanted.

this movie is a perfect start to the perfect dark knight trilogy!

anyone who goes into this movie with any sort of expectations should stop. before you go see this movie, wipe the slate clean. don't even consider the original three(i don't count the last one. sucked way too bad.) as any point of reference. because, frankly, you'll be confused.

this movie was unbelievable. action was awesome, but not too much. it was much deeper with the emotion than ever before, especially with you know who about you know what at the you know where. (watch it and i'm pretty sure you'll know what i'm talking about.) the darkness portrayed in this movie was unlike anything i'd ever seen in a movie before. tim burton couldn't have gotten this close.

the actors were awesome. christian bale, who many people didn't think would do a good job, surpassed michael keaton and val kilmer. he captured both bruce wayne and batman better than anyone. morgan freeman is awesome. "small role" you might think, but sure is important. then michael caine as alfred. beautiful. gary oldman played the best jim gordon i've ever seen. he looked and acted like gordon should. liam neeson's played his part beautifully. but i better stop. if i continue on, i'll have to hit the spoiler button, and i don't want to ruin the movie for anyone.

bottom line, go see it yourself. 10 out of 10, and i'm really picky.

ever since the abomination of batman and robin, it was rapidly decreasing its fans and movie-goers. but batman is back from the grave after 8 years of disappointment. thanks to christopher nolan, the series was revived.

it stars christian bale, michael caine, liam neeson, katie holmes, gary oldman, cillian murphy, morgan freeman, etc.

in tone with the early "batman: year one" style comics. as a boy a young bruce wayne watched in horror as his millionaire parents were slain in front of his eyes, a trauma which led him to become obsessed with revenge but his chance is cruelly taken away from him by fate. after disappearing to the east where he seeks counsel with the dangerous but honorable ninja cult leader known as ra's al-ghul, he returns to his now decaying gotham city overrun by organized crime and dangerous individuals manipulating the system whilst the company he inherited is slowly being pulled out from under him. the discovery of a cave under his mansion, and a prototype armored suit leads him to take on a new persona, one which will strike fear into the hearts of men who do wrong - he becomes, batman. in the new guise, and with the help of rising cop jim gordon (gary oldman), batman sets out to take down the various nefarious schemes in motion by individuals such as mafia don falcone, the twisted doctor/drug dealer jonathan 'the scarecrow' crane (cillian murphy), and a mysterious third party that is quite familiar with wayne and waiting to strike when the time is right.

but this movie right here was better than batman and robin (due to the fact that the movie was very campy, cheesy, and weird).

so far, christopher nolan has made two very successful films to the series, so that adds up to one of the best superhero films ever.

batman begins gets 10 stars.

batman begins does what both burtons and schumachers failed on tim burton delivered a dark batman but there was no motivation or belief to the character, i have to admit i enjoyed batman forever it had great potential but the villains were too comical and not bad enough and what a mess the whole claw island thing turned out to be. batman and robin was just the campy 60s show set in modern day.

but nolan finally pulled it off his story wasn't set around the villain but batman himself and his journey from bruce wayne billionaire playboy to the dark night it explained everything from how he learned the skills that makes batman to why and where he gets his suit, it even shows you why he wears a cape

bale is the perfect batman/bruce wayne you can feel his pain and understand his motivation for ridding gotham of corruption and crime. i wasn't the biggest fan of michael cains performance he was a likable alfred but his accent was too cockney, katie holmes is great here too as bruce's childhood best friend(she is so sexy)liam neeson is one of my favourite actors of all time and pulled of a great job as ducard morgan freeman is top notch too one of the most underrated actors in this film is cillian murphy he is an excellent scarecrow hes always edgy but at the same time calm

when i heard gary oldman was james gordon i was surprised and couldn't see it working as all i could see was dracula and sirius black but i was pleasantly surprised with how he was as sgt gordon

final words mr nolan please make us a sequel

i don´t know if its just nostalgia, but damn do i still hold this great masterpiece dearly. all the action sequences and all the line delivery are so brilliant, the plot is also fantastic and to my knowledge also greatly comic accurate. christian bale was definitely the perfect casting as batman in this phenomenal movie. liam neeson (ra´s al ghul), gary oldman (james gordon), michael caine (alfred pennyworth) and morgan freeman (lucius fox) all did some amazing acting. hey where all just so greatly casted in this thrilling superhero-action-movie.

christopher nolan, you certainly never disappoint in directing masterpieces after masterpieces.

i definitely recommend everyone to give it one more watch, because it is just as good as it was when it first came out.

i´m happy to rate "batman begins" (11/10)

wow. i have just seen not only a phenomenal "comic book movie," but a truly dark spectacle of a movie. this movie works on so many levels. the cast, the script, direction, effects, they are all excellent! now, i must warn you, i have been obsessed with batman for a long, long time. i remember watching the batman tv show with adam west. i even have most of the old batman shows from the 40's. but with this move, i believe the series has hit its peak.

first of all, christian bale is a man-god. he is the best thing about the movie. he is perfect for batman and bruce wayne. i thought he conveyed the fanaticism of bruce wayne perfectly. his acting was top notch and as long as he stays batman, i have great hope for the series.

next up we have the rest of the cast and my, what a great ensemble this is. morgan freeman is great as fox but still seems only like a filler character. gary oldman is incredible as gordon, perfect casting right there. rutger haur, tom wilkenson, hell, even katie holmes in her small role was great. cillian murphy was creepy as hell, even without the scarecrows mask. i hope nolan and goyer decide to include him in future outings of the series.

nolan's direction and creativity shine through. i found the cinematography to be dark, much like insomnia. his added touches were ever present in the film, especially with the overall atmosphere.

now for the movie itself. everything works here. i spent most of the night reading the script when i got home from the show. it really does the film justice. the cast, even with the huge a-list names they have, no one really shines more than they should in their roles. everyone serves their purpose well.

the only beefs i have with this movie are subtle things such as christian bale changing his voice as batman, but when he yelled at the crooked cop that was redeemed. truly frightening. some scenes also look as if they were cut short and it does seem as if some of the better dialogue was cut out, especially in the parts with liam neeson.

overall, (i know you may have heard it before) batman begins marks a true return of the character. the movie is dark, scary(yes scary) and beautiful. my hat is off to everyone involved with the film especially bale and nolan. i can't wait for the sequel as this has been one of the best cinematic experiences of my life.

***10 out of 10***

it took sixty-five long years since first appearing in dc comics, but batman finally received cinematic justice in the summer of 2005. in truth, hollywood had taken an interest in the caped crusader after bob kane's creation made its debut in detective comics #27. but what emerged didn't come from a major studio with a budget similar to that of gone with the wind. rather, these were serialized matinee cheapies from tinseltown's poverty row, and the production values looked shoddy even back then. batman fared much better on the radio, where listeners could fill in the visuals with their own imaginations.

in the comic books, batman would undergo a makeover every decade or so, introducing robin as a sidekick in 1940 before later adding batwoman, batgirl, and bat-mite {remember him?} as supporting characters. in 1966 the campy "so bad it's good" series starring adam west premiered on television and reignited interest in the dark knight, especially among baby boomers. although tim burton's late eighties take had a darker tone than the television show, a certain campiness remained {the villains still overacted!}. as for joel schumacher, he nearly ruined the franchise after taking over for burton on batman forever and batman and robin, the latter of which george clooney continues to apologize for.

shortly after the start of a new millennium someone over at warner bros {which still owned the rights} thought it might be a novel idea to resurrect the caped crusader again....except this time turn back the clock to explore his superhero origins. in burton's batman, the director only paid lip service to the metamorphosis via a flashback sequence showing a prepubescent bruce wayne witnessing his parents' murders. it never really delved into his psyche not did explain how he got his batsuit, batmobile, batcave, and utility belt with various crime fighting gadgets. {after all, having the funds to purchase all that is one thing; acquiring them surreptitiously is another matter altogether.} neither burton nor schumacher were to be involved in the reboot, so the big question over at warners was: who could call the shots now?

christopher nolan had made a positive impression on me with his one-two punch of memento and insomnia. as far back as 2002 it was clear that nolan had the filmmaking vision to go far in the industry. so when i read that he was going to direct the newest batman movie, my initial reaction was somewhere along the lines of "oh, no. he's selling himself out to hollywood already!". boy....was i ever wrong about that!!!! instead, nolan turned out to be the franchise's savior, for not only did he agree to direct, but he also co-wrote the screenplay. nolan described the previous installments as more focused on style than substance, and he was convinced both could be achieved through his reimagining.

in batman begins, nolan continues to go back and forth in time by employing the nonlinear narrative hallmark of his previous films. for the sake of chronology my synopsis will start with a young bruce and his first encounter with chiroptophobia. he's playing on the sprawling family estate with childhood friend rachel dawes when the wooden planks on which he is standing give way, sending him falling below deep into a cavern populated by....yup, bats! also living with him and his parents at wayne manor is loyal butler alfred pennyworth (michael caine), and rachel's housekeeper mother.

it never really states what decade(s) batman begins is set in, but gotham city is gripped by an economic depression similar to that of the 1930's. rampant poverty brings about desperation, and because of that desperation gotham has evolved into a crime ridden cesspool that culminates in the murders of thomas and martha wayne. ironically, it's their legacy and the philanthropy of wayne enterprises that's kept gotham's financial heartbeat on life support. now that bruce's parents are gone, the wayne foundation is in the hands of the board of directors until the lad becomes an adult.

meanwhile, the city has gone to hell in a hand basket. the stench of organized crime is represented by carmine falcone (tom wilkinson), the al capone of gotham city. brazenly wielding his power like scarface, falcone has most of the police and judges on his payroll. one of the few policemen that can't be bought at any price is sergeant jim gordon (gary oldman), who watches on in disgust as fellow officers {including his partner} accept bribes from falcone to look the other way. like many honest officers, gordon is intimidated by the blue wall of silence that turns its nose down on the serpicos of the g. p. d. {besides, as he tells his colleague, "who is there to rat to?}

when we're introduced to a grown-up bruce wayne (christian bale), he's languishing in a chinese prison camp. since dropping out of princeton, bruce has been trotted the globe, living on a self-imposed hand-to-mouth existence while trying to better understand the criminal mentality. it's in jail that he meets henri ducard (liam neeson), the man who will become a mentor to the lost boy-man. ducard has the clout to arrange for bruce's immediate release, and urges him to enlist in the league of shadows, a secret illuminati-type society that for centuries has been dedicated to wiping out corruption.

the current leader of the league of shadows is ra's al ghul (ken watanabe), who rules from a himalayan mountaintop temple. when bruce arrives there with the blue poppy requested by ducard, he is immediately indoctrinated as his teacher instills in him all of the necessary mental and physical requirements. where the student and instructor differ, however, is their interpretation of justice. ducard has the old testament, eye-for-an-eye brand of justice while bruce, despite his tragedies, still believes in the new testament concept of trial of jury of peers. their differences come to a head that eventuates in the death of ra's al ghul and the destruction of the fortress.

when bruce returns to gotham after a seven year absence {he'd been declared dead for legal reasons}, alfred has tended to the family estate while rachel (katie holmes) is now an assistant district attorney. wayne enterprises's board of directors have voted to take the company public, leaving bruce as a minority shareholder. meanwhile, lawlessness in gotham has only gotten worse! by this time, bruce has conceived the idea of a secret alter ego to strike terror into the hearts of gotham city's criminal underbelly. and what better symbol to do that with than his own fear? bats!!

the cave bruce fell into as a boy will serve as the perfect hideaway, but he will still need the special tools to perform his job as batman. and in the applied sciences division of wayne enterprises is the ideal man to assist him. lucius fox (morgan freeman) will be to bruce wayne what q was to james bond: the gadget genius who provides him with the equipment {original designed for the military}. there's a kevlar bodysuit, an unusual cape, and the armored vehicle on steroids that will become his batmobile. {don't we all wish we had something like that during rush hour?} 😆

batman begins is easily the finest treatment of the caped crusader to land on either the big or small screen {that is, until superceded by the dark knight}. nolan and leading actor bale can take the lion's share of credit for the great leap forward insofar as quality is concerned. it's a stylish meditation on the contrast between retribution and justice, and nolan handles bruce wayne's journey with intelligence and grace. he even throws in a little historical context too, with alfred commenting that part of the batcave was used by bruce's ancestors as an underground railway to escort runaway slaves to freedom. nolan also tosses in bits about the london fire of 1666, the black plague, and the sacking of constantinople.

portraying batman/bruce wayne, bale dominates in what could be considered a dual role despite being the same person. and what a supporting cast nolan assembled to back bale up!! batman begins would be the first of seven collaborations between nolan and caine, including two sequels, making the veteran british actor a lucky charm for the director. oldman, freeman, neeson, watanabe, and cillian murphy {here playing the scarecrow} would also reunite with nolan on subsequent projects.

the previous batman films placed too much emphasis on elaborate set decoration and art direction. nolan wanted his gotham city to resemble a typical metropolitan centre, such as new york or chicago, and often used real buildings to film interior and exterior sets. working in tandem with production designer nathan crowley, the gotham of batman begins looks spectacular without being ostentatious, and crowley did similar wonders with iceland subbing nicely for the himalayas. nolan's frequent cinematographer wally pfister is another asset; his photography gives the nighttime scenes something that was missing from the preceding pictures: the look of film noir.

batman begins was the booster vaccination the franchise needed after the schumacher debacles. for loyal fans of the caped crusader, this was the batman movie they'd been waiting their whole lives to see. however, it should be noted that membership with the dc/marvel comics universe isn't necessary for any given person to enjoy batman begins. thanks to nolan's vision, it can be appreciated by virtually every demographic. 🔚

an awe-inspiringly, intricately worked superhero movie. like the instances throughout it that explain how batman is inspired into picking his equipment (the spiked gauntlets, fire-proof cape), everything about the movie assembles into an enthralling whole. with an almost perfect cast, ample production values, seamless cinematography and music, and script that never lets up, no movie in the genre betters it. in fact it raises the bar for all superhero movies, keeping the tone gritty and real, yet doing every bit of justice to the characters.

christian bale is batman, covering every nuance of the character; the journeying, the reactions. he conveys the most cerebral batman yet, expressing the characters strengths and what sets him apart from other superheroes. much better than the darkly humorous keaton and the plain bored kilmer.

michael caine forms a pillar for the storyline and helps draw out the background of bruce wayne. caine simply is alfred, leaving no doubt that anyone could have played the role better. morgan freeman's role is almost ethereal in it's presence which makes it very fitting for his commanding gravitas.

katie holmes has been decried as being a bad pick for her character but considering the limited scope in terms of the story, she didn't do a bad job. maggie gyllenhaal is taking over the character in the sequel, but it can be argued that it is mostly due to the politics behind the movie-making.

cillian murphy impresses in his role as the seriously flawed genius. he earnestly conveys what makes the character tick.

the guy playing carmine falcone is the most major let-down. but at least he shouldn't be in the sequel.

gary oldman isn't given much to do, but he does none of it wrong and we can all look forward to his expanded role in the future instalments.

one gripe is that the movie has a bit too much of a glossed over look to its visuals, this can be attributed to the high contrast lighting in the night and dark sequences which naturally there are many. but it helps to give the movie a more engaging polish and is a small niggle at the cost of realism.

batman begins is a stylish and slick action film. it has everything you could want in a film, emotion, action, love. i was worried that this film would be another george clooney disaster but it was brilliant. i didn't believe you could beat the michael keaton batman films but i was very much mistaken. christian bale is an excellent choice and i am thoroughly looking forward to the next instalment of batman films. not only was christian bale an excellent choice but the supporting cast was also perfect with brilliant performances from cillian murphy, morgan freeman, michael caine (obviously) and liam neeson. overall i enjoyed the film immensely.

watched batman begins starring christian bale(american psycho) as bruce wayne/batman, sir michael caine(the italian job) as alfred pennyworth wayne's loyal butler and mentor, morgan freeman(the shawshank redemption) as lucius fox,gary oldman(the fifth element) as sergeant james gordon, tom wilkinson(the patriot) as carmine falcone crime boss of gotham's criminal underworld,ken watanabe(the last samurai) as ra's al ghul , rutger hauer(blade runner ) as william earle ,the lovely katie holmes(phone booth) as rachel dawes and liam neeson(schindler's list) as henri ducard . one of the most memorable films from the opening of the film and to the credits,the film has non-linear element of storytelling,a strong premise and some very intuitive twists and turns. this is one the best origin movies for batman . due to the fact that all the actors play up to there parts and no just one of them steals the show it also once again an amazing performance from christian bale plays a complex bruce wayne and the best batman liam neeson plays an excellent mentor to bruce wayne which is awesome also i enjoyed the whole bruce wayne being trained by the league of shadows/assassins which was cool knowing that batman is ninja/samurai of the superhero world ,also amazing direction from christopher nolan(insomnia) costume design from lindy hemming(casino royale),amazing score from hans zimmer(the last samurai ) & amazing production design from nathan crowley(behind enemy lines) this film is great opening to nolan's batman saga also one my of my all time favorite superhero movies of all time, and the best batman film of all time 10/10

wow!! simply wow. that's a one word answer to how the film is. the usp of this film is that it does not portray the batman as an outright super hero – whacking criminals with super power but shows a vulnerable bruce wayne who has to be shaped into a combat machine to be a super hero. this makes the film 'connect' instantly to its audience.

the story explains the origins of the character of bruce wayne and starts with bruce (christian bale), as a gypsy traveling the world starting fights with petty criminals to shadow over his guilt over the death of his parents. he is greeted by the mysterious henri ducard who along with a legendary warrior ra's al ghul, teach him to turn fear against those who prey on the fearful. bruce takes him up on his offer and learns to become a warrior of justice only to rebuff the laws of the monastery blindly and return to gotham city to save it from 'dying' in the hands of the mob. things are worse than ever in gotham...carmine falcone, a mobster, owns most of the city's officials, and as he runs drugs and gambling. he begins with his bat-suit, weaponry, and bat- mobile. his trusted aides for the 'mission' are his trusty butler, alfred (michael caine), the head of science divisions at wayne enterprises, lucius fox (morgan freeman), the only decent cop left in gotham, gordon (gary oldman), and his old flame, now the assistant d.a. rachel dawes (katie holmes – she disappointed with mediocre acting though). but his test lies when he meets his ultimate nemesis – ducard who wants to destroy gotham in order to save the savaged livelihood of many.

the film is not about firepower (though it has excellent fight sequences) but about 'mind over body' type tactical warfare blended with a comic book persona that batman is. it's not about the heroics of a hero but the struggle to become great and the insecurity which induces one to strive. a hero has to grow as a 'person' first and then as a 'super-hero'. the fights are great, the gadgets all there, the plot is thorough and exciting, and gotham looks great. batman really is frightening & menacing (and lethal!) the film wins hearts as it is not conventional, corny, over-digitalized comic book –to-celluloid adaptation; but a well orchestrated drama – crime feature film.

whether you're or aren't a fan of christopher nolan or batman fanatic, you'll enjoy every single second of the movie. batman finally begins from here.... (only to be overshadowed by the legend – the joker in the dark knight —phew!! what an anti climax to the 'hero' stuff – a birth of a super hero in 'batman begins' who fights his way to be one – to the birth of a super anti-hero in 'the dark knight' – i thought batman was good but joker even better!! )

9 out of 10 definitely. comic-book films grow up with this one... the franchise fell earlier only to rise in 2005 and again in 2008

this was the best batman movie ever and christian bale was the best batman ever!!! i expected very little going into the movie. i'd seen the trailer & it looked great but i couldn't help but remember the other batman movies that were.....well, let's face it.....awful!! i was blown away by the end of the movie. bale was magnificent, the special effects were great, scenery awesome, and the supporting actors, i mean come on, what can you say, amazing!!! caine, neeson, freeman, murphy, oldman, all amazing!!! just the right amount of comic relief as well. times when the entire theater laughed out loud!!! i can't wait for the next batman.

finally, a director that takes a story seriously and does not mess it up with "bright" ideas. this is the caped crusader i know from my childhood, this is the caped crusader that they should have made in the first place. this is the one pillar all should look to when it comes to creating a comic-to-screen feature. or - for that matter - a book-to-screen.

this one made my day - and night. watching late in the evening and finishing it around 1am seemed to be a good idea after doing so. why? this is a dark movie where bird chirping outside would be a bit - off. too bad i missed it in the theater, as this clearly is a theater-kind-of-movie.

the f/x are as expected state of the art, but the little surprise in this one is the drama and the excellent performances by a range of well known and fine actors. i have to say i like the style of morgan freeman - and even though not in a main role, he plays his part superbly also in this movie.

in this movie, nolan brings us back to the beginning and retells the story of batman. and he tells the story right, he tells the story so fans of the original batman recognizes him. oh, boy, do i look forward to the next one...

o what a tragic tale it is of the batman film series! batman was at its peak in the late 80s and early 90s with tim burton's dizzying incarnations of the dark knight. two films that inhabited the darkest recesses of the character in ways i never thought could be possible. in 1995 it all came crashing down when burton was dismissed and that most terrible of filmmakers took the directors chair, joel schumacher.

and the decline in quality was shocking. his two outings stripped batman of all his shadowy mystery and intrigue, and replaced it with camp theatrics, empty-headed plots and snazzy visuals with nothing underneath. it seemed schumacher had managed to do what batman's enemies never could. he had killed the dark knight.

for eight years it seemed batman was buried in a grave even he couldn't claw his way out of. but all that changed with christopher nolan. nolan emerged on the film circuit with the astonishing memento, a beautifully crafted murder mystery that scaled impressive heights by telling the story in reverse. memento established nolan as one of the most promising filmmakers today.

when it circulated he was directing a new batman film, batman begins, that took the whole story back to its roots, it made me wonder if even a director of nolan's talents could salvage batman. and the answer is...yes, absolutely!

batman begins is a film that really flies high. nolan gets right inside the dark psychology of the character, and turned out one of the most intelligent and thought-provoking superhero films ever made.

this is a film that takes batman back to his beginnings. we learn everything about him. how he became obsessed with bats. his parents' murder when he was a child. watching him grow consumed by vengeance. travelling the world searching for answers. and finding his true calling.

batman begins is a film of two distinct halves. the first half details everything about batman's origins and its this part of the film where christopher nolan seems the most at home. the part where the orphaned bruce wayne has to find his direction in life. so it was important that they find the right actor who can embody tightly controlled anger and channel it into the persona of batman. and christian bale is that actor.

bale has always been an actor worthy of notice. after i saw the machinist, a part that required him to lose half his body weight i was convinced he is an actor with an almost obsessive desire to embody a role. and its this quality that makes him perfectly suited as bruce wayne/batman.

its a good solid hour before we even see bale in the cape and cowl. this allows enough time to explore bruce wayne's struggle with his dark half. never has batman's origins been told in such detail. something not even tim burton's batman films can attest to.

there are wonderful scenes in this part of the film with the conflicted bale and his teacher, henri ducard (an excellent liam neeson), a member of the league of shadows. an organisation that wants to harness bruce's need for justice (or revenge). neeson gets to play a bit of an obi-wan kenobi, and gets a lot of rich dialogue to spout:

"a vigilante is just a man lost in the scramble for his own gratification."

the first half of batman begins is beautifully constructed. each part of his origin falls into place a piece at a time. bruce wants to kill his parents murderer, and is beaten to it by somebody else, robbing him of his revenge. and i particularly loved the way bruce comes to embody the symbol of the bat. in an ingenious twist, bats are what he fears most, but ducard teaches him to embrace his fear and use it against those who prey on the fearful.

when bruce returns to gotham city, now the origins are out the way, the story really takes off. and the way bruce rediscovers himself as the batman is very satisfying. there are scenes right out of a comic book, like when bruce discovers the batcave beneath wayne manor, and is enveloped in a swarm of bats and just stands there.

when bale becomes the batman, he seems for all the world a truly unearthly creature. nolan makes sure he cuts a striking figure against the gotham skyline. and bale's piercing eyes and voice ensure this is one batman you won't forget.

also worthy of mention is the really exceptional cast nolan has put together. just look who we have here! aside from bale and neeson, we have michael caine who makes a wonderful alfred. gary oldman's a revelation as a young commissioner gordon. the always excellent morgan freeman as bruce's weapons designer. and even rutger hauer and tom wilkinson are here too.

cillian murphy is a fine young actor but i think he was a little too young to be playing the part of a criminal psychologist, and one of the film's villains, the scarecrow. but nonetheless he's totally professional, and infuses his performance with his trademark intensity.

really the only black mark on bb is katie holmes, who's a thoroughly unconvincing assistant da. she only gives one of her insipid performances, and she's just shoehorned in as the token love interest.

fans of tim burton's batman sagas may be disappointed this gotham city has none of the dark psychological atmospherics he brought to the table. it could be any city in the world. and i was disappointed the batmobile is a tank instead of its usual streamlined self. but remember, they're still sorting things out, and hopefully the batmobile will metamorphose into its true form as time (and sequels) go by.

overall though, batman begins is a triumph. it's a wonderfully told story. brilliantly directed, acted and wondrous to behold. batman is back, and he's better than ever!

since his first dramatic appearance in detective comics in 1939, batman has grown to become a pop-culture icon. from movie serials in the 40's, to a classic campy tv show in the 60's, to a solid animated series in the 90's, fans have thrilled to the super heroics of this unique character. however, as a film franchise, he has brought results that were somewhat less than impressive creatively. while the tim burton directed films, batman and batman returns were stylish and dark, they also suffered from plot holes you could drive a batmobile through. then joel schumacher introduced a day-glo sensibility to the dark knight in batman forever, before drowning the character in ludicrous costumes (a bat suit with nipples???), pun-filled foes, and whiney sidekicks in the lousy batman & robin. by then, batman as cinematic property had become a laughingstock. fortunately, indie film director christopher nolan reinvigorates the franchise in glorious form in batman begins, a reboot of the batman legend that, for the first time, puts the focus squarely on our hero and not on the over-the-top villains of past films. nolan also bases the film in a strong semblance of reality that allows the audience to not only accept the possibility of the winged vigilante, but embrace it as well.

most fans already know the story of how wealthy bruce wayne (christian bale) loses his parents when they are slain during an attempted robbery, but the movie also tells how he chose the bat as his symbol, as well as the steps needed to become the avenger of the night that he turns into. disillusioned and frustrated by gotham city's corrupt judicial system, the young wayne goes abroad to study the criminal mind. later, while locked in an asian prison, wayne is recruited by the enigmatic ducard (liam neeson), who offers him a path in which to focus his anger and hone his skills. wayne eventually joins his new mentor as a recruit in the mysterious league of shadows, headed by the sinister ra's al ghul (ken wantanabe). eventually, wayne realizes that he cannot follow the league's extreme methods of dispensing justice and returns to gotham to forge his own way. it soon turns out that wayne's return is just in time as gotham falls prey to a fear epidemic engineered by the twisted dr. jonathan crane aka "the scarecrow" (cillian murphy) and a familiar figure from wayne's past.

from the top on down, this film is blessed with a solid cast that adds wonderfully to nolan's vision. as the title hero, christian bale blows all other batman portrayers out of the water with his intense and scary take of the role. this is a batman that you not only fear, but can relate to as well. in fact, he turns in the definitive performance. michael caine adds warmth and humor as wayne's trusty butler, alfred. liam neeson does a great variation of his usual mentor roles as ducard, a man with his own surprising secret. as an assistant da and wayne's childhood friend, katie holmes does a nice job with what is basically a thankless role. cillian murphy makes for a perfectly creepy scarecrow, while morgan freeman is solid as usual as the man who provides batman's wondrous car and gadgets. gary oldman is wonderfully cast against type as jim gordon, one of gotham's few honest cops. the scene in which he drives the tank-like batmobile is a sheer delight.

the screenplay by nolan and david goyer (who wrote the blade films) is awash with characterization and motivation...something that you don't see in many comic book films as a rule. in fact, you get so engrossed by the proceedings that you almost forget that you are watching a "superhero" film in the first place. the special effects are used to enhance the story and not overpower it, while the set design pictures a gotham that is a unique cross of chicago, new york and hong kong. if there is a flaw, it lies in some of the fight sequences. done in close-ups and quick cuts, they can get frustrating for those who want to see more of batman's fighting style. however, this is very minor since the story never ceases to grasp your attention.

in the end, nolan and his superb cast and crew succeed in achieving what was once thought impossible: the resurrection of a film franchise that, if not dead, was at least on life support. as a result, batman is once again flying high and batman begins is a film that i wholeheartedly recommend.

i am officially impressed by "batman begins". it exceeded by many, many, many orders of magnitude all of my expectations (meaning, they were very low). i had no idea i could be so enthusiastic about a (recent) movie.

where do i begin ? well, the subject: batman. the only well-known character worthy of the name "superhero" that isn't "super" at all, which says a lot. you might even say this movie isn't a "prequel", but a whole new restart of the entire franchise, and i hope that when (not if) they decide to make the next one, they'll maintain same style.

the actors ? most of the main characters were almost perfectly casted. christian bale (equilibrium) as bruce wayne was just the right mix between muscle and looks, and even if he does seem pretty stiff at times, he fits the character perfectly. michael caine as alfed (the butler), morgan freeman as fox (call him the "tech guy") liam neeson as ducard (the "inspiration" figure)... they all fit the roles they played like a glove, i couldn't even imagine who else would have been better instead. gary oldman as gordon was slightly disappointing, but only because he had way too little screen time. katie holmes as "the girl" was so-so, i would have expected a less cute-and-cuddly-looking actress casted for that part, but she also played her role quite well.

the plot ? ah, the weak spot of all comic-book adaptations. now, that one was the biggest surprise of all, and a very pleasant one indeed. there is no major bullshit in there. almost everything makes perfect sense. only in a very few short scenes you start to go "now, wait, that can't really happen, now can it?", but those moments are quickly dismissed by the ensuing action or plot development. there's quite a bit of "deviation" in the story from what you might come to know from the established franchise, but all of them are for the better (and more "believable").

there's so much more to say, but i don't want to spoil the fun. go see the movie if you haven't already.

this movie is an impeccable start to the batman/the dark knight trilogy and does a nearly perfect setting up batman, bruce wayne, gotham, and the rest of the main characters in gotham. the plot, settings, theme, dialogue, characters, character scenes, character development, actor performances, deaths, soundtrack, cinematography, choreography, visuals, cgi, practical effects, plot twists, opening scene, and ending are all impeccable. christian bale is nearly perfect as the leading role of bruce wayne / batman. michael caine as alfred, liam neeson as ducard, katie holmes as rachel dawes, and gary oldman as jim gordon are all nearly perfect in their starring roles. cillian murphy as dr. jonathan crane, tom wilkinson as carmine falcone, rutger hauer as earle, linus roache as thomas wayne, mark boone junior as flass, ken watanabe as ra's al ghul, morgan freeman as lucius fox, larry holden as finch, gerald murphy as judge faden, colin mcfarlane as loeb, sara stewart as martha wayne, gus lewis as bruce eayne - age 8, richard brake as joe chill, and rade sherbedgia as homeless man are all impeccable to incredible in their starring and supporting roles. this movie does an impeccable job developing batman, bruce wayne, gotham city, and the chemistry between all the characters. i love all the villians and all the chemistry between all the characters like christian bale and michael caine, christian bale and katie holmes, christian bale and gary oldman, katie holmes and cillian murphy, and christian bale and morgan freemen. the ending of this movie is impeccable and the action epic, epic, superhero, tragedy, action, crime, drama, and thriller aspects are all done nearly perfectly. i absolutely recommend you watch this movie if you like batman films, christopher nolan films, or if you like action epics, epics, superhero films, tragedy films, action films, crime films, drama films, or thrillers. i rate this movie a 9.8 out of 10.

christopher nolan has created a universe for batman that is beyond our wildest expectations. we get to see bruce wayne, from the hurt child at his parent's murder, over a young man consumed by rage and guilt, transform into the heroic identity of the batman. christian bale performs amazingly as wayne, giving us a deep glance into the character's dark soul. he is equally outstanding as the man in the cape and cowl, bringing menace to every word and importance to every look. michael keaton will always be my childhood's batman, but bale has brought the bat back into my adult life.

the other actors shine as well. this is bar none the best ensemble cast for a superhero movie and even one of the best casts i've seen in a long time. from the endearing and witty michael caine (alfred), to the always splendid morgan freeman (lucius fox), the lovely katie holmes (rachel dawes) and the utterly classy liam neeson (ducard), bruce's allies and mentors are indeed a delight to watch. even more so are the villains, exploring all different shades of evil in gotham, with ken watanabe (ra's al ghul), tom wilkinson (falcone), rutger hauer (earle) and the outstanding cillian murphy (jonathan crane / scarecrow) all giving deliciously nuanced performances.

christopher nolan and his cinematographer wally pfister really brought to the film what they promised: an epic scope, beautiful shots reminiscent of "laurence of arabia" and "blade runner" and a return to the traditional, but by no means bland or uninspired, action adventure story. it has amazing dramatic flow, good dialogue, fantastic characters and an intelligent, layered plot.

a great movie, the very best its genre has to offer and a cinematic treat to any film fan.

i just want to say, this movie made me so happy for the franchise, i was practically crying with joy when i realized what a complete 180 has occurred since batman and robin and batman forever.

great acting. excellent plot line. good musical score. good action. believable, and a truly enjoyable film experience. bale is perfect as batman, he receives great support from a lot of the cast - freeman, caine, etc.

the dialogue was truly superb at times as well, it was a nice change from watching revenge of the sith earlier this summer. good lines, delivered at good times. this is what a film should be, and this is the justice batman deserves.

just do yourself a favor and go see it.

what a film, i mean comparing that to the other batman films this one blows them away, i mean bale out does himself, its just great how he changes his voice form bruce to the more macho batman and pulls it of so well and liam has always been one of my fave actors and in this film he does not disappoint, great film, great baddie (scarecrow owns) and all in all an amazing film, one of the best comic films of them all. katie holmes wasn't that good, i've never enjoyed watching her she always seems to act to hard or put to much into a scene, where as bale pulled his role of perfectly showing up holmes. then there's michael caine, hes so good, hes not even good hes amazing, hes genuine british accent which goes so well with his role as a butler plus he just is one of the most awesome actors out there at the minute. and yet another favourite of mine, mr freeman, he pulls his role of perfectly, not white as high profile as other films, he plays a more sub dued role but even so he adds that touch of perfection to the film which really does finish it off.

will i see it again, well i already have

this movie was absolutely dark, thrilling, and exciting. christian bale who played batman was terrific and all of these great actors michael caine, liam neeson, gary oldman, and morgan freeman. the movie was shot in chicago such as wayne tower which is the board of trade building, and the tumbler chase scene at the lower wacker drive. also, the special effects of the monorail down la salle street looks great. this movie is one of my best films.

he finally makes sense. for more than 10 years any one walking in off the streets would be totally baffled by the thought of a man dressing up as a bat. why a bat? isn't that sort of random? this film explains it. this film makes plausible the fantastic. christian bale not only looks the part of the playboy, but he is fantastic as batman as well. michael caine is a fantastic alfred, playing it as stern but loving. liam neeson shows once again that he is extraordinary at playing the mentor. cillian murphy is fantastic as the creepy scarecrow. morgan freeman plays the "q" type character, supplying bruce with all his tools. this batman film does what even recent comics doesn't: makes it real and still fun. in closing, i loved this movie and everyone who enjoys good stories should see it.

it is hard to judge this version of batman compared to its previous (few) movies; that is, the absurdity of those interpretations of the dark knight were just about ridiculous enough to make any comparisons rather insulting to this fresh vision of the most popular comic book character of the 20th century. this isn't the nippled costume wearer who drools over poison ivy and offers his bat-credit card to buy her gifts. this is... far from that.

batman begins takes us, as the title suggests, to the roots. a boy's world is shattered by two bullets that take his parents away forever, and he might as well have died there with them; his demons scream in his ears ever since as he grows first into a bitter and angry young man, and then into an obsessive wanderer with vague ambitious of restoring justice and protecting the innocent from those who would pray upon them - somehow.

we watch bruce wayne's fall and rise in his most fascinating portrayal by christian bale; his work is excellent, maintaining the brooding, dark moods that rage within the character and maintaining a bitter sense of humor none of those who played the same role before - perhaps with the exception of michael keaton - managed to even come close to.

the greatest strength of the film is not even the excellent supporting cast that seems to be having genuine fun with the whole ride; morgan freeman, gary oldman, michael caine, liam neeson, they all carry the movie just far enough to justify caped crusader not even be _seen_ until halfway through the movie, without taking anything away from its value - and, indeed, it only lends strength to his first appearance, making the gadgets in that utility belt actually have meaning after we witness the costumeless wayne almost fall to his death in his first attempt at rooftop jumping.

perhaps a sore point of the movie could be considered to be the presence of katie holmes; she's cute and everything, but i can't help but notice the undertones of teen soap opera in every line she speaks, and truly lacks the intensity required for a supposed idealist trying to make a difference in the most corrupt city in the world; gotham city.

last night i attended a midnight showing of this movie and it blew me away. christopher nolan deserves a bow for the best batman-heck, best movie of the year. while i always enjoy comic book and action films there have a lot of dull flops( hulk, electra...)these past years. but batman begins makes the whole genre so much more fresh, original and exciting. i judge comic book films by their ability to entertain with action and special effects, not great plots, characters or dialog; i leave that type of criticism for dramas and war epics and whatnot. yet batman begins deserves a lot more praise and recognition for what it is- superior movie-making.

christian bale gives a great performance as bruce wayne/batman. as does also supporting cast liam neeson, morgan freeman, michael caine and even katie holmes. the movie takes place before the original batman movies and tells how and why bruce wayne becomes batman. from the reason why he dressed himself in a bat costume, the batmobile, the bate cave all is explained. the action and fighting is incredible, realistic and gritty; the movie is fast-paced and engrossing and will leave you absolutely stunned. 10/10

christopher nolan has created the best batman film ever, with a plot that makes the masked hero's evolution into a champion of justice believable. a superlative christian bale, perfect for expressiveness and interpretative ability, flanked by a cast of the highest quality which sees morgan freeman, michael caine, leam neeson and gary oldman in the key roles. vivid settings, gotham almost palpable in its dark reality sees its favorite son evolve from the condition of privileged to that of a symbol of justice. simply the best superhero film ever produced, surpassed perhaps only by its sequel, the dark knight.

warner bros. released four previous live-action batman films. those films are not related to batman begins. what the title of this film indicates is that this is the beginning of a new series. after the fiasco that was 1997's batman & robin we could have declared that series dead. here, director christopher nolan and screenwriter david goyer attempt to bring a more faithful adaptation of the comic book. there have been so many incarnations of batman in the comic books that i really don't know what that's supposed to mean.

what makes batman begins such a great film is that it allows the audience a better chance of getting to know the character of batman/bruce wayne. the film explores wayne's back story to every single detail. after you're done watching this film you could probably call yourself an expert in batman's genesis.

however, the film has its flaws. the scarecrow for instance is an example. i understand the character's purpose in this film, but like dr. doom in the fantastic four movie of this year, he doesn't really do anything special.

rating: 4 (****) out of (****)

features amazing performances by christian bale, michael caine, morgan freeman, and liam neeson. bale is physically the best batman to appear on the big screen to date. performance-wise i do not know if he is technically yet the best. let's see how he does in the sequel.

this is the most incredible batman movie i have ever seen, when you consider both the keaton/kilmer/clooney series and the bale series. i think i like this film just a hair better than the dark knight. there is perfection in how the filmmakers tell the story of batman's origins. i'm not speaking of faithfulness to the comics, because i don't bother reading the comics. i'm speaking of pure film-making quality, cinematography, acting, music, and directing. the pace of storytelling was perfect; there was a lot of story to tell in this film but they did not overload it. there were no slow parts, and no cramming of stuff into a short period of time like they had in spider-man 3. the placement and usage of flashbacks was done well too. i like how half of the film was devoted to batman's training, and the other half devoted to his first major campaign against crime in gotham city. it took me a couple viewings to completely understand all that was going on but i liked how they tied the league of shadows to his training and then to being his ultimate enemy later in the film. ra's al guhl was awesomely played by liam neeson. the teamwork between him and scarecrow, very well done. and of course there's the musical score, provided to us by the musical genius of hans zimmer. although the soundtrack for the dark knight is superior, it largely contains the same music and is very, very good. the music really set the mood and the power of the film quite well. i also highly approve of the choices of michael caine to play alfred, and morgan freeman is amazing in almost any movie he does. any movie gets extra points just for having morgan freeman in it. while the tim burton films were enjoyable, i like that this movie was more realistic without over the top camp or art deco. it looked like real life, not fantasy. not over-stylized like the joel schumaker ones. simply perfect. i can't even find anybody in the film that needs a punch in the face!

the filmmakers have set the bar really, really high for the new batman series with batman begins. miraculously, equaled their success with their release of the dark knight. because of these two films, the 3rd batman movie has two tough acts to follow. let us hope the series is not ruined.

see my profile to understand my rating philosophy.

finally a film which lives up the hype, and more. if george clooney killed batman, christian bale has well and truly brought him back to life, with a vengeance. batman begins is as about as far removed from the joel schumacher-inspired disaster that was batman and robin as is possible to be. where schumacher seemed to just throw a full palette of colour at the film, christopher nolan has returned to batman's roots, and has brought back the original, and definitive dark knight. he is once again the heroic anti-hero, and not the cut-from-the-template typical clean-cut hero that schumacher turned him in to. spiderman/peter parker he ain't. the new batman is a much darker creature, not solely driven by the inane desire to do good. instead he is revealed to be a much more complicated individual, angry, grief-stricken.and driven by desire to wreak vengeance on the criminal underworld of gotham city that took his parents from him.

the film reflects this new, less clean-cut, almost more sinister batman. the tone is one of a delicious darkness, with precious little sunlight allowed in. taking it's source material from the batman: year one comics, the campness of the 1960s adam west series is well and truly gone. and no robin in sight! the plot is an unusual one though, as rather than having just one nemesis to battle, he faces many different foes throughout the film, highlighting the desolate, god-forsaken nature of gotham, and the size of batman's task to restore justice to the city - and mirroring the task of director nolan to resurrect the batman franchise!

however, this darkness is more than compensated for by the sheer star power present in the film. morgan freeman, michael caine, liam neeson, gary oldman, linus roache, tom wilkinson, rutger hauer, katie holmes, and ken watanabe all provide superb stellar support. caine in particular clearly revels in the role of alfred, bruce wayne's butler and mentor. oldman, playing completely against type, is the world-weary but honest sergeant gordon (obviously destined to become commissioner gordon) and, for a man so often a brilliantly effective bad guy, is surprisingly believable as a nice guy.

the star of the piece though, is of course christian bale. the ultimate method actor who famously slimmed down to a walking skeleton for the machinist, after bulking up for american psycho, has regained his former muscular frame to be bruce wayne. he brings a new intensity to the role which really captures the full essence of being batman, something even michael keaton did not fully manage.

the film has everything required to be a top film. adrenaline-pumping action, a wide array of gadgets, an exhilarating car chase and a fight against evil (as well as the obligatory romance). but the important core of the story is one of a man's struggle with himself, the fight to find a purpose for his life amidst his inner conflict, and overcome his own demons of grief and anger. at the film's heart is a real human story, and all the action and gadgets serves to amplify rather than obscure or pad out the film.

most probably the best batman yet, the way is set for bale to don the cape once more in a sequel to the prequel, and for once it will be a sequel welcomed with open arms. the only question remains at the end is whether or not this film (or films) will tie in with tim burton's original batman, or if it will plough its own, new path. the intriguing ending leaves both options open.

i am neither a comic book fan nor a super hero fan and i am generally not a connoisseur of action movies but my husband is and i knew he would want to see this movie so we went to a midnight showing. this was a great movie! christian bale is excellent as the caped crusader, having the ability to show the torment and determination of this human super hero. morgan freeman, gary oldman, michael caine, rutger hauer and liam neeson were great. i know little of katie holmes and i was a bit surprised at the mention that she discovers who he is but it ties in with the idea that they cannot have a romance between them. the imagery is stunning and the reality of this hero's potential is fascinating. the explanations of the origin of the suit, vehicle and "gadgets" make the story more interesting. the evolution of the boy who loses his parents to a man who truly wants to help people is inspiring. i rarely see movies in the theatre these days but i would go see this one again. i can't wait for the sequel.

this story gave the true essence of batman. i try not to have expectations when attending films, but even if i had had expectations they would have and were met with this film. the attention to detail, keeping the dark undertones, the character development all created the ultimate batman experience. chritian bale did an excellent job, this coming from a huge michael keaton fan. i cannot wait for a sequel to this series of batman stories if they continue with the same director and caliber of actors that graced batman begins--liam neeson, morgan freeman, gary oldman, michael caine. the only character/actor i felt fell short was the character played by katie holms.

i am not a huge batman fan, although i did enjoy the first 3 movies and when i was younger i was a regular viewer of the animated series. however, i didn't believe that any of the movies had accurately captured what batman is all about. the first movie was almost all jack nicholson, the second just didn't have a whole lot of action, and batman forever had far too much comedy in my opinion. batman and robin, well, i don't think i need to say anything about that movie.

i was really excited to see batman begins, because it looked like they had finally made a more gritty and less outrageous batman movie. let's just say that after seeing it, it definitely exceeded my highest expectations. even if you aren't a big batman fan, this is just a great movie in general. it has enough action, the right amount of comedy, some excellent drama, and i must admit a few parts made me jump.

christian bale blows all the other actors who portrayed batman away, even keaton. bale is batman. he is the first guy to really be good at portraying both sides of batman, meaning the dark knight and bruce wayne. the rest of the cast is definitely top-notch, everyone seemed to fit their part perfectly. liam neeson was the perfect choice for his role as ducard, and like bale as batman, i can't picture anyone else in the role. it also featured strong performances by katie holmes, michael caine, morgan freeman, and cilian murphy as the scarecrow.

this movie bring all the elements of batman together. it has his rough and difficult past, it is the best at explaining how he became batman. it also has a very outrageous plot, as every batman movie should. it is definitely more realistic and intense then the previous batman films, but it still fits in some welcome comic relief. this is by far the best batman film to date, the only problem is....how will they ever top this?

this film, to me, is better than the other two. i haven't directly seen the two, but i had seen parts of the second movie, and it felt very violent and mature. this movie however, is one of the best movies i have ever seen, let alone a batman movie. i saw it several months ago, and i have made it a top favorite movie in my eyes. the story is about bruce wayne, who's father and mother were murdered before his eyes. years later, he wanted to kill his parents' murderer, but someone else did. the next 7 years, bruce wayne, comes upon the league of shadows, where a man named ducard, teaches him a powerful way to combat justice. when he returns, gotham city is now a corrupt city, where police are cowards, gangsters are controlling, and crime is everywhere. soon, he gains help from lucius fox, who gives him his armor, his tumbler (the batmobile), and ultimately all his gadgets. with his support of his butler alfred, and police officer named gordon, bruce wayne becomes his worst fear, into the ultimate superhero batman, and save the now corrupt gotham city. christian bale's performance of batman is probably the best, i have ever seen out of the character himself. he is more realistic than the other interpretations of the character, and is able to pull off such a complex character. michael caine, morgan freeman, katie holmes, gary oldman, and liam neeson, also give awesome roles. you will love this film.

just like burton's batmans, a great ensemble cast led this film to triumph. nothing can be said that wasn't said previously in these comments. it seems to be unanimous, it was a complete and ultimate success. bale is phenomenal, as usual, and freeman, oldman, and neeson give great performances with no one showboating and stealing the spotlight. very descriptive take on the forming of our caped crusader, with all your questions answered and then some.

katie holmes sucks.....sorry. she is the only thing the movie could have done without. but then we would have a movie without breasts, and even though it worked in master and commander,....batman movies need breasts.

great movie, take the kids,...just don't sniff any psychotropic hallucinogens before you go. although, dropping a hit of acid would probably be cool in some parts.

at long last after many years of waiting the fans finally got the batman movie they were waiting for. a batman movie that puts the hero in the spotlight, not his enemies, putting more emphasis on his growth and internal struggles than the heroics. forget about the biff! pow! campiness of the 60's series or the tongue-in-cheek darkness of the tim burton movies, this one gets it right with the origins and more. we see our hero go through many painful stages before finally becoming gotham's protector. as much as i loved tim burton's first take on batman, this one expands upon it even more, and you get great actors to back it up like michael caine, katie holmes, liam neeson, morgan freeman, and gary oldman in their roles and they play it straight not hamming it up here. christian bale is a strong contender for the role of the caped crusader bringing both torment and duty to his role. throughout his character has to make difficult choices between vengeance and justice. the question is can he put everything together and save gotham from a deadly menace? that remains for you to see.

i really loved this movie! as a fan of batman series, i strongly believe this is a perfect movie to start the series! christian bale was at his best! katie homes,morgan freeman, liam neeson and michael caine played the most other favourite characters of mine! nice story line! excellent screenplay, best quality photography, the greatest actors made a flawless, smooth and complete entertaining movie !the bond between bruce wayne and alfred was remarkable ! after a series of unsuccessful projects nolan and david s. goyer began to work on the film in early 2003 and aimed for a darker and more realistic tone, with humanity and realism being the basis of the film. the goal was to get the audience to care for both batman and bruce wayne! i believe they got success.when batman becomes a public hero he loses rachel, this part always hurts me. i always want to see they together as soul mate ! but you know, that never happens for the super hero, remember the superman and his girlfriend ?

though this is very likely forever going to be overshadowed by its epic sequel, the dark knight, batman begins is nevertheless a masterpiece in itself. it is the film which rescued the batman franchise from the campiness and superficiality that had all but destroyed it after joel schumacher's dismal batman and robin and redefined and reinterpreted this iconic character for a new generation, by telling a story which had thus far seldom been coherently and completely told outside of the comics canon: the origin of the batman. while at its core, the story is a simple and tragic tale of a young boy, forever scarred emotionally by the brutal murder of his parents, who is motivated to fight a relentless war against injustice in order to rid a city of the evil which claimed his parents life; there are greater dimensions to the story which christopher nolan has done a superb job of representing on the silver screen in a most compelling manner.

the primary appeal of the story lies in its psychological depth. unlike previous superhero outings which relied primarily on plot and action, nolan has chosen to centre both of these around the psychological development of the protagonist, bruce wayne (played to perfection by christian bale). this movie is as much about bruce's emotional and spiritual journey from a traumatized young orphan, to an aggressive young man disillusioned with the justice system, to the aimless wanderer seeking a means to fight injustice and haunted by his childhood demons and finally to a determined and focused man who has mastered his skills and fears and is prepared to begin his war against injustice; as much as it is about the story of how bruce puts on the cape and cowl. it is under the tutelage of ducard (liam nelson) that bruce wayne learns to conquer his own fear and by doing so manipulate the fears in others. returning to gotham and resuming his public life as a billionaire playboy and socialite, wayne secretly goes about his task of constructing an alternate identity, a symbol that shall forever remain incorruptible and indestructible and shall strike terror into the hearts of the criminal underworld. before long, with assistance and moral support from his faithful butler and confidant alfred pennyworth (michael caine), lucius fox (morgan freeman) an old friend of his father's and a skilled scientist and engineer and sergeant james gordon (gary oldman), one of the few untainted officers of the gotham city police force, bruce unleashes upon the city's corrupt underbelly his alter ego: batman, and succeeds in single-handedly bringing down its biggest crime lord. but soon, gotham's mysterious new vigilante finds himself facing his first great challenge-of saving the city from an enemy who has also learnt to manipulate the fears in others, through more insidious means...

bale's performance as both bruce wayne and batman is par excellence. bale portrays batman as being not merely a man in a suit, but rather a force of nature unto himself, completely distinct from albeit wielded by bruce wayne. michael caine, morgan freeman and gary oldman play their parts well enough and katie holmes does a fair job as bruce's childhood friend and love interest rachel dawes. liam nelson's character is a far more sympathetic villain than previous 'batman baddies' in the films, being, like bruce, a man committed to fighting injustice, albeit in more extreme ways. his actions act as a counterpoint to batman's strict moral code of refraining from lethal action.

with an excellent musical score and eye-popping (albeit moderately realistic) action, batman begins is undoubtedly a fait accompli which can never be underestimated no matter how successful any sequels it has spawned are or will bee...

this is how the modern batman film should have been directed. it is dark, dirty and dangerous. this is the real dark knight. having read the comics and coming to admire the story 'the dark knight returns', the batman is not some campy show in the 70s, nor was it the film directed by tim burton. okay. tim burton approached somewhat the style of the dark knight, but it was still not as dark as it could be.

christian bale is amazing in this, he has the right physique and he has the fighting skills on film (see equilibrium). the supporting actors of michael caine, morgan freeman, gary oldman, liam neeson and cillian murphy are perfect.

gotham city is dark and a scary place, just ripe for a winged crusader to save it from the criminals lurking around.

the story itself is quite 'meaty' and setups the story quite nicely. it also ends by leading the audience to a possible sequel. if the sequel can outdo this excellent first attempt, then i am already salivating.
