title: batman begins (2005) director: chris nolan cast: christian bale, cyllian murphy, katie holmes, morgan freeman, gary oldman, michael caine, liam neeson, rutger hauer review: um, i think we should be thanking joel schumacher in a strange sort of way. now, before you start hurling your baterangs at me for saying that let me explain. as we all know, joel schumachers disastrous run on the batman franchise nearly annihilated any possibilities of future batman films making it to the silver screen. his films where campy, cartoonish and didn't take themselves seriously. dumb story lines, too many characters, bat nipples, reverse photography, neon colors, you name it schumacher did it. and with one final blow know as batman & robin the series ended its ones fruitful and artistic run that tim burton helped shape with his first two films.

now i say thank you mr. schumacher because if he hadn't made his laughably cartoonish versions of batman, then maybe we would have never seen a serious batman film like batman begins. schumachers films pushed the studios to go in a completely different way this time around, the complete opposite of what schumacher did. nolan has finally given us what we had never seen before....a realistic batman movie.

the story centers around batmans origins. where he came from, why he became the vigilante known as batman, and what pushed him there. once we get past the whole "formation of batman" phase of the film, the movie kicks into high gear with batman defending gotham city against ras al ghul, a villain hell bent on destroying gotham to see it "reborn" from its ashes. with the help of another goon known as the scarecrow, he plans on releasing a gas on the city that will make people have nightmares and make the city destroy itself basically.

there's more good points in this film then bad ones so ill start with the good ones. first off, this movie has depth. its story is deep and it takes its time to develop batman as a character. in a great moment in the film we see how he deals with the anger he feels towards the man who murdered his parents something that had been previously ignored in other films. he is not a perfect citizen, he has many flaws and makes many mistakes in this one. after all, this is his first adventure. so bale as batman gave the character a depth that had not been there before.

the rest of the cast is excellent. without a doubt the best cast in any batman flick ever! michael caine as alfred was lovable as bruce waynes father figure. morgan freeman was basically that character in the james bond films that supplies bond with all the cool gadgets. cyllian murphy was creepy as the scarecrow, the guy who runs arkam asylum, where all the super looneys get locked up in. having the scarecrow in the film allowed many cool scenes involving nightmarish images. you wont believe what batman looks like through the effects of the scarecrows nightmare inducing gas! the look of the film was very realistic when compared to burtons gothicky gotham or schumachers campy sets...this gotham feels real and alive. in many instances it felt like the city in blade runner and that was because nolan used that city as an inspiration for this gotham. of course its got its few futuristic touches here and there (like that train that goes around the city) but its nothing too far fetched. the batmobile is awesome! in previous films the batmobile felt like if it could never really pull a curve or anything, this new batmobile is a tank that will swerve any way you want it, turn through the narrowest curve and destroying anything in its way! the car chase involving the batmobile running through the rooftops of gotham was very very memorable.

and as an added bonus...cgi was only used when necessary! hurray, it seems like certain directors are finally releasing that cgi is best when kept to a minimum and used only when there's no other way of filming a scene. so kudos to nolan for that.

but there's always something that doesn't work. what was it? well for me anyways, i didn't like how bale changed his voice when he was batman, he sounded kind of goofy. some people in the audience actually giggled when he talked with his raspy voice. and then there's the thing with the story being very similar to that of the first movie. in the first one joker (jack nicholson) wanted to poison the cities water supply so that everyone who drank it or used it would die with a smile on their face, here its the same thing only ras al ghul wants to poison the water supply so that everyone will have nightmares and kill each other. i don't know, i just found the story to be too much like the first one in that respect.

but those are only minor nit picks, because i really thought the movie achieved what it intended to do, which was give us a fresh and realistic look at the dark knight. while at the same time making us say "cool!" every five minutes.

rating: 5 out of 5

this film, in my opinion, is absolutely amazing. it captures the realism of the batman dc comics and accurately brings the essence of the true character of bruce wayne and batman to the screen. the film is an absolute gem with its intelligence, realism, gritty action and is blessed with a stellar cast of top flight actors from bale, caine, freeman, hauer, neeson, to oldman etc etc. batman was good, batman returns okay, batman forever very poor and batman & robin should never be discussed! batman begins for me, tops them all including the michael keaton & jack nicholson film. and the batmobile/bat-tank (aka the tumbler) is a beast of a machine!

geez, what on earth took them so long? after the campy adam west tv series, the tim burton gothic flicks and joel schumacher's nippled dark knight, the real batman has finally arrived. in batman begins the caped crusader finally becomes the brooding hero he was meant to be. it traces back to his origin, as young bruce wayne, the only son of his billionaire father, who witnesses his parents die to the hands of a mugger, and swears to uphold justice by 'turning fear against those who prey on the fearful'. however his journey towards becoming a vigilante is not as simple as that. unlike the original batman where we're shown pearl beads dancing on the floor that inspired a rich kid to don a suit and fight evil, this bruce wayne had a strenuous journey learning the difference between vengeance and upholding justice. he must also confront his fears and decide on his own ideology.

this is probably the first time i've enjoyed seeing bruce wayne more than batman. it was compelling seeing him develop, as he studies the mind of a criminal and, being human, sometimes questions even himself. fortunately there's his trusty butler alfred on his side, who instead of just serving him steak, assumes the role of a fatherly figure. there's also the up and rising cop in jim gordon, in his early days as a sergeant, posing as batman's only ally at this point in time.

chris nolan does again what he do best; playing with the scene sequence. although this time he only uses that style for the first half of the film, alternating wayne's training scenes with his childhood memories, it did nothing except enhancing the whole story-telling process. the heavyweight cast live up to their names. christian bale does a great job as bruce wayne, excellently portraying his transition from a troubled young man to a profound, philosophical individual. batman, on the other hand, is a cold and menacing figure who's rough voice(that was heavily under criticism) i felt was appropriate, considering that his priority was disguise and also to scare the living daylights out of criminals. for the rest of the cast, michael caine and gary oldman looked like they came right out of the comic books, and then there's also morgan freeman and rutger hauer, making a surprise return to mainstream cinema.

begins sets a new standard for dark comic book films. if spider-man 2 is considered one of the best superhero movies in the 'fun' category, then batman begins would undoubtedly be on the other end of the spectrum, the prime example of how a serious comic book adaptation should be.

i'm glad to say that they've finally got it right. for the first time in film history, the dark knight is portrayed correctly. the batman franchise didn't reboot; it has only just begun.

i was not expecting this movie to wow me as much as it did. everything about it was excellent and i was literally at the edge of my seat my first time seeing batman begins. i'm a huge comic book nerd and a movie fanatic which means that i am not easy to impress. first of all, i was blown away with christian bale's portrayal of a dark batman that i forgot he was acting. bale is a perfect bruce wayne in this movie and it was almost like he became his character.he was witty, intimidating, and hilarious all at the same time. in addition, great performances by liam neeson as ra's al ghul and morgan freeman as fox. i also loved scarecrow, he was scary and sinister - which i was hoping he would be. batman begins does have minor flaws like every movie, but i rate it a ten out of ten simply because it is truly amazing and a great film to rewatch.

christopher nolan's batman begins is the rare origin story that not only revitalizes a character-it redefines an entire genre. released in 2005, it marked the rebirth of batman on screen, abandoning campy aesthetics for a grounded, character-driven narrative that treats its mythos with gravitas and realism. it's a 10/10 film not because it reinvents the wheel, but because it sets the gold standard for how to do it right.

christian bale delivers a layered, intense performance as bruce wayne, charting his transformation from a grief-stricken orphan to a symbol of fear and justice. bale's batman isn't just a costumed hero-he's a man wrestling with anger, identity, and responsibility. we understand his motivations, and more importantly, we believe them.

nolan surrounds bale with an exceptional supporting cast: michael caine as the loyal and heartfelt alfred, morgan freeman as the brilliant lucius fox, gary oldman as the earnest and principled jim gordon, and liam neeson as the morally complex mentor ra's al ghul. every character is treated with care, and every performance adds depth to gotham's world.

the film's tone is its triumph-rooted in realism, but never afraid to be mythic. gotham feels like a living, breathing city plagued by systemic decay, and nolan's decision to focus on fear, corruption, and redemption gives the story weight. the league of shadows, scarecrow's hallucinogenic terror, and the collapsing social structure of gotham create a narrative that's both thrilling and thematically rich.

hans zimmer and james newton howard's score is haunting, pulsing with tension and hope. the action is intimate and raw, emphasizing impact over spectacle. and while the film never loses its blockbuster appeal, it never sacrifices character or theme for the sake of cheap thrills.

batman begins isn't just a great superhero movie-it's a great movie, period. it reintroduced batman as a symbol with psychological complexity and purpose, laying the foundation for a legendary trilogy. it's dark, thoughtful, and emotionally resonant-a cinematic origin story done to near-perfection.

oh my god! finally someone made a movie and showed me that batman could be everything i hoped and dreamed he could. no more of the neon lights and laughable villains of the past. the first batman of the old series focused on batman's dark and mysterious persona to strike fear into the heart of villains. each of it's sequels became more about production and special effects that sacrificed the essence of what batman is supposed to be. this new series has brought back that fear and drama almost effortlessly. however, do not mistake my words...this batman has some rather sexy special effects that will keep you satisfied, but they are done tastefully as not to take away from the darkness of the film. if you don't like christian bale or have some personal vendetta against him then you might have trouble believing in him, but i found his performance to be splendid and truthful. that being said morgan freeman is in this movie...and my good friend if you don't like morgan freeman then i don't believe you know what good acting is. i don't believe i've ever seen a movie with him that i didn't like. some actors and actresses just don't make bad movies and like cuba gooding jr. (although i never have seen rat race or snow dogs...mostly because i don't wanna risk ruining this fact) morgan freeman is one of those. all around excellent movie! and even if you don't enjoy batman as much as i do (what's wrong with you...j/k) you still get to see some kick arse action and look at katie holmes for two plus hours. enjoy!

finally, the dark knight achieves cinematic justice with christopher nolan's "batman begins". after tim burton's strange, art-house approach and joel schumacher's camp-on-steroids versions, moviegoers are given a batman feature made with dignity, intelligence and respect.

the title says it all: the film charts bruce wayne's growth and transformation into the caped crusader. only this time, much more of the material delves into bruce's psychology, which grounds the entire film into a reality more akin with the bourne films than a comic book. everything about batman is explained; his weaponry, his tactics, the people around him, everything. not a moment is wasted in david goyer's script, his best since "dark city".

each character has an important role to play in bruce/ batman's life. unlike the previous four films, bruce wayne is center stage for most, if not all, of the proceedings. christian bale takes full advantage of this, making his performance the now definitive bruce wayne/ batman of the silver screen. nolan surrounds bale with a top-notch supporting cast that's all talent and no ego.

the villains, no longer the focus of what was never their films to begin with, have never been better (at least in a dramatic sense). their relation to fear and how it functions plays into the very theme of not just "batman begins", but batman himself. ken watanabe, liam neeson, cillian murphy and tom wilkinson give it their all. the good guys, played by michael caine, gary oldman, morgan freeman and katie holmes, are fleshed out enough to create a surrogate family for bruce wayne. performances such as theirs help keep the film grounded in reality.

gotham city is no longer towering statues and neon-colored city blocks, but an actual american city sprawling in its own decadence. even the gadgetry and the batmobile seem plausible, if not insanely expensive. in closing, nolan has created a film worthy of a hero such as batman. no longer content with just "comic-book movies", the dark knight now has a full-fledged movie to call his own. in fact, as far as adventures go, this is the most dramatically competent i've seen (and that includes indiana jones -- honestly, how much do you really know about his character?).

i am amazed by how much time the script took to develop everything, and it tells an honest-to-goodness story, instead of filling in the blanks and insert-action- sequence-here. bravo to all involved; it's about time a live-action film gave as much respect to batman as the animated series did. here's hoping that batman continues. (this is not a spoiler, but i would like to put in my vote for mark hamill in a certain role for the next film. that is all.)

for all you batman fanatics who were severely let down at the post tim burton batman movies, you certainly will not be with this one. batman is back and is as darker as ever in his bid to save gotham city from total destruction.the film carries a star studded cast including christian bale, morgan freeman & micheal caine. but it is christian bale who stands out the most, bringing that much needed life back to the cape crusader that we have missed for so long. much credit must go to christopher nolan for picking out the right cast and creating an inevitable new batman era.

no doubting on this one, batman is truly back and better than ever. a real winner! 9/10

wow! what a great movie but it was very long. i have to say this was the best movie i saw this year in the theaters besides star wars iii! the music! the action! the loudness! i can't say i like loudness that much but it seemed to fit in this movie. bruce wayne/batman (christian bale) has to face his fears and what he fears most is bats. his parents own wayne enterprises (you'll find out what happens to them early in this movie). this movie finally tells the whole story of the "batman" series. first the movie actually starts out when he's an adult in a chinese prison (you'll find out how he got there). this movie has quite a few flashbacks though when he was a boy and a young adult and goes back to the present with his trainer (liam neeson) for martial arts and facing all of his fears. finally, after maybe an hour, he starts doing some hero work with the help of arthur (michael caine)- bruce's butler. bruce gets all the batman equipment from applied sciences dept head lucius (played by morgan freeman) in the basement of the wayne building. the city where the movie takes place is, of course, "gotham" but it was really filmed in the city of downtown chicago. there was also a villain in this movie (as there always is) that was quite a frail person but quite an effective and disgusting villain. although he was quite wimpy, his mask gave him power. in this movie bruce's trainer surprisingly turns against him (and you'll find out what his evil plan was in this movie) this was a long movie and there are many other things to talk about in this review, but i'd like to give every person that is reading this review to have some rest for your eyes! i definitely recommend this movie to everyone! movie directed by christopher nolan. oh, by the way, you better go to the bathroom before you see this movie. i'm glad i did.
