it is a good movie. christopher nolan does a good job bringing batman back to the dark atmosphere it belongs. christian bale does a good job as bruce wayne/batman, with notable actors like gary oldman, liam neeson, and morgan freeman doing good as well. the story is an interesting take on batman's origin, and the special effects are good. this is a good batman movie i would recommend to any fan of batman or anyone into superheroes in general.

spiderman was good, spiderman 2 was great, but in my opinion, this is without doubt the best comic book movie i've ever seen. and i know most people won't agree, but i personally enjoyed this a little more than sin city although that was ace too.

i was a bit sceptical too, cos i didn't really like memento (directed by nolan) although its premise was very good. and bale sometimes seems a bit...i don't know...just the way he does that macho voice all the time in every part.

but it all worked in this movie! and how!! the story was gripping, the action was dark and intense and the effects were brilliant. i really loved the way the whole concept of batman was developed from his symbolism as wayne's fear to the way his costume came together (the cape and the suit etc.) bale was ace as bruce wayne and every better as batman, but i think this is because he really treated him as a disturbed character. i think i heard bale say in an interview "batman is not bruce wayne in a costume. he's bruce wayne as a demon." the supporting cast were brilliant (well, actually i didn't like holmes buy hey!) - michael caine, gary oldman and morgan freedman are legends! hopefully it's the first of a few and maybe, just maybe, one day the nightmares of batman and robin will just be a ghost story you tell grand children!! excellent movie - 10/10

growing up watching the batman series and movies i have alway held batman above all other super heroes.however, even though i loved all the batman movies, i never thought any did batman justice since micheal keaton. but now my hopes were full filled. the story plays out at a fast pace yet it explains it self quit well. the plot has its twists and turns but i found that my mind was always one step ahead. unlike the recent batman movies, batman begins is set in a more realistic gotham city and a more reality based society. the comic book look is still there with its long shots of the city but it does not over do it. the characters are more believable also, christian bale does an excellent job, his style suits the billionaire who is not a money hungry rat, but a billionaire who wants to do more for the people. i could never understand bruce wayen's mind extensively until now. micheal caine as alfred was an excellent choice and i think he was exceptional, but i did miss the original alfred. morgan freeman was his usual best and a lovable character. liam neeson was truly mind warping, he defines what an actor should be, i think hollywood should recognize him more. katie holmes was also good but her character and place in the story kept reminding me of mary jane from spiderman. but all the leading women in superhero movies seem to go along these lines also. i recommend any one who wants to have a rush and leave the movie learning more about how humanity is should go and watch batman begins. 10/10!

as to start the batman franchise back up again, christopher nolan delivers the focus of both bruce wayne and batman accurately in this first installment to the absolutely outstanding the dark knight trilogy. batman begins is a 2005 action superhero film directed by christopher nolan. christopher nolan has been known to be one of the most influential directors in the film industry today. even alongside the dark knight trilogy, he directs the prestige, inception, interstellar, and dunkirk. however, nolan creates a more eccentric look on batman with the dark knight trilogy. the first installment involves around bruce wayne's life before batman and as the start of becoming the hero. after his parents were killed in front of him at a young age, he grows up wanting revenge. after setting and leaving the league of shadows, he goes to become batman. he decides to strike fear in the hearts of criminals and bring them to justice. more characters involved include his allies alfred (michael caine), rachel dawes (katie holmes), sergeant jim gordon (gary oldman), and lucius fox (morgan freeman). the villains include henri ducard (liam neeson), the scarecrow (cillian murphy), and carmine falcone (tom wilkinson).

not only does the bat-flick show batman in action, but it also shows us how and why bruce wayne became what he is. what's cool about it is that the dark knight trilogy starts off with the origins of bruce wayne/batman and then it will involve into a much bigger story. i really enjoyed the film! plus, i am a batman fan and a dc comics fan as well! any fan of batman or any superhero in general should find this film fascinating! i loved christopher nolan's direction and his idea to make the batman story bigger than what it is. he also shapes the movie to make it focus on more than batman and also his allies. the acting was also great and i've also decided that christian bale is my favorite batman so far! the cinematography was moving, the musical score is well-known to many viewers (also as it continues on with the rest of the trilogy), and the accuracy for its depiction of batman was also fantastic! i give credit to nolan for his direction, the amazing acting (including the portrayal of batman), the moving cinematography, and for the outstanding well-known musical score provided by hans zimmer and james newton howard. this is a great batman film and a great start to the dark knight trilogy!

batman has always been a very complex superhero. he doesn't have powers, but he is considered as one of the most iconic comic book characters of all time! i give batman begins a 10/10 for its outstanding depiction of batman's story, the amazing direction by nolan, the awesome acting, the moving cinematography, and for the well-known musical score! the dark knight trilogy has started off fantastic with batman begins!

it was nominated for 1 academy award for best cinematography (wally pfister).

when batman first hit the silver screen, in his own movie named after himself, he was treated as a secondary character because jack nicholson cost ed the producers a lot of money for screen time. in his second outing, he was placed in a soulless nightmare and didn't seem very heroic. then his last two movies were so corny and out of whack that we thought we, the viewers, would forever shudder when we hear the name batman.

friends, those days are now history.

batman begins ****/**** it's batman's origin story. not only does it follow its original material from the comics (which is always the best way to go with these type of movies), it is consistently dazzling with its action, its drama and its incredible cast.

this has got to be one of the greatest ensembles of actors ever to be involved in a film. christian bale becomes a superstar, micheal caine portrays his loyal butler with true grace and soft power, gary oldman nails the character of jim gordon both in vision and in performance, cillian murphy also grabs our attention, liam neeson portrays the mentor (again) with perfection, morgan freeman... what can you say that has not been said already?...... it's just amazing.

the action here, for what it is in its heart and soul, is easily 10x better than cgi festivals like the new star wars movies. most of it is all real, using miniatures and sometimes full scale batmobile action, stunt men flying etc. etc. it's the kind of action that has you feeling emotions you've never felt for a long... long time.

the characters are all three dimensional. everyone has motives, backgrounds, and reasons to do what they do. batman is rightfully the best developed character. ultimately you have to ask yourself "how in the hell can a man become inspired to fight criminals while dressed as a bat?". as crazy as it sounds, the movie provides very good answers.

now it is long, but worth every milli-second. we first get to know bruce wayne through multiple flashbacks. then we move on to his training and some of his early days of crime fighting. we don't see the suit for a good chunk of the film. but rest assured, the majority of the film does have batman in it.

we get to know everything about him. the explanations of his wonderful toys are freakin' awesome! some of his items, including his cape, are based on actual technology. personally when i saw publicity shots of the new batmobile i thought it was the most atrocious piece of crap ever to grace a batman film, and i imagine some of you probably;y feel the same way now. but let me tell you, that car is amazing. it's ugly because it's designed to plow through everything like a tank on speed-steroids. you have to see it in action to truly appreciate it.

fantastic movie. basically anyone who's been missing that spine tingling feeling you get from perfect action movies should go out and rent this now.

this is a great film whether you're a batfan or not - i personally disliked the recent batman films and just wish i could see some more of that shark-repellent batspray. it's probably just not meant to be.

there are some brilliant performances by morgan freeman, liam neeson and michael caine, though i'm glad the former two had fairly minor roles since it could have detracted from the story.

the story was very compelling and while i believe there were some continuity issues with the other films, this stands out brilliantly from the others so it doesn't concern me.

there are moments where the film is dark and scary - i'm sure there are guidelines for parents about whether this movie would be suitable for their children, just be sure to read them if you have children who are prone to being frightened. needless to say there are bats. the special effects were very good (thankfully there wasn't much cgi in the film) but didn't distract the eyes.

compared to other films i've seen recently it's in a league of it's own - if you're looking for an action film this summer it just has to be batman begins.

nolan couldn't have been a better choice to take the director's seat, and while bale has a strong resemblance to west, their batmans are completely different. after eight years of silence, the batman reemerges with a most appropriate reboot which explains the whole history of how bruce wayne became batman. nolan makes both burton and schumacher look like ed wood — most impressive of all is that, while technology has improved tremendously since 1997's flop "batman & robin", "begins" chooses to take little advantage of it. a-list actors are casted as supporting characters, with michael cane as alfred, and a calm gary oldman (that's a first!) as gordon; among others like liam neeson, katie holmes and morgan freeman. tom wilkinson, rutger hauer, ken watanabe and colin mcfarlane are also so wonderful in their minor roles. cillian murphy modestly appears as the scarecrow, which one can say is a bit underused as a well-known villain, but it actually makes it all the more realistic. perhaps the older series should have considered using major stars as supporting characters, not villains. this film proves that superheroism isn't impossible — you just have to be a billionaire. nolan's uncle, john nolan, plays fredericks.

**** (out of four)

the batman movie that stood out the most. yes, it is better both the dark knight and the dark knight rises. yet unfortunately, it is the arguably the most underrated one.

so where do i start here? oh yes, the beautiful scenery that caught my attention first. when you see bruce wayne traveling to ra's al ghul's palace, you are exposed to incredibly eye-pleasing landscape. you see even more during the sword fight between wayne and ducard (ra's as you will find out in the end). beautiful sky-blue mountains everywhere. how can you not commend this movie for having this? so ra's trains bruce wayne. and let me tell you, his lines are magnificent and poetic. all his talk about theatricality and deception makes you even more excited for bruce wayne to finally don the cowl. in my opinion, his performance was far superior than the not-so-amazing health ledger's joker. liam neeson did an excellent job as a ninja master and his lines make his fights with bruce seem like a masterpiece. why did we not get this sort of action in the sequels?

after returning to gotham, bruce is no longer the angry rich kid. now he is a different person. however, before he completely goes 'all-out', he must run a test, and i'm referring to his very entertaining visit to gordon in his ski mask. with gotham you can tell that it's not a place that you would want to live in. it is pretty much the ultimate dystopia for law. corruption, drug trafficking and bribing is virtually everywhere. nolan did a fantastic job portraying more hell-like than the gotham in tdk or tdkr.

now for christian bale's batman. before i watched this movie, i expected to see very little of batman or see him at the end of the film. but i got more than i expected and we received batman who occupied the 2nd hour of the movie. batman here is a beast. "the dark knight", "the caped crusader", "the world's greatest detective" apply perfectly to this batman. this is not the wimp with throat cancer we got from the sequels. bruce wayne was trained to be a ninja, and it is reflected how much he learned in his batman activities. he has got everything you want from a batman: stealth methods, mind games, fluent martial arts skills, tons of gadgets, intimidating suit, and a voice that you can understand. don't believe me? watch this movie again. this batman tackled a whole group of ninjas (who should be as, if not more skilled as him). yet in tdk he couldn't beat joker, a clown who doesn't know how to fight, and a few of thugs? the batman got a little rusty, hadn't he? also, this batman does not shout/talk as much as tdk's bats. during the tumbler chase scene, he really did not speak much, except on occasions to calm rachel down. to add more proof, re-watch the scene where he gets poisoned by the scarecrow's fear gas. when he breathes in, he starts getting hallucinations, yet he doesn't say a word. this is the true "silent guardian" that gordon was talking about in tdk. this makes me feel that batman himself is not the primary character here, bruce wayne is. however, when bale dons the cape, he steals every scene he's in, something i did not receive in tdk (aside from the lack of stealth techniques).

alfred and lucius fox's fantastic in this film. both of their lines are very clever and very humorous at times. if you had a butler like alfred in real life, he will reassure you that things will work out. "why do we fall, master wayne?"

however, this movie is not one without flaws. katie holmes, as much as i think she better than her replacement in the sequel, sounds extremely sarcastic in a lot of her scenes, e.g. when she first meets batman or when she meets scarecrow on a horse. also, some people complain that the fight scenes in bb are terrible due to their 'shaky' feel. i must agree, it can be frustrating sometimes to work out who's hitting who. however, it works effectively with batman as it makes him look more like a living shadow. overall, this movie is my 2nd most favorite film i've seen in my life. batman's performance, ra's al ghul, the amazing cast and the fantastic soundtrack more than convince me that this is superior than the rest of the trilogy. it's entertaining, clever, soul-grasping and most of all, inspiring whereas the dark knight is mentally exhausting. if you love batman and see him be a total badass monster, go watch this movie. if you despise batman with all your heart and want to see him suffer, please go back to watching your tdk and keep telling yourself how "amazing" the health ledger's joker is. or you can watch the dark knight rises to see bats' ass handed to him by bane.

this is without a doubt (in my humble opinion) the best take on a comic book hero ever put on film. an incredible cast, a director with a fresh take on the mythology of the dark knight, and a strong and almost-realistic storyline makes this one a definite 10 out of 10.

christian bale owns as bruce wayne/batman. i had my doubts about him taking on this role, but they were quickly laid to rest when he first dons the batsuit. morgan freeman and michael caine are excellent in their supporting roles, and although screen time is limited for both of them, the both have time to shine. gary oldman, well, this is one of his most subdued roles and yet he still does his thing, memorably taking the character of gordon from secondary character to a pivotal figure in the storyline. and, oh my god, cillian murphy....steals the show. who would've guessed that the guy from 28 days later could play such a menacing character? fantastic performance, and i hope we see more of the scarecrow in future films.

the direction is tight, giving the movie a darker feel than even burton's version of the tale. kudos to nolan for delivering every fanboy's wet dream. i hope warner brothers signed him to a sequel contract, as his directorial style meshes beautifully with batman lore.

overall, i can't find anything that i did not like about this movie. it was the best time i've had at the theatre so far this year. 10 out of 10.

so before heading off to see this movie, i was a little hesitant. i have been a batman movie fan my whole life. being only 17, the first two were a little violent for me, but i fell in love with the whole idea of the one man vigilante story. i grew up with batman. i went through my awkward phases, and so did the storyline. there was a noticeable difference with the shift from tim to joel, and michael to val. there wasn't any continuity other than the key player of batman. gotham changed instantaneously, and it became a more airy feature and an audience pleaser, but that was all. i thoroughly enjoyed the last two in the batman series, but i could never get over the batman i had first viewed after borrowing one of my big sister's videotapes when i was 5. the villains kept getting funnier and funnier, and the scenes became less meaningful and more action packed, heart racing, and pointless. but then i ventured in to see batman begins.

i left that theater happier than ever. this movie was everything and more. it was a return to the darker, more mysterious batman i first fell in love with. christian bale is the perfect man for this role, he has all the appeal. i was hesitant at the idea of a star studded cast, because some of these movies receive more hype than they are worth. morgan freeman, michael caine, tom wilkinson, and liam neeson are all oscar contenders and some winners. they gave well rounded performances and proved that as actors they can truly dive into their roles and not steal the show. katie holmes was good as rachael dawes, but her role wasn't as pivotal as i had hoped, but despite that, she managed to hold her own and deliver a good performance. i was so surprised by this movie. the comedy was light, but present none the less.

this batman was unpredictable, and the unknown villain always makes for more edge of your seat viewing, and this movie did not let me down on that factor. i never took my eyes from the screen. the cinematography was so splendid and the story was so perfect. there wasn't so much focus on batman, but it was on bruce wayne and how he transformed into batman. that was the winner. this plot was so rich and perfect to the return to roots theme every prequel should take. batman is supposed to be dark, mysterious, and more thought provoking than the, "saving the world and gotham from certain destruction theme as two villains team up and giggle and joke the entire time" themes that were so prevalent in the last 3 batmans. this movie was the best of the bunch, and a return to the original batman from 1989.

batman begins is a great movie, and the best of the pack. it has everything the previous movie had, but delivers them in a more concise and pleasing way without focusing too much on one aspect such as action, mystery, or comedy. it is all of these and more, and i guarantee everyone will if not love, at least enjoy this movie.

nolan's batman is by far more superior than tim burton's mediocre stylized batman (that seems to lack in character development) - in so many ways possible. unlike burton's vision of establishing batman as a second rate character in his own films which i disliked immensely, nolan creates layers upon layers of dimension for the batman character as well as the bruce wayne individual that acts as the mask for who he really is. the 'realistic' approach makes the film stand out upon others, with the gritty realism pouring everywhere throughout the film that makes it sometimes take itself a little too seriously. let's face it, christian bale is better than kilmer, clooney and possibly keaton as playing millionaire bruce wayne - a man with a haunted and distort soul. not only does he embody everything i see in batman and bruce, he's an amazing actor and adds a great blend of dark, brooding, and richness to the portrayal of a quite sane young man. he has the best of scenes (especially the one's involving freeman), and he's fairly buff in the role, something the ladies will undoubtedly like. the rest of the cast is top-notch, mostly oscar winners or nominees or just plain outstanding actors (though holmes is neither) in some way or another. caine is butler alfred, freeman is inventor lucius fox in wayne industries, oldman is good cop jim gordon, neeson is henri ducard (well, this turns out to be false) - mentor and father figure to bruce, watanabe is actually the decoy as neeson turns out to be terrorist villain ra's al ghul, and holmes gets to play the damsel in distress/love interest/childhood friend as d.a. rachel dawes; her character isn't in the comic and was only invented for the film, just to let you know. she's not at her best to be honest - with her slightly insipid lines and the fact that she looks awfully young compared to bale (and her character is older if you can believe that). there's also two performances that took me by complete surprise. first, cillian murphy is dr. jonathan crane also known as the scarecrow, who happens to work in the infamous arkham asylum. it's nice to say, his creepy presence on screen gets creepier by his influence of his 'fear gas' - hallucinations from your wildest dreams or nightmares. then there's tom wilkinson as crime boss falcone who has a lot of people doing his dirty work in gotham. the accent he puts on is somewhat mafia-like and i like it. now enough with the cast, let's talk about the fight scenes that are disappointing to some degree. nolan isn't really good at the fight sequences delivered in this film, but he still has time for major improvement (i'm talking about the sequels - if he's willing to make them). there are extremely choppy, yet not what you'd expect. the editing is all wrong, but i'm willing to look past it (you should too). overall, the plot is convincing as a batman flick and nolan deserves most of the credit as do the people that have worked their butts off creating a masterpiece with depth. batman has been truly reborn, once again.

i have to say it. this batman movie is by far my favorite. after the atrocity known as batman and robin (now let us never speak of that again), i was hoping- really hoping- for a good batman flick. man, this did not disappoint. i think what really makes this movie shine is it's cast. christian bale is bruce wayne. he is dead on as the dark knight.

i cannot understand how michael caine was not cast as alfred for the other 4 movies. if he was busy with something else, fine, if not what was the excuse? morgan freeman is excellent as lucius, same goes for tom wilkinson as falcone. cillian murphy really broke out last summer, and this movie helped significantly. he was great as the creepy scarecrow. watanabe was great as ra's al ghul. but my favorite performance was liam neeson as ducard. he is the main reason i love this movie so much. i mean seriously, is there a movie where this guy sucks? he is awesome in very movie i've seen him in. i have to agree with roger ebert. this really is one of the best movies of 2005.

gripping from start to finish. christian bale is the perfect choice for batman (and bruce wayne). the action is great, the dialogue is great, big players like michael caine and morgan freeman are used wisely and effectively. a must see film and probably one of the best i have ever seen - and i have seen a lot of films! it's emotional charge grabs at your chest like a rampaging gorilla and there is never a second when you are not entertained or swept along with the story as it unfolds. from the tender moments to the high octane action this film hits the spot at all levels and is relentless entertainment form start to finish. wow!

i was surprised that it was this good, i just got back from the movies and damn i expected something good but this is one of the best, if not the best superhero movie i've seen. people always tend to think of superhero movies as not being able to achieve the same blockbuster status as other movies, but all that changed with spiderman which set the bar higher for other superhero movies and i can say that nolan has clearly found the best way to show the birth of batman. i mean come on, this batman is nothing like any other batman we've seen. its not bale wearing a costume, its batman, nolan showed us how different bruce wayne and batman are. the split personally shown in a very in your face way. and bale portrayed that very well, change of voice as batman, change of walking pace and style and the way he shouted to that corrupt cop: "swear to me" when the guy said "i swear to god" that was powerful, its the way bob kane wrote batman at the beginning. that is, not as bruce wayne in a costume but as a separate character from bruce wayne. the only thing in common is the compassion that he has for people and the hatred for injustice and crime.

the scarecrow was impressive even with just the mask and not the whole scarecrow costume that we've seen in the comics. and luscious fox fits well in the story, as usually(in other movies) its alfred who designs/works on the gadgets but this makes more sense. alfred cant do everything. michael caine is believable as alfred pennyworth, a father figure and a friend for bruce.

henry ducard(liam neeson) impressed me in the first scene itself when he beats up bruce wayne, he's bad. the training looked cool on screen, with the ninja outfits and armour. in the previous movies we haven't been told how batman has all these skills(in fact they don't show that much fighting skills anyway) but this one shows how, by training bruce wayne becomes more than a man.

he doesn't have any superpowers thats what i like about batman, he doesn't need the powers. the way that he scares the enemies was well thought, in the first scene where we actually see batman in action, he gives these guys the creeps. and thats what batman is all about.

gotham city looks great, the landscapes, buildings, the train and especially the wayne building. now the batmobile not only looks good, its bulky, bumpy but still sleek looking and its massive, the scenes where the cops are chasing it are awesome, even if its just a vehicle you can get a feel for how it relates to batman's personality.

why excellent? i've been a superhero buff all my life and i a 42 year-old woman. this movie does the batman series a huge tribute. it brings a tear to my eye that the first series didn't due batman the justice that this movie does. i have been a christian bale fan ever since i saw "newies". he plays an excellent bruce wayne/batman. i was a little nervous for such great actor to play such a part. when it's not done well, an actor can get type casted or worse. now i actually look forward to seeing him playing batman again. like tobey mcquire when a superhero movie is done right, you don't have no fear of losing your career. top notch stars like liam neeson, michael caine, morgan freeman, and gary oldman round out this movie. such great talent for such an excellent movie. i hope the director christopher nolan stays on board as well through the series. at this time, i have no idea what they have in the works, but as long as the team stays on i hope to see many more. (rule of thumb - never let the bad guys out shine the good guy!) this should be as successful a film as the spiderman series. so go spend the big bucks to make it happen.

batman begins (2005) **** christian bale, liam neeson, katie holmes, michael caine, cillian murphy, gary oldman, morgan freeman, tom wilkinson, rutger hauer, ken watanabe, mark boone junior, linus roache. excellent prequel 'origin' of the dark knight that adds fresh blood to a weakened franchise thanks largely to the unlikely pow! bam! combo of indie filmmaker christopher nolan and bale (with an intense, brooding yet vulnerable turn and a fine jaw for the infamous cowl to boot!) as billionaire heir bruce wayne hellbent for vengeance for the murder of his parents which leads him on a journey of redemption from the brutal asian prison camp after taking a nowhere-to-go downward spiral attempt at crime where he encounters the mysterious henri ducard (a suitable neeson) and the ninja-training from guru of vigilantism ra's al ghul (an imposing watanabe) laying the foundation to his inner turmoil exploited into an iconic hero to thwart the evil in gotham. watching all the jigsaw puzzle pieces interlock from the beginnings of wayne's brainy conceit of the batsuit to the humvian batmobile are giddy joys for the inner fanboy of every squandered youth. a sound cast of international bravado (caine as alfred, the butler, wayne's manservant/father figure, adds a dash of subtle observations and common sense; freeman as wayne enterprises' best kept secret displaying the varying degrees of know-how and bat-phenalia; oldman as a young (soon-to-be commissioner) jim gordon  apparently the only honest cop on the force has a few nice subtle moments of awe and cunning; silky murphy as dr. jonathan crane aka the scarecrow; wilkinson as ganglord carmine falcone affecting a new yorkese dialect tuff guy demeanor; hauer as a reptilian board chairman of wayne's empire with oily ease); sterling production design by nathan crowley envisioning gotham city as "new york on steroids", the dank cinematography by wally pfister, and reimagining of the stealthy costumed caped crusader by designer lindy hemming combine for a robust display of ingenuity. the wraithlike incarnation of the man into batsuit avenger is a thing of gothic beauty (echoing the tim burton and frank miller conceit) expertly designed by screenwriter david s. goyer (the "blade" trilogy to name just three successful comic book to screen adaptations) with nolan flexes the mind, muscle and sardonic humor quintessential to a truly american original hero. arguably the best of the batman films and highly entertaining; what more can you ask for when you see a flying batman soar over the glassy plains of gotham! ** see this on the imax and all i can say is : wow! five words: a 90 foot katie holmes; how can you go wrong!!

what will you want to see when you go for a batman movie which tells you of how bruce wayne becomes the dark knight of gotham? an introduction to his childhood, his deepest fears which become the stimulus for what grows within him, his aimless wanderings around the world, his methodical training, his realization to where he should put himself in this world despite what his training demands him of, his preparations for his new life, the slow and very slow ways of introducing his secret self, teasing glimpses of his style and action, and a prodigious ending where all of what he is, is displayed full, as the colossal batman.

this movie has it all.

christian bale is one of my favorite actors since equilibrium (2002). he has given a very responsible and matured performance. i liked michael keaton. i liked val kilmer. and bale? from his post-adolescent age, through the wanderer period and till the end as a superhero, he has shown significant differences in every stage of his acting. he is born for this role.

bale has given a performance through which the subtleties of his character of a batman growing from scratches are very carefully depicted. for an instance, even after wearing the hood, his manners and ways of delivering speech are full of emotions. he shouts, swears, worries. but as his personality builds on and on, he becomes more silent, more methodic, more dark and more a batman.

liam neeson is as usual the screen stunner. he is as cool as he was as qui gon jinn (star wars - episode i) and as godfrey (kingdom of heaven). i loved watching him train bale exhibiting his arrogant confidence. morgan freeman comes only in a few scenes but makes his mark. his witty talks and the proud-but-humble way he displays his inventions to bale are some on the lighter side of the movie. hats off to sir michael caine as alfred. no one else would suite better, particularly when he has to say - "never".

every character and every scene has been chosen properly. the deliberate minor imperfections in clothing, weaponry and action scenes vividly reminds us that this is a prequel portraying a beginner and not an advanced superhero. the gripping score from hans zimmer and james newton howard constitutes the power drive for those amazing 141 on-screen minutes. ultimately, the movie has justified its title.

i have never seen batman so dark and so powerful. this movie is a dream come true for a die-hard fan like me. extending his black wings the dark knight vanishes in flight before we could even realize it. nolan has teased us to the core but has made sure to leave those awing flashes behind our eyes which tells us of... what batman means!

after seeing batman begins on friday night, i was just totally gob smacked, sitting there as the credits rolled, i've seen a lot of films, and being an actor myself, i find myself being very critical, analysing and over-analysing films from the acting to production, and so forth; but as i sat there after the film finished, it dawned on me that i had seen for than just a batman film, more than just the batman film, what i had seen in my eyes was truly a cinematic masterpiece, that realised and achieved everything the script by the talented mr goyer, and indeed the comics of the last 66 years and set out to tell; mr nolan and company, have put together one of the finest most breathtaking films i have seen in a long, long, long, long time. the epic quality of this film, gives this the feel that this is very much a real film and not your typical comic book hero film. there is very much a wealth of emotion within in this film, predominantly fear, but it draws you in to care about the characters, especially christian bale's bruce wayne, you can at times feel yourself in his shoes. one of the catalyst moments in this film, the murder or thomas and martha wayne, is handled and executed (no pun intended) very well, the camera angles draw you in from both sides of the situation; it isn't drawn out too long before there demise, creating a quick sense of panic and fear, ending quickly with the murder, bang thomas is shot , within a second or two, martha is shot, as someone viewing this you're are not given time to react the first shot before hearing the second, which places you in the young bruce wayne's shoes; the whole scene is just in your face up close and personal, and through out the film scenes are done in this way, no matter how far away from the screen you way be, this technique draws you in and involves you in every critical moment. the very essence of this film and the examples in cinema, and graphic novelisation it draws from (last time i use the word draws, promise) blade runner for example, and the very comics its based on, this film surpasses them all for it's visual quality, indeed the comics could learn a lot from this film. the spiderman films may have raised the bench mark for these sort of films, but this film has made the bench unreachable, and could easily hold its own up against the the top 50 classic films of all time; it is a real pleasure to see this film in 64th place of the top 250 films on this website. full praise is deserved to the actors in this film as well, bale is bruce wayne/batman, its hard to imagine anyone else in the role, bale owns it. the same goes for michael caine, morgan freeman, and gary oldman, the roles they play, were made for them; the chemistry between these actors works works extremely well and adds to the attention to detail this film maintains through out. but i'm not going to single out the rest of the cast, as all were exceptional, no matter how big or small their part in this film. the villains of this film, all carried a certain panache, all equally chilling in their individual ways, nothing over the top, just purely sinister and insidious. one thing that annoyed me about reviews of this film is the katie holmes bashing and how she lets the film down, can i say to those of you out there who feel this and you know who you are, you are talking rubbish, katie does a splendid job playing the friend and the d.a. that gets caught in the whirlwind events that take gotham city, indeed even her performance plays a vital part in the chemistry that links the characters, and makes you care for them. my hats off to the production staff and special effects team, every location of the batman myth has been faithfully and realistically recreated, the batsuit, the utility belt and kit, especially the bat mobile, all make realistic sense, considering batman's mission to reclaim gotham and considering how dangerous that will be. the tumbler is an amazing piece of machinery, and shouldn't be changed at all. i love the way every aspect of batman's suit and gadgets are explained, with out boring us, and with out sounding far fetched, remember the bat mobile really can do most of those stunts. my only recommendation is to go and see this film, see it as many times as you can on the big screen, whether it will earn the credit or respect it so rightfully deserves, this film has earned its right in cinematic history. i have one piece of advice, forget starwars, and war of the worlds, these heavily special effects laden films think that cgi is the answer and is the selling point, and ignore good story telling, and lose passionate character acting, both films represent a misguide tired tradition in hollywood, batman begins finally proves that cgi should only be used to enhance a film and not carry it. don't be made to think these films are better than batman begins, they are very different in their own right, but can't hold a candle to good old fashioned story telling, god bless you mr nolan, for sticking to your guns, and producing a film the way it should be done, as for you mr lucas and mr spielberg....shame on you, the public is wising up, batman begins has sent the bench mark sky high, just try topping that

i tend to dislike comic book movies, but "batman begins" is much more than that. it's action packed, but realistic, with characters you feel emotion for. it's dark, mysterious, and moody. the hype, cartoon junk of the last two batman movies is gone, and in it's place is a movie which is scary, dark, action packed, and fun. a perfect cast combined with a perfect story line combined with perfect direction and production equals the best comic book movie i have ever seen. christian bale plays both the roles of bruce wayne and the dark knight with perfection. he doesn't go without a hinge, and you actually can develop feelings and emotion for bruce wayne, the first time i have ever felt that in a batman movie. michael caine, morgan freeman, katie holmes, liam nisson and the others all do their roles very well also. go see it today and see what batman truly should be like.

i loved this movie. "batman begins" has done something other movies have failed to do in my opinion, it lived up to it's expectations.!!!!!!

words can't describe how the good the movie was except it was excellent. i knew this movie was going to be good when i saw the cast list: morgan freeman, liam neeson, gary oldman, the question mark seemed to be christian bale could he pull of the biggest role of his career? the answer to that movie fans is yes!!!

bale is somewhat underrated, he's appeared in some good movies and some stinkers but this movie interviews he did for "batman begins" on access hollywood, i knew he could do he was sincere and serious about making a good impression and he did on them some. he underwent some serious training to get into the role and it definitely shows on screen.bale did an excellent job!!!

liam neeson who i praised on "kingdom of heaven" likewise comes through with another memorable but short roles as ducard, the man who takes bruce wayne under his wing and makes him a fighting machine.

with ducard's help, bruce wayne (bale) is able to come into grips about the murders of his parents, something that was eating away at him and destroying him.through ducard and alfred's (michael caine) guidance, we see the origins of the batman starting to come through until his metamorphis in gotham city is complete.

plotwise the movie title says it "batman begins" we see the origins of batman/bruce wayne in detail from childhood to adult as he grows from a child coping with the death of his parents to a man possessed by his own destiny to rid the world evil and battle the demons inside him.

then comes the real challenge for wayne as he faces the corruption and violence that is overtaking the city. sure we've seen this in the other batman movies but what sets this one apart from the other ones, is the acting, the character development, in bruce wayne's growth as a man as he struggles within his demons, the psychological battles he plays with himself.

enter katie holmes who plays rachel dawes , waynes love interest and batman's love interest, a good girl being caught in some bad company. you know wayne loves her but he is still dealing with issues, becoming the batman then provides an avenue for bruce to get closer to rachel while protecting her at the same time.

cilliam murphy as dr. jonathan crane/the scarecrow, is also excellent, he actually seems like an insignificant foe but once he's alter ego shows on the scree, it's a different story. ken watanabe as the other important figure ra's al ghul who aids wayne's training is good and last but not ;least morgan freeman as luscious fox who basically gives the first look at the creation that is the batmobile is excellent.

director christopher nolan not only deserves a pat on the back for his excellent adaptation of the comic book character but a hug from every comic book fan whose been wanting a respectable version of the "dark knight" for quite some time.

this movie had heart, it was gritty, it was dramatic, and batman wasn't a stupid a cartoon cutout like george clooney's stupid portrayal but he was a man, a real man with real problems and issues, and above you liked it, you really him we sympathized with bale's portrayal as wayne, and we cheer as he goes through his whole training until he becomes the dark knight and imprints his legacy as the defender of justice and truth.

i can't say anymore about this movie except it's perhaps the best if not the best batman movie ever made, at the same level if not surpassing the original by tim burton.

go see it now and enjoy!!!

last year around may the batman begins hype started up. i of course always being a fan of batman was excited to get the chance to see batman done right. the cast was perfect, the director was perfect, but i always wondered if the story would be accurate and perfect? last night my questions were answered when i was privileged to see a free screening of batman begins. anyone who had any doubts about this movie can now be at ease because this movie has now set a new standard of what a good superhero movie truly means. we have seen spider-man and have seen daredevil but what both of those have in common is there fake and not believable. don't get me wrong i'm not saying a guy who dresses up like a bat and fights crime is real but in batman begins as you watch you start to realize why he is doing this and why for some reason it makes sense. i was trying to figure out if the acting was just great or was it the story. well the acting is amazing christian bale is batman and thats all i have to say bout that. michael cain, gary oldman, morgan freeman and liam neeson all give great performances and you can tell they put everything they had into this movie. cillian murphy as the scarecrow was something to see as they tie it all together very nicely, ken wantanabe as ra ja gule is very good even though you only see him for a short time. one aspect of the movie that could have been left out but you learn to understand why it is in there is katie holms, not to say she didn't do a great job but the character of rachel dawes being in the movie can be questioned. but as good as those actors are it was the story that makes this movie, the story was right on and explains every single thing in detail. you will not leave the theater asking yourself questions about the movie but leaving the theater talking about part after part of this movie. in closing this is the batman movie everyone has been waiting for and the superhero movie that will be the new standard on what good is.

after four films, (since 1989) and years away from the big screen, batman "begins" in a whole new way, and it's by far the best adaptation of the caped crusader on film yet.

batman begins, written by screenwriter david s. goyer, and directed by christopher nolan, is definitely the best screen version of one of the most popular icons in american history.

after more than half a century of his adventures in print, and on television, we now find out about the beginnings of the caped crusader, where he got his state-of-the-art batman fighting costume, his utility best, his cool gadgets, his batmobile, and how the batcave was conceived. best of all, batman begins allows the audience into the mind of bruce wayne and why he became batman himself in the first place.

for the first time on film, batman is not upsided by the villains of the piece, but rather batman/bruce wayne himself becomes the most interesting character of the film with some of the coolest gadgets seen in a comic book movie.

christian bale does a terrific job of becoming bruce wayne and his alter ego batman, while liam neeson, michael caine, and morgan freeman shine in their supporting roles.

only katie holmes is wasted as bruce wayne's supposed love interest, rachel dawes, an assistant gotham district attorney, and is given nothing much to do in this film.

cillian murphy, known to audiences in the film 28 days later, does a great job of portraying the frightening scarecrow.

all i can say is that batman is back and better than before, bring on the sequels of young batman and many more to come! after years of marvel dominance at the cinema, dc comics is finally back on track!

a 10 on a scale of 1-10!

well, i was glad when i came out of the theater because i was smiling. this is the definitive batman movie because it actually explore batman's origins and went a lot deeper than other previous films have attempted. this had a much grittier, darker and realistic feel which i thoroughly enjoyed the way the material was handled with great respect and care and to try and make it all realistic??? excellent approach!!!! i thought all the actors were wonderful, liam neeson as ducard/ raz, morgan freeman as lucius fox, gary oldman as commissioner gordon, michael caine as alfred, and christian bale as the bat. michael caines one liners were just hilarious. i thought katie holmes did well in this film, the tumbler was awesome, and the way batmans voice sounded when he was in the mask, awesome! especially when he shouted "rachel!" that was beautiful. i thought it was a bit sad when they broke up but then again, batman was destined for a greater love, which resides in catwoman. i especially loved it when bruce told off all the rich phonies! ha! awesome! it was just an awesome movie all around and is one of the best movies of the year!!!

this is just a throwaway to add to the list, but this film was so much fun and so well done that i just had to add something... having 2 kids, a wife, a house in the 'burbs, and being the only working one (outside anyway), means missing a lot of films until dvd release...nevertheless,i was so impressed with the scope and story of this film! in the style of the spiderman series, batman begins starts before the beginning and chronicles the evolvement of the whole sha-bang, and boy, what an evolvement! christian bale, katie holmes, michael caine, morgan freeman, ilam neeson, et. all are finely cast, and the direction, story, and appearance of this film are all right on! the care taken in the story to tie so much so neatly together is evident; any small reference at the start of the film could have major implications by the end... it's a wild, complicated plot, but hey, this is based on a comic strip and it all works! great film-making! if you are so bored that you actually read this review, i hope you had or have as much fun watching batman begins as i did!

so many times style rules over substance, leading us to true disappointment. for a change, hollywood has taken the mythic tale of the dark crusader and made it into a truly satisfying movie-going experience. bruce wayne's dual-sided personality is finely detailed, with his evolution from a scared child to a superhero.

the film explores issues of morality, vulnerability, loyalty, ethics, and more. with the help of an outstanding supporting cast, the story takes flight, allowing the audience to partake of both a fantastic array of amazing gadgets and special effects; yet the audience's emotional level never stops feeling real. michael caine, morgan freeman, and gary oldman prove themselves once again three of the finest contemporary actors.

the film, however, belongs to christian bale, whose portrayal of the dark knights shows a range of emotions rarely seen in a film of this type.

i'm glad someone finally got it right.

i wasn't excited about the prospect of batman begins. the film is based on the dc comic the batman(and, unlike the last 4, its faithful and fun) and comes from indie king christopher nolanimer. it's an attempt to revive the batman franchise, a franchise dead sense mega failure of batman & robin starring george clooney and arnold schwarzenegger. the cast for the movie was good-it continues the batflick tradition of big name actors. the trailers made it look good and serious, and the marketing was heavy. the only drawbacks were that i felt that batman was a character that when made too serious, it might not be fun. luckily, my expectations were completely confounded; batman begins is a sensational blockbuster.

despite its origins, the plot is by turns exciting and surprising. young bruce wayne sees his parents murdered before him. he leaves the world behind, and trains as a ninja. upon returning to gotham city he becomes batman. his first task is to bring in carmine falcone, but in the process he uncovers a plot against gotham involving horrifying villain the scarecrow and an old foe.

katie holmes and gary oldman strongly portray batmans two allies while michael caine shines as alfred, who is busy trying to keep bruce wayne sane. morgan freeman is hilarious and better return for the sequel, rutger hauer is good as the snobby businessman, and liam neeson and ken watanabe are quite the villainous duo in the "league of shadows".but this film is stolen by two people: first, unknown cillain murphy gives what will go down as perhaps the most memorable villain since, well, jack nicholsons joker. hes so normally creepy yet there's a trusting sense in him. but the film is really stolen by christian bale. he is the undisputed star in a inspired dramatic performance. hes also quite easy on the eyes, and can kick some serious butt when needed. some of the action is breathtakingly exciting, particularly one spectacular fight aboard the stunningly real monorail that runs through the canyons of gotham, and the batmobile chase is incredible. but perhaps the most praise worthy element of the production is gotham city-of the art and special effects don't get oscar nominated then this is biggest robbing at the oscars since titanic won best picture. its so grand in scale, i don't think i've ever seen a modern city so big in a film, yet its style and darkness is so real. all it does is add the experience. the score, by james newton howard and hans zimmer, is yet another oscar worthy item in the film.

but what makes batman begins such a triumph is the ease with which it leaps between styles. the film unexpectedly has some great comic moments, but also manages to be exciting, scary and moving. flashbacks of bruce wayne and his father are quite moving, the villain scarecrow a lot more threatening and intimidating then one would expect. from this hybrid premise you feel many directors would have delivered a half-baked pastiche but chris nolan has come up with a genuine swashbuckling epic loaded with drama, comedy, and romance. batman begins. is, in short, awesome. you cant take your eyes off the screen. its going to be a monster on dvd sales and a sequel will be eagerly anticipated. i didn't think i'd be saying this, but batman begins is the ride of the summer.

this movie is outstanding in almost every respect. not only is it arguably the best movie of the genre, but it should be considered a very good film on its own merits. i left the theatre feeling as if i had just watched an extremely well-crafted and engaging movie that happens to be about a superhero. the cast is great from top to bottom -bale perfectly finds a balance of emotional complexity and moral growth that needed for this realist rendition of the comic book hero. gary oldman is great as a conscientious cop and, even though she might have been corrupted by that alien scientologist tom cruise, katie holmes does a credible job as an assistant da with the right amount of moxie, faith and determination. caine, freeman and neison are, as usual, excellent despite the fact that the former two feel a little under-utilized but they more than make up for it by capitalizing on the screen time they were given to work with. definitely a movie not to be missed this summer and one that should be seen on the big screen.

batman begins

after schumacher's "batman forever" and "batman & robin" it proved difficult to imagine the dark knight ever being as strong as he once was when burton was at the helm. but thanks to the amazing christopher nolan and the extremely dedicated christian bale, batman is back and better than ever. this movie seriously kicks ass and although it cannot undo schumacher's unforgivable attempts at not 1 but 2 batman films, it provides more than excellent consolation.

the plot: this film is unlike the previous 4 as it takes a completely different slant on the character of batman all together. "batman begins" is more about bruce wayne than anything else. the film effectively follows his life and shows the viewers where batman came from and why. the story is brilliantly told and i do feel that this is a film which never fails to deliver. we see bruce grow up carrying the guilt surrounding his parents murders and after a court hearing where the murderer is offered early release, bruce disappears from his home of gotham city, a place that is rotting under the power of men such as carmine falcone, a big time gangster who "owns" the city of gotham. during a 7 year absence, bruce learns the art of deception and theatricality along with other values from a man named ducard and his group the league of shadows. this training inspires bruce to "save" his city and resurrect gotham to the place it once was when his parents were alive.

some viewers may be disappointed that batman doesn't actually appear until more than an hour into the film, but if you look at the film in detail and learn to appreciate the story, you will see as i said before, it is a movie about bruce wayne, not batman, hence the title "batman begins".

other characters include lucius fox (morgan freeman) and bruce's ever faithful butler alfred pennyworth (michael caine) who provides most of the laughs in this movie. bruce's love interest, rachel dawes, a district attorney for the city of gotham, is played by katie holmesyes the one from dawson's creek and yesthe one that is now engaged to tom cruise. even though she is not an original character, i have to say she acts the part well and is a character that is needed as she does give something to the movie. the villains are really the only ones that were left to pick-the scarecrow and ra's al ghulscary. i've often wondered that if the scarecrow were to be picked, how on earth they would pull of a man that wears a potato sack on his head, but much to my delight and anticipation, he does look fantastic.

the only downside to this film, and believe me it isn't easy to find one, is the unfortunate change in the story of bruce's past. any true batman fan will know that bruce's parents were murdered by jack napier, who later becomes the joker. however, because the joker has already been used as a villain (in tim burton's "batman"), he couldn't be used again. this is why bruce's parents are murdered by some no bodyalso, this means that if a sequel were to be made, it may complicate things further.., but apart from that, i would recommend this film to anyone. it's one of those movies that deserves to be seen more than once and it is a delight to see the dark knight soaring the skies of gotham city again, back to how he used to be before schumacher got his hands on him, sinister, gothic and bloody scary.

before batman (christian bale) battles his mortal enemy ducard (liam neeson), he recalls to d.a. rachel dawes (katie holmes), "...it's not who i am underneath, but what i do that defines me." director christopher nolan truly defines the dark and tragic hero, batman, by reinventing this uncompromising and gothic tale of the origins of bruce wayne and his symbol of justice, batman. his hero's will and actions define batman. nolan's "batman begins" is the best batman movie-- one of the best movies of the year. screen writers david goyer and chris nolan have created a powerful narrative driven by strong character, classic tragedy, and sheer will.

as the movie opens, wayne fortune heir, bruce wayne is searching for the darkness that lies in all men, in tibet. he believes therein lies true power. he becomes disciple of the ninja clan, the league of shadows, lead by the powerful, ra's al ghul (ken watanabe). wayne's ninja mentor, henri ducard (liam neeson), tells his charge, "to conquer your fear, you must first become your fear." personally, i have an affinity for bruce wayne, as a man who "masks his guilt" with great rage and fear.

bruce witnessed the murder of his parents as a young boy. he blames himself for not being strong enough to save his parents, and not being strong enough to avenge them as a young man. his refuge with the league of shadows ends when his act of mercy is deemed as betrayal.

bruce returns to gotham city and wayne manor. gotham is ravaged by crime, corruption, and economic depression. all the work of his late philanthropist father, thomas wayne (linus roache), has fallen in vain. wayne corp. is now run by bottom line conscious chairman of the board, mr, earle (rutger hauer). bruce reunites with his butler and caretaker, alfred (michael cain). their relationship is the underlying strength of the movie, even more so than bruce's romance with his childhood sweetheart, rachel (katie holmes). alfred raised bruce after his parents were brutally murdered, and always believes in and see the best in "master bruce". alfred believes in bruce, when bruce has forsaken himself. there is a moving scene toward the end when everything has gone awry, bruce confides in alfred, "you still haven't given up on me..." powerful relationships and the belief in people's best distinguish "batman begins".

the tale of gotham city follows several different story threads. grown up d.a. rachel dawes is a target of a crime syndicate lead by carmine falcone (tom wilkinson), refusing to compromise her ideals. a large drug shipment is due in gotham. one of the drugs is cocaine. the other is a deadly mind altering drug, employed by sanitarium director, dr. jonathan crane (a very creepy cillian murphy), who is also super-villain, scarecrow. this is part of the conspiracy to vanquish all of gotham city using this x-like drug, to establish a new order.

christian bale is simply an amazing and commanding force as bruce wayne/batman. he is a tortured and charismatic soul. bale is so believable as both bruce wayne and batman. bruce wayne becomes batman to confront his fear, and reconcile his quest for justice and revenge which may be two sides of the same coin in this context. wayne's journey to find peace in life, starts with battling evil as a symbol. as a man he knows that he can be killed. an ideal or symbol can live forever. the great thing about the movie, is that in the end compassion and mercy are qualities of great strength. batman is distinct among the superheroes in that he does not possess any superpowers. he uses his intelligence, skill, and courage. he battles evil driven by sheer force of will. bale imposes awesome will as batman and bruce wayne.

however, even sheer will needs to enroll others in the cause of justice over great evil. enter, lucius fox played by the great morgan freeman. freeman adds a refreshing light touch as the "james bond- m" to batman. fox is the wayne corp. scientist demoted to the labs-- pastures. fox provides the body armor, utilities, and batmobile to the gothic hero. batman is now ready to battle the evil in gotham, and more profoundly reconcile the fear and rage deep inside himself.

the fact that the love story of bruce and rachel is downplayed, is effective. this emphasizes the tragedy that is bruce wayne's journey. katie holmes is perfect as rachel dawes. her rachel is the heart-broken idealist, who despite all has faith in bruce. holmes is beautiful, exuding a quiet strength and faith.

the supporting cast are amazingly talented. liam neeson as ducard is powerful, and his character turn is surprising. michael caine gives alfred such strength and compassion. he provides a soul in chris nolan's gothic vision. gary oldman is rock solid as det. jim gordon (before he was commissioner gordon). ken watanabe is awesome as ra's al ghul, which is a surprising cameo role.

nolan gives "batman begins" a physically dark, gritty look that is visually stunning. the action sequences are expertly done. the ninja fighting and training scenes are amazing. the fighting sequences with bale as batman are sleek and crisp. he truly mastered the physical aspect of the character. in the end acknowledge nolan for making a movie driven by strong characters and a compelling hero's story. christian bale has arrived as a major force. he imposes his sheer will as both batman and bruce wayne. nolan and bale have reinvented batman, having something to say. ultimately, "batman begins" is a story of redemption, compassion, and mercy. in this context may batman as a symbol live on.

obviously there will be people turned of to this movie because of the infamous batman & robin... and batman returns... and batman forever... some people may be turned off because of the unorthodox batmobile that seems to be the focus of many a criticisms. forget all of that. this film finally takes the character of bruce wayne and give him justice. if you have any inhibitions about seeing this movie, forget them. great cast, great acting, great story. the perfect way to reclaim the glory that tim burton brought to the original. i am still in awe of the development of the motivations of young batman. from the very first shot of the bats to the final confrontation with al-guhl, the first half of the movie and its buildup of wayne's character are phenomenal. it only gets better from there. the action, the story, nothing disappointed me and nolan deserves a lot of respect. the scarecrow is finally given just praise as a legitimate villain, as he was unrightfully ignored in the first 4 films. while nolan took some artistic license, it's entirely expected in any superhero film. bale, holmes, neelson, freeman, all do exceptional jobs with their characters and breathe new life into the gotham world. with its themes of fear, vengeance, revenge, vigilance, unique social commentary, impeccable tone, and overall authenticity of the batman univerise, this is not adam west's batman. here's to a new beginning to the batman legacy...

i was a little apprehensive about bale as batman... then i saw batman begins and i was floored... christian bale was amazing in both roles as the hero and the antagonist. katie holmes surprised me with an outstanding performance. and the minor roles of gary oldman, liam neeson, morgan freeman, and michael caine brought back my faith that big name actors can have small parts in a big movie and not over-power the outcome of the story. i don't think that has really been done since pulp fiction. the film was dark, full of meaning, humor, drama, plot, beautiful visuals... if you are a dark knight fan you will love this, if you are the casual movie goer you will love this. it is a beautiful movie and worth every bit of hype and praise and adoration... but thats just me! but honestly, the best part about the movie was the lack of typical superhero attitude (from the love interest to why he does what he does) that you see with superman and spiderman... batman is and will always be the best superhero around...!

i remember seeing the new batsuit on a empire magazine; i did not like it at all.

"looks like something the army would create", is what i said.

bruce wayne lives a happy childhood, born to one of the most wealthiest families in gotham city; he spends his days playing with the house maid's daughter, rachel.however his life is about to change when he fall into a old family well; and here he encounters something that will become a fear and a weapon.

a bat.

later on bruce accompanies his parents to the opera where his bat phobia returns and he leaves; as his parents exit the opera house they are mugged and in the process bruce's parents are killed.

bruce grows up alone with only his family butler, as a guardian.

as he grows older he becomes more and more disillusioned and wants revenge on the criminals responsible for the death of his parents. this thirst for revenge ends his friendship with rachel and a meeting with a local gangster, carmine falcone; leaves the young man with a dilemma.

how can you bring someone to justice, who is feared? bruce leaves gotham and goes travelling and meets ra's al ghul; leader of a vigilante group. bruce learns valuable lessons, especially the one thing that will help him the most. fear.

as bruce realises the difference between revenge and justice he finds himself in a predicament; ra's al ghul is a killer, something bruce is not. bruce destroys ra's al ghul fraternity and arrives back in gotham ready to fight the evil that infests the city.

he discovers the bat cave; finds a symbol that he can use, a bat. he finds high-tech weapon and armour that was designed for the army and uses this to aid him, he tracks down gangster carmine falcone and brings him to justice only to learn theirs a bigger threat, scarecrow.

a psychopathic psychologist; as batman wages war with the insane, he finds his alter-ego, the batman becoming more and more dominant.

nolan brings the batman origins into the light in this movie; the origins of the bat have never been revealed on a live action movie.

christian bale portrays the role of multi-millionaire with pure elegance and plays batman with a ferocity. actos such as liam neeson, michael caine, gary oldman, morgan freeman and even katie holmes hold there own, against the lead.

but cillian murphy is a pure treat as the sadistic and insane scarecrow; he oozes evil.
