overall, christopher nolan sets his batman trilogy on the right path with this movie. everything about this movie appeals to batman fans, or superhero fans in general. everything about the movie is great. christian bale takes on the role of batman and does one of the best jobs as the character to this day. the movie accurately captures the character "scarecrow" and tops it off with the league of shadows and ra's al ghul. this movie is absolutely perfect, every dc fan should see it. 10/10

the first time i saw a trailer for this movie i though it will be a big hit. the critics said it is a big hit. and after watching the movie, i guess i was right. you take a good story, amazing director, mix it with the great and talented actors and what you get is the movie people will be talking about for a while. christian bale shines as he changes the traditional batman character into something completely new. let's not forget morgan freeman who is interesting as always. this movie leaves us guessing and wanting more. i have to say the audience, including myself, will be looking forward the next chapter of batman movies. (that is if there will be another batman movie made.) this movie is definitely oscar-worthy.

in 'batman begins', christopher nolan's suburb introduction to the caped crusader, fear drives the story. fear must be conquered but fear is also used to conquer. bruce wayne must stare his fear straight in the eye to truly become the symbol of justice he intends to be. the film uses the thematic nature of fear to drive the story and the character of bruce wayne, it makes the film a satisfying whole.

'batman begins' is a brilliant opening film to this reboot of one of pop cultures most popular characters. it is brilliant because it defines how and why bruce wayne becomes the man he becomes and the symbol of justice in which he chooses to fight fear. in the opening act two major things happen, one when bruce wayne is a child falling into a well on the grounds of wayne manor. he is trapped in a dark, lonely place, confronted by hundreds of bats. the other event is the murder of his parents, in front of his own eyes. this was a result of wayne's fear resulting in him asking to leave a play the family were attending. fear, guilt and later anger consume bruce in regards to his parents death, part of him wants to avenge their deaths but another part knows that there is a greater responsibility, one that he must oblige to. this is spurred by his fathers own efforts to clean up the streets of gotham, in his own way.

the opening act so adeptly introduces us to the character of bruce wayne (christian bale) and what drives him, it also introduces us to 'the league of shadows' , ra's al ghul and henri ducard (liam neeson). the scenes between neeson and bale are fantastic in setting up wayne's strengths and weaknesses. ducard refers to compassion being a weakness that enemies will not share but wayne insists that is what sets him apart. of course if he did not have that compassion he would be a villain.

in the second act we are introduced to the character of batman. batman is wayne's way of using a symbol of fear against his enemies. it is this element of fear mixed with the compassion that mark wayne as an interesting character. to do this he must create a mask, to do this wayne needs his own company - particularly the applied sciences department and lucius fox - to gain the resources he needs, including weapons, armour and heavy duty vehicles! the film is essentially a number of larger and smaller introductions and both the introductions to wayne and batman are exceptional because the thematic elements as to wayne's motivations are always at the forefront of the story.

the second act also introduces us to the major plot of the film that lies beneath the true intentions of the film - and to be honest fully tie back into those intentions. we are introduced to jim gordon (gary oldman), the first of batman's allies, the only honest cop in gotham. we are introduced to the criminal component of gotham with crime boss carmine falcone (tom wilkinson) and dr. jonathan crane/scarecrow (cillian murphy). we are also introduced to rachel dawes (katie holmes), the childhood friend that wayne still cares about. the plot largely has to do with the misplacing of a devise that can vaporise water. scarecrow is working for someone who wants to use that machine to cripple gotham, by running drugs through the water system thus allowing the toxins of the drug to be inhaled by the poor citizens of gotham. i fully expected the film to be weaker once this plot was introduced but the man behind this diabolical plan happens to tie in with wayne's beginnings on the path to becoming batman thus the film ultimately comes full circle by the end.

there are so many elements that i love about this film. not just the thematic elements but the design elements, the tumbler acts as the armoured tank version of the batmobile. it is robust, bulky and angular. it is a perfect machine for this new batman, one that is based more on reality than previous incarnations but when that has a darker and more dangerous appeal. i love some of the images from the toxins that scarecrow uses with his mask - or the images we see when the toxin has been released, such as batman looking like the devil or the surreal image of scarecrow riding a fire breathing horse.

christian bale is the perfect choice for bruce wayne/batman. to be honest it doesn't take much to play a decent batman, as long as you are physically cut out for the role but in wayne, bale is able to play the role as a conflicted, angry man who uses fear to drive him. he is also really good at being the philanthropist arsehole, the other mask wayne sometimes uses to turn attentions away from any suspicious activities he may be up to. mostly all of the cast are great in their roles, michael caine, gary oldman and liam neeson especially, but holmes is absolutely miscast as dawes and rightly replaced in the dark knight.

overall though, this is a brilliant introduction to an iconic character or characters. nolan proves he was up to the task of taking on such a hot property and being able to deal with a big budget production, in fact this is only the beginning of what he could achieve. a cracking film all round.

1989-1992 tim burton made two classic batman films ("batman" and "batman returns"), just great and must-watch movies. in 1995, joel schumacher did "batman forever", which actually was a good movie, but with only a good and perfect performance (jim careey -the ridler). and then, in 1997, schumacher completely ruined the franchise with the film stupidly stupid "batman and robin", ruining and destroying the batman franchise forever, being vanished from hollywood what seemed to be forever. eight years later, in 2005, it was given the task for christopher nolan to resurrect the franchise from the dead, some liked the idea, others thought it was going to be another horrible movie, and it was?! far, far from it!

"begins" tells the story of bruce wayne (christian bale), who as a child saw his parents die in front of him during a robbery. years pass and bruce returns to his hometown gotham city for the final judgment of chill, the murderer of his parents. bruce planned to kill him with his father pistol at the end of the trial. but before bruce could have the chance, a woman kills chill at close range, because chill had secrets from the big criminal mind of the city, carmine falcone (tom wikinson). after that bruce leaves the city and begins a journey around the world with the mission of knowing and understand the criminal minds and tries to somehow tackle corruption and violence of his city. and then he meets ducard (liam neeson) who offers bruce the chance and the weapons to fulfill its mission. months later bruce returns to gotham with the help of his butler and best friend alfred (michael caine). now more mature and decided, bruce begins to do justice with his own hands, but not as the man bruce wayne, but with his new identity, "batman".

what nolan begins to resurrect the franchise is not only putting the story more mature and also full of action without exaggeration (not lacking in this film), is doing the character of bruce wayne relevant. in previous films, bruce wayne was only the rich guy who decided to do justice, and his main concern was to hide his superhero identity out of the press. here, it is also that, much better, but also humanizes the character. for the first time we see the man behind the mask, making him a relatable character (thus, making us finally to worry about his character). all thanks to a superb storytelling that nolan gives the film, giving dialogs tat flows perfectly to the characters and for the first time a superheroes movie really well written and also we feel that everything in the story is real, that it could really happen in our world.

nolan was only known for the magnificent "memento" and the underrated "insomnia", both were known for their realistic style that works very well in this movie as well. since batman's car and gadgets, all with their scientific explanations (all possible, look it up), and even the gotham city (filmed in chicago). nolan makes gotham the economic center of america, but also the center of corruption and violence (new york ¬¬¬¬¬¬¬¬¬plus chicago). making with the obscure style of the first films of burton, while keeping the realism.

great story and excellent direction, but also their characters guarantee the final success. nolan surprisingly, even not faithfully following the comic-book, he manage to bring to the movie many of the characters (even some that not major fans knew that existed). christian bale simply superb both as bruce wayne and batman (in my opinion the best batman actor who ever had); liam neeson as mentor (and a surprise later) simply excellent; michael caine is superb, capturing the spirit of alfred , loyal and funny; gary oldman also captures the spirit of commissioner gordon perfectly, stubborn and smart with a hatred of injustice and corruption; morgan freeman as lucius fox (nor i knew he existed), the inventor of the hero's gadgets, and captures the right philosophy that he and bruce wayne had in the comic, if lucius knew or not that bruce was the masked man, always a mystery.

even not faithfully following the comic and realizing the dreams of fans, nolan resurrected the franchise completely. managing to capture the spirit of the only superhero without powers, putting a dark and even a cop-thriller tone to the history. also bringing heart and soul to the character of bruce wayne, and all the other characters thanks to an excellent narrative; superb direction really well action packed. what at first was to be a prequel to the classic burton was the great beginning of one of the best trilogies ever made.

9/10

after enduring many years of waiting for the right portrayal of the dark knight, this movie has finally hit the nail on the head. everything from start to finish truly grips the viewer into thinking that batman can be a reality in our world. no more of batman jumping off rooftops, no more of how unrealistically invulnerable he is, because this movie explains every single detail that makes batman who he is and how he fights the crime of gotham through very believable ways.

the casting is fantastic. christian bale is perfect. his gripping performance highlights the dilemma that is within bruce wayne and also the true angst that surrounds batman's mood and style of crime fighting. this aspect has always been difficult to portray and yet christian bale has done it perfectly. alfred was great and again, a great snatch by the makers of batman to cast a wonderful actor in michael caine. his portrayal, alike to thomas wayne, is the perfect balance that keeps batman's sanity. the villains are great too. cilian murphy is perfect with his quietly psychotic portrayal of the scarecrow and liam neeson's very lasting impression of ra's al ghul. together with ken watanbe (his decoy), their exchanges in the movie helped built the character perfectly. katie holmes portrayal of bruce wayne's love interest though, has seen very little screen time. however, her role in the movie is essential in building and sustaining the idealism that is in bruce wayne. hopefully, we will see her character being further developed in the following batman movies. last but not least, the addition portrayals of both lucius fox by morgan freeman and commissioner gordon by gary oldman adds the the reality of batman that in these two, batman has found great allies in fighting crime.

i must truly say that the dialog, script and the setting of gotham city is perfect but special mention must go to the creators of the new batmobile. it is awesome! the structure of the vehicle, the chase scenes... fantastic to the very end.

last but not least, i would like to thank the team of batman of choosing the right concept and theme for batman - fear, that will grip the hearts of villains and criminals alike. and for all those out there guessing who the next villain will be... he will be back by popular demand, playing batman's arch nemesis, and all batman fans out there will be eager to find out who will be casted into that role.

thank you to all that contributed to the perfect movie for all batman fans worldwide

batman begins (2005) is nothing short of a cinematic triumph, redefining the superhero genre and setting the gold standard for origin stories. directed by christopher nolan, this movie flawlessly captures the essence of the dark knight, combining rich storytelling, stunning visuals, and a powerful score to deliver an unforgettable experience. it's the perfect balance of character development, action, and thematic depth, earning a well-deserved 10/10.

story and character development at its core, batman begins is a story of transformation. it brilliantly chronicles bruce wayne's journey from a grief-stricken orphan to gotham's savior. the narrative is meticulously crafted, taking its time to delve into bruce's motivations, fears, and moral struggles. his time training with the league of shadows, guided by the enigmatic ra's al ghul (liam neeson), is compelling and gives the film a grounded yet epic feel.

unlike typical superhero movies that gloss over the "why" of a hero's journey, this film explores every detail of bruce's psyche and his decision to become batman. christian bale's portrayal is pitch-perfect, embodying both the tortured soul of bruce wayne and the determined, morally driven persona of batman. his duality as a flawed human and a symbol of hope is beautifully realized.

supporting cast the supporting cast is equally phenomenal. michael caine's alfred brings warmth and wisdom, serving as bruce's moral compass and emotional anchor. gary oldman as jim gordon is earnest and relatable, providing a grounded perspective amidst the chaos. morgan freeman's lucius fox adds a touch of humor and intellect, while liam neeson's ra's al ghul is a complex and menacing antagonist with a philosophy that challenges bruce's ideals. cillian murphy's chilling performance as dr. jonathan crane/scarecrow is an added bonus, making every scene he's in utterly captivating.

cinematography and direction nolan's direction is masterful. the way gotham city is portrayed-gritty, shadowy, and oppressive-perfectly mirrors the tone of the story. cinematographer wally pfister captures the darkness of the city while still creating visually stunning set pieces. from the haunting bat cave to the chaotic narrows, every setting feels alive and integral to the story.

the action sequences are a testament to nolan's attention to detail. the fights are raw and visceral, showcasing batman's skills while maintaining a sense of realism. the batmobile chase scene is thrilling, combining practical effects with clever cinematography to deliver pure adrenaline.

themes and depth what truly sets batman begins apart is its depth. it's not just a superhero movie; it's a film about fear, justice, and redemption. the exploration of fear-both as a weapon and as a personal hurdle-adds layers of complexity to the story. bruce doesn't just fight criminals; he fights the fear within himself and uses it to inspire change in gotham.

the moral dilemmas posed by ra's al ghul's extremist ideology versus bruce's belief in justice create thought-provoking tension. the film's themes resonate beyond the comic book world, making it as much a philosophical drama as an action blockbuster.

music and sound hans zimmer and james newton howard's score is a masterpiece in itself. the music perfectly complements the film's tone, with tracks like "molossus" amplifying the intensity of key moments. the score's balance of haunting melodies and triumphant crescendos makes it unforgettable.

conclusion batman begins is everything a superhero movie should be-and more. it's intelligent, thrilling, emotional, and visually stunning. every aspect of the film, from the cast to the cinematography, direction, and score, comes together to create a masterpiece. it doesn't just tell the story of batman; it redefines what the character stands for and cements his place as one of the most compelling heroes in cinema.

a perfect 10/10, batman begins isn't just a great superhero movie-it's a great film, period.

batman begins directed by: christopher nolan

the dark knight makes a triumphant return as christopher nolan directs a restart of the popular "batman" franchise. it has been eight years since a batman movie of any kind has been released, and it was well worth the wait.

plot: unlike the previous four movies, "begins" explores the main origins of how billionaire bruce wayne (christian bale) became batman. the audience is captivated into a world that for once, takes place outside of gotham city, as wayne seeks to join the infamous league of shadows (lead by ra's al ghul- ken watanabe). his journey takes him into asia and is trained by ra's right-hand man ducard (liam neeson). wayne, still trying to overcome the loss of his parents, learns he needs to control his fear and unleash it on those who use it as a weapon. in this case, the fear is bats. steadily, wayne transforms into batman and begins his quest to restore justice in gotham city.

characters: bale delivers as bruce wayne and batman, something many feel was a hard task to accomplish in the previous four films. the audience can actually see a difference between wayne and batman, and they are easily two different characters. as usual, liam neeson plays the mentor role, and does a superb job in the process. many complain that katie holmes, who plays love interest rachel dawes, was not suitable for the role. it is a little distracting, but not enough to tear one away from the movie. michael caine fits alfred like a glove, and i've always been a fan of michael gough. the performance that stood out for me though, was cillian murphy's representation of the scarecrow. he is downright creepy, and his performance is right up there with jack nicholson's joker. supporting actors morgan freeman (lucius fox, batman's version of "q"), and gary oldman (the determined future-commissioner gordon) solidify this outstanding cast.

analysis: "batman begins" is uncharacteristically realistic for a superhero movie, but this is one of the movie's best qualities. the audience actually believes that a bruce wayne's self discovery is indeed possible, which grips them into thinking a story like this could actually happen. the realism comes down to how batman got his costume, something the audience never understood or even cared about until now. this is what i liked most, how believable it was.

bottom-line: superhero fan or not, this is a must see. outstanding. 9/10

i wouldn't know where to start. i knew if this movie wasn't the best comic book movie ever, i would've been disappointed. going in, i have the highest expectations ever. nolan? bale? freeman? neeson? oldman? you're kidding me right? if this movie flops, it would be the biggest disappointment of all-time.

no exaggeration, this movie makes spider-man feel gay and x-men's wolverine feel soft and i loved the sm & x-men movies. it's dark, it's scary, it's real and much much more.

kudos to nolan for making the movie all about character development for batman. good for him. i see a lot of people complaining about the fight sequences. i have no idea how stupid some of these audiences are. fact : nolan did those fighting sequences like that on purpose to focus in on the whole "stealth/ninja" gibberish. it was totally believable on my part.

christian bale. wow! this is a huge achievement on his part. how do you go from playing trevor reznik at 120 lbs to bulking up like that within a few weeks to audition for batman? dude is a genius. he is the best batman by far. i mean obviously second best would be given to michael keaton but he looks too old for a bruce wayne.

i hate liam neeson. i hate gary oldman. i don't mind michael caine. i love morgan freeman though. it didn't matter. all of the supporting cast except for holmes kicked ass. i'd like to take this time to say liam neeson was probably the best performance other then bale himself.

people will say it over and over and over again and the reason this movie worked so well was because batman is real. he doesn't have super power and all that mambo jumbo to make him who he is. he's real. he's human, he bleeds, he can be destroyed.

i also like the fact that the movie really zooms in on bruce wayne being the mask of batman and not the other way around.

i could go on and on and on and so forth but this is so far the best movie of the year competiting with millers sin city and it is by far the best comic book movie ever. if this is what we're in store for when it comes to x-3 or spider-man 3 or even batman 2, then pardon my french but jesus christ! a

simply put batman begins is the best ever comic-book movie adaption because it not only entertains us but also makes us think. chris nolan did a fantastic job in breathing life into the batman story and the whole 'superhero' genre. the film works on all levels, it has a great origin story to set it up brilliantly, an excellent cast, clever script and visuals that don't rely on too much cgi ( which too many other superhero movies now rely on) and a director who wanted to give it a realism which other superhero movies don't have. chris nolan said he wanted to give the film an epic cast similar to the one in superman and he delivered a top- notch cast who all filled the roles perfectly, bale was a superb choice and has made the role his like sean connery did james bond, everybody suited there roles and liam neeson i thought was particularly excellent as ducard and when he returns as ras al ghul near the action-packed ending he became a brilliant baddie! even the lesser-known actors like cillian murphy, tom wilkinson and mark boone junior added a touch of class on top of having acting gods like caine, oldman, freeman and neeson above them. the bar has been raised and it will be difficult to top this when the follow-up eventually hits screens, a poll put the begins sequel as the most anticipated movie and after seeing batman begins you can see why, we want more! batman begins is a great movie and should have been up for best film at the oscars but was vastly overlooked for 'meaning movies' - what a disgrace! bring on the joker! honorable mention for comic-book movies must also go to superman:the movie which was a classic but begins wins overall.

this is truly the correct incarnation of batman. there is so much happening in this film, and yet none of it seems rushed in any way. it is a true comic book film, yet it never seems campy or even very unrealistic.

the strongest point is easily the cast. christian bale portrays batman and bruce wayne both with such realism. perhaps a key point is that bale avoids trying to make batman look like bruce wayne in a batsuit. bale realizes that to a degree they are different personalities, and he conveys this in just the right way. cillian murphy is wonderful as jonathan crane, and even katie holmes, who is way too young to be a lawyer, manages to perform her role with excellence. the real treats are michael caine, who is truly the perfect alfred, morgan freeman, who adds a bit of down to earthness, and gary oldman, who makes jim gordon a likable guy who grounds gotham in a sense of reality (after all, not every cop can be corrupt!) batman begins really succeeds when it is explaining how things come together. you can actually start to understand the mysterious (and previously silly) aspects of the character. and bale does such an excellent job of creating the character through real emotions that real people feel.

and of course, the direction of christopher nolan has brought it all together so well. this is a great film. to call it the best batman movie is to simply not do it justice. i have always believed batman was the purist, most praiseworthy superhero. now we have a film that does that ideal justice.

this movie hit the mark on how and why batman is beloved by so many comic-lovers and film-goers alike. tim burton and joel schumacher, while giving us four memorable batfilms (well three, if you want to exclude batman&robin), missed the mark on the star, batman.

don't get me wrong, i still enjoy burton and schumacher's films, and if it wasn't for them, christopher nolan may have never had the chance to make this masterpiece.

christian bale is the batman! no question about it. of course, we can not forget about the rest of the talented cast: sir michael caine, liam neeson, katie holmes, cillian murphy, morgan freeman, gary oldman, ken watanabe, and tom wilkinson. without them, we would be wondering what could have been.

i give this film a 10/10 all the way! -serpent

batman begins, is based upon the batman comic books and is a prequel to the previous batman films made. the film takes place when bruce wayne (batman) is an eight year old child who lives with his rich parents in gotham city. his father thomas wayne, owns the wayne building and and tries to do good for the city. one day after leaving an opera bruce's parents are killed by a robber and bruce is raised by the family butler alfred. when he gets older bruce travels and on the way is taught martial arts and several years later returns home when he was presumed dead. bruce gets a job working at his father's company which was left to him and he sees how the city is run with corruption and violence so he plans to use his martial arts skills for good. bruce meets lucius fox, a scientist at the wayne building who he has discovered has made several weapons and a suit which was meant for the army. bruce takes the equipment and alters it a bit and soon becomes batman and tries to right the wrong in gotham city by bringing down the various evils. batman currently has to take down a drug lord and a doctor who is releasing his toxic drug in the water supply of the city. batman begins, has good direction, a good script, good performances by everyone involved, good original music, good cinematography, good film editing, good production design, good art direction and good set decoration. i was a big fan of batman and batman returns, and i remember liking batman: mask of the phantasm and the animated batman series as well. i however did not like batman forever or batman and robin, so i wasn't quite sure if i would like this film or not. one reason i liked batman and batman returns so much was because of the dark atmosphere and setting provided by director tim burton for both films which was sorely missed in batman forever and batman and robin. i must say that i was very pleasantly surprised with batman begins. the film has a great story that at times is serious and at other times very entertaining and original. the film is also engaging, stylish, well acted and well made, is entertaining with a lot of action, it is fun and unique. actor christian bale makes a good bruce wayne/batman and i liked how the film's director christopher nolan didn't use a lot of cgi for some of the effects. the film is good looking and has a nice dark futuristic type atmosphere and the film as some good art and set decoration. batman begins is the first real surprise i have had with a movie in theaters this year so far. i really thought the film would just be a dumb action film that would be quickly forgotten but i was sure wrong. there is a lot more to this movie than the action and it is very thought provoking and engaging. and then we get the action and the film is very entertaining. this film works on many levels and hits all the right keys to being a perfect superhero film and is just as good as the original batman from 1989 by tim burton. one of the best action films i have seen in years and a true masterpiece. one of the best films of the year.

it's been 16 years since the world was introduced to batman on the big screen and oh, how we cherished that film and the sequel that came after it. i say sequel, because the "other" two films that came after batman returns were a disgrace to the comic book franchise. the truth is, it's been almost 9 years since george clooney graced us as the caped hero and that was just about long enough for me to forget about how stupid and cheesy it and it's predecessor really were. luckily for us though, time heals, so by the time the idea for batman begins was released to the public, i think we were all ready for something new and exciting. and i must say we got what we wanted, plus 100 times more in what many critics, including myself, are dubbing the best batman flick yet.

with a cast like the one in batman begins, it's hard to single out just one actor. even before seeing this film, i felt like no other actor would match michael keaton's performances in the first two batman flicks, but christian bale did, plus some. and bale (american psycho, equilibrium, the machinist) wasn't just good, he was convincing, yet raw, which played nicely to the story going on. bale brought all the anger into the role that was needed and just ran with it. but, that wasn't all. he was great without the cape too, cracking jokes and pulling off that playboy charm we all love in the bruce wayne character.

playing opposite bale was such screen legends as michael caine, playing alfred pennyworth, morgan freeman, playing the tech-savy lucius fox and of course liam neeson, who was excellent as ducard. but, at no point did any of these screen legends overpower bale, which was needed to keep the focus on his character. not even cillian murphy's scarecrow, who was brilliant, overpowered bale's batman. and in reality, there probably could have been more scarecrow/batman exchanges, but who knows, maybe there will be in the next film. filling out the rest of the powerful cast was katie holmes, who was good in her small role as assistant d.a. rachel dawes and gary oldman, who played a very convincing jim gordon, the last good cop left in gotham.

the one thing that is almost undeniable in batman begins is the amount of detail that was put into it. i can't think of anything that was missed or didn't flow with the rest of the story. that says something about director christopher nolan's (memento) work ethic, who is really a rookie director. it's clear he worked hard with screenwriter david s. goyer (blade trilogy) on making sure he gathered all the right information on the cast of characters included in his film. detail like that and the detail surrounding batman himself was enough to ignite this film into something bigger than itself.

i think the one aspect that defined this film was how well the story was molded into the action and special effects, something george lucas obviously forgot to do with star wars: episode iii  revenge of the sith. nolan did wonders with goyer's story and made sure the effects around the story were not overdone, a key to films like this. the one aspect of the action that caught me by surprise though was nolan's camera work with the fight sequences of batman. instead of just having a big open fight sequence, nolan chose to use batman's undeniable scare tactics on his victims as the biggest weapon, almost like an element of surprise. and you know, some critics say this film could have been better visually, but i disagree. i think the balance between the story and the special effects was perfect, right down to some of what i call the "money shots" of batman flying or standing atop a building.

with two films to go, batman begins was the ideal start to refuel this once famed franchise. with a script that couldn't have been better, director christopher nolan earned his worth in hollywood by producing one of the best adaptations of a graphic novel in recent memory. if you didn't know who christian bale was before this film, you certainly will after it, in a movie that almost makes you forget about any previous batman flicks, which is a feat like no other if you ask me.

a+

the first time i saw it, i knew it was the best film in the batman franchise. not only because today we can do whatever we want to do because the film industry broaden its limitation, and taken a new step in visual greatness. if we compare the four batman movies in today's, the special effects had improved and if batman wishes to blow up a solid concrete in the rooftop, he can easily do so, very realistic and not cartoonish. but i don't really care about the special effects they put in the movies. it's not the point, the real reason why i love this film is because it was directed by christopher nolan (memento, the prestige); with his powerful style of directing that will blow you away with its amazing lines, and his cast did a very very strong acting, including the veteran actor, michael caine as the ever faithful alfred pennyworth, the butler of the wayne family. and of course the supporting actors, gary oldman as sergeant and soon-to-be lieutenant gordon, liam neeson as henri ducard, morgan freeman as lucius fox (same with q in the james bond movies). christian bale's bruce wayne exceeded all the actors that had played it (michael keaton, val kilmer, and george clooney). he did a great job of being a billionaire and a playboy, and of course being his alter-ego, batman. tim burton and joel schumacher had handled it, but no one does it better than christopher nolan! batman begins is all about conquering fears and preventing gotham city from self-destruction. it was delivered to us wonderfully entertaining like nolan's other films. the transformation of bruce wayne to the creature he had feared all his life and his reason for being the gotham city's dark knight is so powerfully shown to us. the gotham city is dark, dirty and full of criminals everywhere like it always was. nolan's gotham city structure is quite amazing, it is darker and had a more realistic tone than the other batman movies. the film focuses on its people and the humanity. hans zimmer's score brought a heavier theme. batman's first contact in the screen was one of the finest moments in the film, you don't know where he is, where he's coming from and who's his next target. the scene where batman was talking to gordon, and when gordon replied to him he's gone is a cool thing, he did it many times in the film. whenever batman is in the screen you can't stop watching him, he's a powerful force in the screen, and he'll just let you drop your mouth when he's making his moves. there are many great scenes in this film, keep a good look at those when you watch it, i've already seen batman begins five times, and it's not hard to tell that i'm a big fan of batman. scarecrow is the perfect antagonist since it is all about fear, he completes the entire idea of the film. but who's missing in the film? it's the crazy freak, joker, the archenemy of gotham's dark knight. in the last scene you'll know that he will be the next chaos maker in the next picture.

you bet your a** it is! i just got back from a showing of the latest batman installment, and while i have always held tim burton's batman in very high regard, it in no way matches the brilliant story and directing shown in this newest installment.

christopher nolan (memento) directs from a script penned by david goyer (blade 2). the story shows how bruce wayne became batman. now previous entries in the batman franchise were good in their own right. tim burton of course delivered us a great film in 1989, due in part to the performances of michael keaton, and of course jack nicholson. in the newest film, we have a new batman, played exquisitely by christian bale, and of course a new villain, scarecrow played by cillian murphy.

the performances in the film were top notch to say the least, from the fear ridden and guilt consuming bruce wayne to the maniacal paranoia's of cillian murphy. what was executed flawlessly was the direction of the picture. chris nolan, still shows us that after 3 films he has what it takes to tell a great story with superb direction. my only complaint in the whole film was the camera work done during the fight sequences... *** chris... move the camera's back so we can see the beatings taking place. *** i will admit i did roll my eyes a few times at the over dramatic delivery of batman's lines from time to time, but it was easily forgotten as the story unfolded. each performance from michael caine, morgan freeman, & gary oldman was terrific and well honed, and you felt for every one of these characters. liam neeson gave a truly enlightening performance, where was this performance during star wars ep. 1 i ask... i guess he saved it for batman begins.

chris nolan succeeded on many lines with this film... joel schumacher should take notes, as should a lot of director's of superhero comics turned film. however, chris cannot get all the credit. david goyer had a truly superb script, and warner brothers should be on their knees kissing his feet thanking him for such a great story. i read the batman begins script early last year and i told everyone i knew that this is the batman movie to go see.

this entry into the franchise runs a little long, it comes in around 2 hours and 25 mins, but it goes by so quickly because you are just engrossed in the story from beginning to end. now while i praise bb for being the best batman movie ever, i will also extend that praise to the team behind it, including the cast. one thing that i kept flashing back to while watching bb was christian bale's performance. his performance reminded me of the same performance he gave as daytime stock broker patrick bateman in american pyshco. i was smiling from ear to ear every time he would get into his patrick bateman mode. it was truly a joy to watch.

now i know some of you have commented on the 8.6 rating this movie has received on the imdb.com boards... well let me tell you, it deserves a 9.5. so do yourself a favor. turn off your computer, get in the car, head to the cinema, and buy yourself a ticket for batman begins. then go into the theater, sit back and enjoy the ride.

batman begins is truly the best superhero film ever made, and should be used as a model for all future superhero movies.

just perfect, the best of all the four, with character development, great action, good acting, it all fits perfect.....

the movie goes back to the or-gin of bruce wayne who later have the alter ego batman, the story follows him in his quest for justice, and how he became batman, he must save a city in ruins of corruption and drugs....

he will face challenges like dr. jonathan crane (cillian murphy) who will become the scarecrow, ra's all ghul (ken wattanbe) a fearful leader of a group who goes by the name of: league of shadows, a group who wants justice butt by extreme methods, carmine falcone (tom wilkinsen) a gangster who runs gotham, and not only batman gets his enemies also bruce wayne must save his wayne company from richard earle (rutger hauer).....

butt he also gets help from the likes of his always trustworthy butler alfred (michael caine), a woman who also seeks justice (katie holmes, a man who supplies the mechanics for the batman who's name is lucius fox (morgan freeman, always great) and of course one of the only good and honest cop jim gordon (gary oldman, who nails it)....

it is truly a wonderful film and finally after the good burton movies, who were more burton than batman, this is not only a great film butt a great batman film....

the movie was absolutely perfect. the actors were incredible. i had never heard of christian bale before this movie. but his performance was incredible. he is by far the ultimate batman. but my highest commendment actorwise would go to liam neeson. liam was absolutely perfect. when he played ra's al ghul, he was so different from playing henri ducard. he did not alter anything about himself, but one thing: his personality. liam knows how to become the character he's playing. his performance was absolutely enthralling. the other performers were extraordinary as well. katie holmes, morgan freeman, and gary oldman. the best commendment of all would go to christopher nolan and david goyer. excellent plot formation. now that i've bored you by having you read all of this; i think i'll end it by saying: batman begins has an extraordinary cast. i think bob kane would be proud. if you want to see a movie that lives up to the legend...well...look no further.

i took my dad out for father's day to see this. we saw it at a new theater that opened a few days ago. it was great. i think it is even better than the first film. batman was great, batman returns was just as good, batman forever was decent, and batman and robin was just plain terrible. it is about bruce wayne before he becomes batman. he trains with the league of shadows. he meets lucius fox, who is the scientific head of wayne enterprises. he gives bruce the car, weapons and equipment, and the suit. he learns that a hallucinogen is going to destroy the city. it turns out that the league is behind it. christen bale is great. michael caine, katie holmes, gary oldman, and morgan freeman were also good. we meet the scarecrow, who was very frighting and cool looking. i had no regrets seeing this.

"batman begins," under the direction of christohper nolan (memento), breathes new life into a franchise that was nearly demolished with "batman and robin." christian bale's bruce wayne/batman is more dark than michael keaton's version. bruce clearly has issues with bats and the death of his parents (his fear of bats caused him to want to leave the theater the night his parents where killed). gotham city is a cesspool of corruption, with gangster carmine falcone (tom wilkinson)running the town. during bruce's journey, he is soon trained by ducard (liam neeson)to perfect his fighting skills. working with a cult run by ra's al-ghul (ken watanabe), he starts to take shape into becoming the dark knight.

returning to gotham city, wayne sees that things have gotten worse. with the help of alfred his butler (michael caine),luscious fox, an employee of wayne enterprises (morgan freeman)and the assistance of a policeman named gordon (gary oldman, playing a good guy for once), the legend of batman grows. however, with falcone and the scarecrow (cillian murphy)trying to run gotham city, it's not an easy task. plus, there is an unexpected wrinkle in the mix as well.

with the exception of katie holmes as wayne's childhood friend (and prosecuting attorney)rachel dawes, all of the performances are first rate (particularly oldman, with a bit of comedy relief). it is also interesting in seeing how the batcave and the batmobile had evolved (the batmobile looking like a huge atv). there is lots of action from start to finish, and a glimpse of things to come (particularly a playing card with a joker on it!). i am looking forward to what comes next.

after the very average batman movies of the 90s, "batman begins" is an awesome portrayal of the dark knight the way fans of the comic & graphic novels will appreciate.

the casting of batman begins is super (michael caine, morgan freeman)!! the dialogue is loaded with thought provoking pieces of philosophy. the action scenes are nail biting, yet not "campy" (in the sense that any cg special effects are hard to spot!).

even non-batman fans will love this movie. (my wife, who is not a batman fan, thought the film was better than star wars episode 3)! kudos to an awesome & long overdue batman film that takes the character & what he stands for seriously!!

directed by christopher nolan and starring christian bale, michael caine, liam neeson, katie holmes, gary oldman, cillian murphy, tom wilkinson, rutger hauer, ken watanabe and morgan freeman.

after witnessing his parents' murders, bruce wayne (christian bale) travels the world seeking the means to fight injustice. with the help of his trusted butler alfred (michael caine), detective jim gordon (gary oldman) and his ally lucius fox (morgan freeman), wayne returns to gotham and unleashes his alter-ego: batman, a masked crusader who uses strength, intellect and high-tech weaponry to fight evil.

this movie is brilliant! this movie has great acting, great storytelling and great characters.

without question this is the finest comic book movie ever made . i thought i would never say that after spider man 2 but here i am . christian bale was perfect . finally he portrays batman with emotion .in the previous movies keaton (great) and kilmer(so-so) were monotone and boring to watch at times . liam neeson was awesome and i hope they expand on the character of ra's al ghul throughout the next few movies as was done in the comic. (lazarus pit). cillian murphy was creepy as the scarecrow but should have been in it more . michael caine was the best alfred yet and morgan freeman was very cool as well . the plot was perfect and the mix of story and action was just right . if i have to make one complaint it would be that batman would stop revealing his identity to every leading lady, but hey that's hollywood . can't wait for the sequel . (adrian brody would make a perfect joker)

as a long time fan of batman i have longed to see a big screen batman that displayed the depth and power of the character i had come to enjoy while reading: batman: year one, batman: the dark knight returns, batman: the long halloween, batman: the killing joke.

i longed for a batman movie where batman was not overshadowed by the villains he fights. when i first heard about this movie i almost screamed in pain, expecting another joel schuemacher insult to batman. a movie that had more in common with the campy adam west series of the 60's then the character i had come to enjoy in the comic books.

walking in with no expectations i was blown away by what i saw. here was a movie that not only reached the dark, film noir levels of tim burton's original batman, but reached even farther. i could almost see flashes of frank miller in the script with i'm sure fans of batman: year one will recognize and enjoy.

i know some people don't like how the fight scenes were shot in this film, but i think they were perfect. you don't get to see all of batman's style, but it makes the fights seem more real. like you are there trying to follow a real fight between batman and the thugs of gothman's underworld. it heighten's the drama, and makes the movie seem less like just another hollywood action film with crisp easy to see fights. if there is a sequel i implore chris nolan to leave the fight scenes like he did in this movie.

batman begins is filled with great performance from michael caine, morgan freeman, liam nieson, and gary oldman. but not even that all-star supporting cast can steal the light from christian bale. as batman he delivers the sharp obessiveness that i had come to look for in batman. for that is the key in my mind to batman, bruce wayne died the night his parents died, and in the pain of that night batman was born.

the title of this comment is an actual line from the movie. bruce says it when alfred wakes him in the afternoon, the day after his first night out as a superhero. this is the kind of humor you can expect from the film. it sometimes appears in unexpected situations, which makes it that much better. the batman films can't really be classified as comedy, but they all had funny bits, and this one is no exception.

that said, the action is certainly not boring. we get to see the young bruce wayne in flashbacks and nightmares, and we get a better idea of why he became batman in the first place. then we see him training, occasionally getting his butt kicked, and learning how to navigate gotham city as a shadowy ninja-like crime fighter.

the actors all did very well, even katie holmes. that one surprised me a little. i'm no fan of hers, and i wasn't sure she belonged in a batman movie, but she pulled off her character pretty well. really, the female lead characters in the batman movies aren't there to be realistic, wonderful characters. they're there as a contrast to the city itself - gotham is huge, dark, gothic, and filled with crime and other horrors. each of the female leads embodied a different idealistic quality. the katie holmes character was the pretty assistant d.a. only interested in making sure justice was done in every situation. remember vicki vale? the kim basinger character was the intrepid reporter looking to write a fair and revealing story about batman, to show the world his true motivations. blah blah blah. they're secondary, important to the plot but ultimately forgettable, for the most part. katie holmes was no exception, and she did a decent job of it.

christian bale was absolutely the right choice for this batman. he has such a wide range of talents when it comes to acting, it's almost difficult to believe he's only one person. really, would anyone think the same actor could play the lead in a live-action disney musical about overworked children and one of the best incarnations of batman on screen? usually not, but there you go. he's funny in the right places, and he's able to convey a lot of emotion with his face and voice, a talent that is all too rare these days. also, his role as the psychotic patrick bateman in "american psycho" proved he's got the chops to play dark and demented. i've thought of batman that way since the early tim burton films, with michael keaton.

michael caine was the perfect alfred. he was able to show us how much the butler really loved the wayne family, and when the parents were killed he assumed the role of surrogate father to the grieving child left behind. caine was also good at conveying that sense of aristocratic attitude i saw in the older versions of alfred without going over the top.

i love morgan freeman, so i'm biased on this one. i love everything he does, including this role. lucius fox was every inch the eccentric inventor. he seemed like he was glad to see his creations finally put to good use. plus, he got to ride in the car, and he got to show batman how to use all the cool gadgets on the utility belt. great role, played by the right actor.

at first, i thought cillian murphy was the guy from eurotrip. i looked him up, and he isn't. while i can't quite remember what else i may have seen murphy in, it doesn't really matter. i loved him as scarecrow. it was interesting to me, to see what kind of villain scarecrow really was. no super powers at all, no mutations, no gadgets except the mask and the psychotropic drug he used to work his evil magic, but it worked. hey, batman doesn't have any powers either. he's got gadgets though, and lots of training. scarecrow has a background in psychiatry, drugs and a cool villain mask. and with these few tools he was able to bring gotham city to turmoil within the course of this almost two-and-a-half hour movie. the mark of a great villain is his ability to do a lot of evil with very little power or help. this guy is one of the greats.

really, there is no way to spoil this movie. i could sit here and type the script verbatim, and those who read it would still enjoy the movie. there would still be surprises, if only visual ones. it's worth the price of admission just to see what gotham city looks like in this film. and they managed to make it look real, like a city that might really exist somewhere out there.

that's the word for this film: real. batman is seen as a real guy, doing things other real people could do with the right training and enough money. scarecrow/dr. crane is a realistic - if slightly unbalanced - head shrinker who simply gets overly fascinated by the mind of the criminal psychotic. everything ties together in the end, and there is some good foreshadowing to get us hooked on the batman story until the end of time.

as fans of the batman series we have suffered through two lousy movies at best. the years of michael keaton had long passed us by and george clooney and val kilmer had shown us exactly what we did not want batman to be. today i can honestly say this has all changed. christian bale has rekindled a feeling for batman that most of us have not experienced since the days of micheal keaton. however, the credit for this outstanding movie does not only lay with christian bale. each and every person in this movie is what makes it so amazing. christian bale is to date the most believable batman we as fans have witnessed. katie holmes (who i personally do not favor) did a great job as she did not overact her part in this movie. morgan freeman was his usual self as he put on a great performance with what little screen time he had during this movie. the special effects were amazing as were the fight scenes. i realize that star wars and batman are two completely different arenas, but the fight scenes in batman put those in revenge of the sith to shame.

any true fan would realize that the bulk of the credit here should go to director christopher nolan. the man who brought us momento gives another great directory performance with his interpretation of batman. truth be told this is not a movie for young children. this is not a batman with a fake gotham city and toys that all kids would enjoy seeing. instead nolan gives us a world of reality, one that each and everyone of us can relate to. to me that is the greatest accomplishment of batman begins; the fact that we can watch as viewers and actually relate to the slums and downtrodden way of life this movie portrays.

if you are a fan of dark movies with amazing action sequences i suggest you take a chance on batman begins. it may be a long movie (with running time actually being over two hours) but it will not seem as if the movie is two hours long. the action mixed with the amazing acting will make you remember what batman was supposed to be: a dark yet driven person who would do anything possible to stop the plight that has hit gotham city.

i've always been a fan of the dark knight, but not always a fan of the way that he was portrayed in movies. christian bale does an amazing job at playing up batman's darker side and his dueling personality bruce wayne. bale is by far the best choice for a batman that there's ever been. michael caine, liam neeson, gary oldman and morgan freeman were also brilliant in their parts. this stellar cast really shines among a more than stellar movie.

another big plus about this batman movie was the cinematography. there were some very awe inspiring take your breath away moments in the movie where you could feel yourself being pulled in along side of the battles.

i would not however recommend this movie to the lighthearted who are expecting the 'cartoon' version. it's dark humor and personality are what makes it great. i will surely be seeing it again in theaters and owning it right away.

**** out of ****

if there ever was a movie which could be not only so original, it would be great, but also would make us forget the other prequel movies of it, that movie would definitely be batman begins. do you know when you watch a movie, and then you watch a sequel? even if the sequel is always supposed to be different, even though at almost many times, it becomes imitation of the original, you still see some resemblance of the two movies, like same styles, same scenarios or same ideas. maybe the sequel may evolve, maybe not. but batman begins is kinda different. not only it is a movie that actually evolved a lot from its other prequels, but also a totally unique and brand new movie where you will not see many (or none) resemblances because the film-making changed completely to make us see batman in a total different way.

in fact, when the movie ended and the credits begin to roll, i immediately told my friends that this is the first batman movie. there wasn't any batman movies before this one, this is the first. finally batman arrives at the big screen. for the first time ever. i know that this isn't true, but that's the feeling i had when i watched it. i don't know how the sequels will be (because if there is going to be three spider-man movies, why can't we have three batman movies?), but the first one surely was a great start for (we hope) a great trilogy.

as a friend of mine even said: "this movie remade the batman image completely." watch it and you'll agree right away. batman begins, nicely directed by christopher nolan, tells the story of the beginning of bruce wayne's life. how and why he became batman. this time, the bat-man is played by christian bale. i still think that michael keaton is the best, but bale was great too. at the party, the scene where bruce wayne says goodbye to his guests is one of the greatest proofs that bale plays bruce wayne very good! michael caine is good also as alfred (he never let me down in one of his performances), but still i find out that michael gough was much better, not only because of his performance, but because he really looked like alfred. the rest of the cast includes great actors, some of them, very unlikely to appear in a batman movie, but they did. cillian murphy, morgan freeman, rutger hauer, katie holmes, gary oldman and liam neesom. this last one is great as one of the villains.

overall, batman begins is the batman movie. even for those who are not fan of the comic books we'll sure to enjoy this movie, as in my country, many people really did. i just give a 9 out of 10, because i guess that sometimes, when you look at it, this movie looks like a crime movie. this happens because of the many sub-plots and because of the long-waiting for finally see bruce wayne in the batman costume. but getting past that scenes (which are not by any means, unnecessary, they're just the trigger to be pulled for us to see the rest of the movie), what happens next is of total delight.

i usually reserve judgment on movies until months after i've seen them in order to be able to properly reflect on how they compare with other movies...but in this case, it's safe to say that batman begins is the best superhero movie ever! this is the way the movie should have been done in 1989 (begin a franchise with the character's origin...what a concept!!!). let me also say that i've been an avid comic book collector for the past 25 years, to include batman. i never liked any of the first four batman films, although i gained an appreciation for the first batman after watching the horrendous "batman and robin" by joel schumacher. i also thought val kilmer did a good job as batman, despite the fact that he was burdened with a terrible script.

that said, christian bale's performance is the definitive bruce wayne/batman. the story draws you in immediately and makes you understand why bruce took his course of action in becoming batman (much more believable than anakin's transformation to darth vader). supporting cast is the best of any superhero movie...check out the interaction between bruce and alfred, bruce and lucius, batman and gordon, even bruce and rachel (i'm one of the few who didn't think katie holmes' performance was that bad). ra's al gould and the scarecrow are great villains who don't steal the show from the hero (as in previous batman films...actually making a batman film about batman--what a concept!!!) top off great acting, a great story, pulse- pounding action, and the best batmobile of the franchise, and you've got the best superhero movie ever (x-men 2 is a close second, followed by the spider-man films and superman i and ii). a must see, and one of those rare films i give a 10/10.

i kind of lost trust in hollywood when it came to batman films since they totally butchered "batman & robin." how could you go from tim burton's masterpiece in 1989's "batman" to that pathetic piece of crap "batman & robin"? so understandably so, i was apprehensive towards seeing this movie until i saw the extended trailer before "the longest yard." watching that trailer and finding out that such esteemed actors like christian bale, liam neeson, gary oldman, michael caine, and of course morgan freeman were in it, i actually felt compelled to see it out of excitement. and after watching it, i can safely say that "batman begins" is probably the best super hero movie i've seen.

aside from several absolutely amazing action sequences and virtuoso, scene stealing performances by morgan freeman and michael caine, i'd have to say that the best thing about the movie was the overall character development. you could actually feel the tension between liam neeson and christian bale. you could understand christian bale's resentment towards society and the justice system after the death of his parents. you could feel michael caine's fatherly love and affection for christian bale after the death of his parents. and you could feel the trust in gary oldman as gotham's last and only "good" cop.

all in all, batman begins sets a new bar as far as super hero movies are concerned. it has everything that the spiderman movies had, plus more. despite casting katie holmes, the only mistake made in the movie, it is without a doubt flawless when it comes to everything else. definitely a must-see for the batman enthusiast.

this film is a great throw back to tim burton's original, and in many ways surpasses it. here, gotham city is back to it's gothic atmosphere and thankfully, as far away from the campy nature of batman and robin.

the story of batman's origins makes for a prefect film. why this regular man, with no actual superpowers, becomes the dark knight is a great story. from the beginning, when bruce wayne is training with ducard, to his transformation into batman, the story is given a realistic edge to it that makes the characters all the more interesting. the reasons behind wayne's choice to become batman are made completely plausible through flash backs to his childhood. it's difficult to say more without ruining the plot, but it's actually a very interesting look at how fear can rule people's lives.

the action in the movie is reminiscent of the bourne identity, and earlier action flicks like speed. there are great car chases and fight scenes. one fight scene in particular has a horror movie edge to it. the action mixed with the interesting story make this an excellent film.

christian bale makes a great batman and a great bruce wayne, and not at all difficult on the eyes. i think he tops michael keaton and, since the film itself kind of rests on the shoulders of the actor playing batman, it speaks to how good bale is in that the movie is so good. gary oldman is fantastic as lieutenant gordon. it's nice to see him not play a psychopath . . . michael caine (alfred), morgan freeman (lucius fox), and liam neeson (ducard) also offer great performances. cillian murphy, who i have only previously seen in 28 days later - and who also auditioned for the role of batman, but ended up being cast as doctor crane/the scarecrow - proves that he is going to be an actor to watch for in the coming years.

the only person who falls short in this cast is katie holmes. she is by no means bad in the movie, but compared to the huge talent that surrounds her, she just can't quite compete. it's too bad that a better actress couldn't have been cast, but she is the only weak point of this film, and as i said, she's not even that bad.

so, i give this movie a 10 because batman has always been my favourite comic book hero and this film made the movie franchise great again. go see it!

i saw this movie on opening day and i must say i was very impressed by christopher nolan's version of the dark knight. the thing i liked about it is that it starts form the very beginning of the batman legend and dosen't do what the tim burton film does and already join bruce wayne after he becomes batman. this starts from the very beginning and takes you through the journey bruce takes to become batman. when the movies starts you see a young bruce wayne (probably about 9 or 10 years old)and you see his parents tom and martha wayne before they are shot. from there it pretty much goes in chronological order on how he becomes the bat. this story and look of this movie are taken more from frank millers graphic novels and the batsuit looks like it was inspired by paul dini and company(the new batman/superman adventures which later spawned the justice league series) and the supporting cast is just excellent in the roles that are given to them. katie holmes is brilliant as ada rachel dawes, cillian murphy is really creepy as dr. jonathan crane/scarecrow(by the end of the movie you really want to beat the crap out of him he is so evil and creepy) tom wilkinson plays and excellent mob boss in carmine falcone, gary oldman is probably the best choice for commissioner gordon(in this movie he starts as sargent gordan and is promoted to luteinet), micheal caine is a little bit better as alfred than micheal gogh was in the original batman movies because he has a little bit more wisdom for bruce and liam neeson does a bang up job as henri ducard because he is just so mysterious and when you see the movie you don't really trust him. morgan freeman also does a good job as lucius fox who is a trusted friend to the wayne family but one actor who shines more than the others is cristian bale as bruce wayne/batman he is better than micheal keaton was in the original because he portrays bruce as a darker person who needs to confront his fears before he can become what he is destined to be. and the plot is better than any of the plots in the original series. the plots in the original series were just the fact the villains wanted to take over gotham and run it to the ground but they had to get rid of batman first. the plot in this one is a little bit more sinister and requires a bit more work on the villains behalf but you will find out when you see the movie. all in all this is a really great movie and i recommend you see it twice because believe me it is worth every penny and i plan on seeing it a second time.

-spoiler alert read at own risk-

the best of the movie is the end when they set up a sequel with everyones favorite villain the clown prince of crime the joker

this is the best batman by far! focusing mainly on character development, director cnristopher nolan draws viewers into the most in-depth, accurate, and entrancing story of batman ever with a logical storyline and a cast full of hollywood's most distinguished actors, including morgan freeman, liam neeson and michael cain.

this is, by definition, the beginning of the great saga that is batman. bruce wayne (christian bale) is a man struggling to get through his adult life with the self-claimed guilt of his parents' murder on his hands and conscience. he eventually falls under the tutelage of ducard (neeson) and is trained in the arts of stealth, fear and harsh justice.

bruce wayne, upon return to gotham city, regains control of his mansion and his father's company. he sets up the bat cave on his property to be the batcave. at waynecorp, shoved into a secluded basement, is lucius fox, the man who supplies bruce with almost everything he needs for to be batman.

as batman, he strikes fear into the hearts of the criminals and villains who patrol and run gotham. these include my favorite villain from the batman cartoons (i don't remember him from the comics, but maybe i missed that one): scarecrow (cillian murphy). employed by ducard, scarecrow is dumping tons of a panic-inducing toxin into gotham's water supply and batman has to stop them from destroying civilization as they know it.

this is a perfect portrayal of the soul of batman. christian bale was flawless and i like how they finally got alfred away from being only a butler; michael cain plays more the role of a father figure than servant. i also love how 'real' this movie seemed. they made gotham very believable and it seemed as though the suit, the cape, the gadgets and even the batmobile could be logical products of present day reality.

when i heard that they where rebooting batman i was excited to see what it would be like, christain bale was awesome, liam neeson was fantastic, katy holmes was great, michael caine was outstanding for what all he was in it, as was morgan freeman, ken watanabe was greatly menacing for the little bit he was in, and cillian murphy was epically villainous, even rutger hauer stood out as an annoyingly mean guy, the only thing i didn't enjoy about this was how overly serious it was, its 140 mins. and almost all un comically. i recommend this film to lovers of intense action, and tales of heroism.

i give this film 9/10 *'s because it rocks.

having seen this film a 2nd time only confirms my initial take on it. this is an angry, ferocious, intelligent and thoroughly adult batman. however it is a warmer film the 2nd time around. when nolan was announced as the director to resurrect the bat a couple of years ago i was thrilled. i knew he wouldn't screw it up. let's face it the excellent memento and insomnia weren't exactly laugh riots. the thoughtfulness that made those films what they are make batman begins what it is. before we declare it the best film based on comic book character or story we must remember the crow. bale is perfect as bruce wayne/batman. he is brooding, tortured and deadly serious, but (like brandon lee as eric draven/the crow) there is a real soulfulness in his work. he and russell crowe (from the greatly under-appreciated cinderella man--the other great film of '05) dominate but never steal, the screen when they are on it. also i loved michael caine, liam neeson, gary oldham (refreshingly playing a good guy) and morgan freeman. there is not a single sour note in any work here and, yes, i think tom wilkinson as falcone does a fine job. this is a film for the mind and the eye. like cinderella man the riches here are very abundant. when i was 1st blown away by frank miller's revisionist batman in "the dark knight returns" (and it unfairly maligned sequel), batman begins was how i hoped batman would be translated to the big screen. batman returns came close (thanks to keaton, pfieffer and devito), but this bat even blows that one away. this film has as much frank miller in it (along with some alan moore) as miller's own sin city. batman begins is astonishing. note to christopher nolan and david goyer: if you can pull off an r-rating i loved to see "the killing joke".

i was 18 when i saw the first batman movie. i won free tickets to the sneak-preview showing late on a weeknight. the theater was packed to the walls and everyone must have been as big a fan as me because we all ooo'd and aaah'd, cursed, laughed and whooped at all the same places. the experience was so unique to me that i felt a little of it every time i wore one of my batman t-shirts or hats for years afterwards.

at the time, i was sure that was the best comic-book hero movie that could ever be made. this feeling was reinforced after the other batman movies were released. sure, they were ok and it was cool to watch a character you love go through new adventures, but the movies were not as good overall.

i have to say that batman begins certainly has given me a new perspective. i still have a high opinion of the 1989 flick, but this movie rocks. it made bruce much more human, and in my opinion, much more likable. i was surprised how much i liked bale as batman.

the focus of this movie is, obviously, how bruce got started in the role of thug-busting. turns out he spent some time in an asian prison, hooked up with a bunch of ninjas that were led by a tag-team of ol' rob roy / qui-gon jinn and the next-to-last-samurai. this film had an awesome and very impressive list of cast members.

morgan freeman shows up as a wayne inc version of "q" -- let's call him "w" -- who really knows how to hook a fella up. full body armor, magneto-cable-guns, electro-memory cloth (used to turn batman's cape into a glider -- how cool is that!?) and (the best for last) the tumbler, aka batmobile.

christopher nolan brings batman to life with the origin story which had never really been told in on screen. spending time visiting the cave, where adam west and burt ward raced out of, from the 60s tv show, nolan and david s goyer knew they had to return to the roots of what made batman. what's interesting about this film is how much anticipation is created whilst the audience awaits batmans first appearance. with great storytelling we are invested into bruce wayne as much as we are batman. the suspense is so thrilling even before he puts on the cape and cowl. with different beliefs to his mentor and the league of shadows bruce wayne sets out to find his own purpose. along with the amazing composing of hans zimmer and james newton howard we feel the fear and emotional pain of bruce losing his parents. henri ducard becomes a new father like figure to bruce and trains bruce in martial arts whilst he has left gotham. this film has outstanding sequences and great cinematography. batman is seen in flashes at first like a horror movie creating fear in the eyes of his opponents. comparing it with modern super hero movies there is a lot more genuine solidility with cgi only being used when it is absolutely necessary. from being filmed on location, to epic full scale narrows and batcaves being built, which is the foundations of this standing out among the rest. one of the most authentic comic book movies ever made. whilst being a big james bond fan nolan even adapted to incorporating lucus fox into the mix as your gadgets man. using state of the art army like gadgets almost everything you see in the movie can be done. with a variety of quality actors from gary oldman, christian bale, michael caine and liam neeson this truely is a movie to bring a comic book film to life at its highest level. a nice twist along the way, for me batman begins is not only the best batman movie to date but also the pinnacle of all comic book movies. where it all does truely begin.

i think that the first iteration of batman i ever saw was the adam west tv series. you know, the one with nonchanging story lines, joker with a painted-over mustache, bat shark repellant, and "na-na-na-na- na batman" theme. boy, have we come a long way since then. christopher nolan revolutionized the character. tim burton's version had already brought back the dark shadows, the heavy themes of duality and fighting enemies of your own making, the brooding and the melancholy. but nolan took all that and updated it to the modern day. suddenly it felt surprisingly plausible that someone might make the choice to fight crime dressed as a giant bat.

this is also one of the first films in ages to show as the origin of batman. i mean, we all know the story. bruce wayne is the golden son of gotham, but then his parents get killed in a random mugging and once he grows up he takes up the moniker of batman to strike fear into the hearts of those that have terrified him so much. but we usually start long after he has become batman. and the question often remains: where did the learn all that? sure, he's wealthy beyond belief so getting all kinds of gadgets is certainly possible, but you don't really learn to fight like he does without some form of training. and in this movie we get to see that training. and it is very entertaining and makes for a great cinematic experience, especially with nolan directing. his nonlinear storytelling and visual style compliment the story perfectly and once bruce wayne begins his war against crime, he gives us a great version of one of the best villains batman has ever had.

it's also a well-acted film with christian bale stepping into the boots of bruce wayne and batman. i do think that he is a bit better bruce wayne than he is batman and this is definitely the film where he gets to be bruce wayne the most, but his batman isn't all that bad by any means. even the infamous voice isn't as bad as people make it out to be, especially in this first film. and the supporting cast is equally great, with michael caine and morgan freeman giving us their absolutely a-game as alfred and lucius fox, respectively. not to mention gary oldman as commissioner gordon, though his best moments are still ahead in the next film.

batman begins is one of my favourite superhero films and one of my all-time favourites in general as well. definitely my go-to example on how to tell an origin story. check it out if you haven't already.
