batman begins marks the 5th attempt at bringing the dark knight to the big screen. after the last two camp filled monstrosities (part 2 wasn't that great either), i was a bit hesitant about this one. needless to say, i walked out of the theatre in shock and awe at how well the film was done. as roger ebert said, this is the batman film i never knew i was waiting for.

a young bruce wayne witnesses the murder of his parents. he then sets out to understand the nature of criminality and the criminal mind. years later, he is a prisoner in an unnamed asian country, where he has nightmares about his childhood fear of bats where he meets a man named ducard who takes him to the doorstep of ras al-ghul. from this point on, bruce trains to become a "symbol" that fights those who prey on the fearful.

christopher nolan and david goyer's setup was brilliant, since this is undoubtedly the only batman film that actually does batman justice. the writers went above and beyond to make sure the story was believable. the inclusion of the luscious fox character (played by morgan freeman) adds to the believability of the batman story. bruce wayne needs an array of gadgets and automobiles to fight crime, all of which were developed by wayne's own company. the design for the batsuit is that of a suit that was designed for warfare. this is only fitting since wayne declares a one man war on crime in gotham city. batman as a character was never supposed to offer the escapist, fantasy elements that spider-man or superman offered. most of the single entity superhero titles out there try and sell themselves on big explosions, heat vision, and big webs. in other words, the others make their money from the cheap thrills that are offered from the very nature of the character. batman is just a guy sworn to fight crime; a guy who pushed his body and mind to the limits of human capability. they don't call him the world's greatest detective for nothing. from this stand point, batman is more about the thick, complex plot structure and the deep, complicated, and usually dark take on each and every character (not to say the film doesn't offer any action). this is what makes batman "the thinking man's" super hero, not to mention knowing that any guy walking the street could be batman if he was driven enough.

christian bale's dark and brooding performance only adds to the gritty realism of the story. bale truly captures the three sides to the coin; the public bruce wayne, the private bruce wayne, and the beast that is batman. bale's physical appearance just makes his performance that much better. one half is the filthy rich, billionaire playboy. the other half is a man who spends his nights jumping off rooftops and fighting thugs by the dozens. alfred's relationship with bruce does add that more humanistic touch to the film, and michael cain does a great job of showing how alfred acted as a real father figure for bruce as he grew up.

the only real downside is the presence of katie holmes. she just doesn't look her part. after wayne comes back from the years spent traveling the world and fighting crime, rachel is supposed to be near thirty, yet she still looks fifteen. i personally would have liked an even darker approach to the camera work. the images of batman standing, hiding, or jumping out of the shadows with fog and lightning ripping through the screen would've been a real treat. but looking back on it, the film was supposed to be real and it is real, that's why it works.

i'm already looking forward to the sequel. go watch this one, now!

enter the world of batman, or rather, christopher nolan's batman. the genius behind "memento" has taken an unexpected turn in his film career by directing a movie franchise that was previously shot down with titles including "batman forever" and the dreadful "batman and robin". it would take an immense amount of work to revive the franchise and to rid the audience of the image cast on them through previous batman films.

nolan does just that. completely rebooting the franchise from scratch, he tells the story of batmans origins; what drove a billionaire heir to his fathers throne from riches to becoming his city's greatest protector. nolan immerses the audience into emotional depth by telling the story that had yet to have been told. in previous incarnations of batman, the villains are the interesting characters. their stories are told. this film is different. batman begins tells the story of bruce wayne.

nolan's version is one that was never thought of. who knew that all a batman movie needed was more character depth and less action and special gadgets? though this movie focuses less on the action, the action that is in it is intense. the fight scenes are incredibly realistic and not special dancing that are seen in kung fu movies. gadgets used by batman are not only conceivable but current experimental technology.

one question i always had about batman since i was a kid was "why would someone who wants to fight crime just wear a bat costume?" although batman comics and the batman: mask of the phantasm addresses this issue, begins takes it into a new level and makes it to the point where it's no longer a mystery as to why bats, but it's point blank obvious as to why he chose bats. "bats frighten me. it's time my enemies share my dread." an exceptional cast makes the story all the more compelling and epic. liam neeson, michael caine, morgan freeman, gary oldman, cilian murphy, ken watanbe and (of course last but no where near the least) christian bale act with great conviction and devotion, creating the emotional feel for their characters.

the twists and turns in the movie leave the audience surprised and amazed. the choice of telling the story in a non linear fashion was perfect. the movie is without competition in it's franchise.

superhero movies have finally grown up. batman begins deserves every bit of praise it gets.

for the last eight years, all of the die hard fans of dc comics, and in particular, the long-suffering fans of the most mortal superhero of our time, the batman, have watched in agony as comic book films reign triumphant at the box office, almost all of them with the marvel logo attached. the x-men films, the spider-man films, the blade trilogy, and a few others are an example of their success.

meanwhile, the dc fans have writhed in pain as the last time they could remember their caped crusader was when he wore a nipple clad suit and fought the governor of california in one of the worst movies ever made, batman and robin.

the dc fans went into exile, hoping, praying that one day their real hero would return them the way he was meant to.

on june 15, 2005, the day finally came. the batman came back to cast his shadow on comic book cinema.

more importantly, from the moment the brand new dc comics logo appeared before the movie, dc comics finally sent the message they have wanted to send for some time: we are back.

batman begins is a film that for the first time ever tells the story of how bruce wayne became the batman, the dark knight of justice against evil in gotham city. instead of focusing on the villains of the film and how they rose to power, this movie, in a formula similar to spider-man, tells how batman was created, and finally gives his character the depth that he deserves.

the story follows bruce wayne's life from the moment his parents died, through his teen years as he dealt with the loss, to the point where he realizes his ultimate vision of becoming gotham city's symbol of justice, and the best part is that everything is explained.

when you watch this movie, you know why he is batman and you know how he is batman. he is never simply a crazed vigilante in a bat suit scaring people. his methods are logical and realistic and for the first time, you understand why he does what he does.

the story is excellently crafted by david s. goyer, who is capable of making masterpieces as long as he is paired with the right director, who in this case is christopher nolan, the genius behind memento, following, and insomnia. at no point did this story seem too campy or unrealistic and at no point did it fail to draw in the viewer. everything is clearly presented and highly engrossing.

the cast is excellent from top to bottom, even at its weakest link with katie holmes playing assistant d.a. rachel dawes. christian bale, in what might be his strongest role yet, is the perfect age and personality for the playboy of bruce wayne and more importantly, he makes you believe that he is the dark, frighteningly vengeful batman, with a voice and personality that scares everybody, good or bad.

michael caine is the perfect alfred pennyworth, the consort and friend of bruce wayne, morgan freeman is sharp and resourceful as lucius fox, the wayne enterprises executive with all of the wonderful toys, and gary oldman, after years of playing the bad guy in so many films, once again displays his versatility by bringing jim gordon to life, something that none of the other four films ever did.

the villains do not take away from the attention paid to batman and they do not dominate the story. they are there to do what they do, which is cause trouble and put a face on who the batman fights. tom wilkinson, cilian murphy, ken watanabe and liam neeson are strong antagonists in this respect, doing only what they are supposed to be doing and not going over the top with their performances.

in addition, for the first time ever on film, gotham city is gotham city, a true comic book metropolis brought to life, displaying its true to life cityscapes while also showing its dark grittiness.

for awhile i always believed that the best incarnation of batman was the 85 episodes of the animated series that appeared on fox from 1992-1995. now, with this new movie, the batman looks better than he ever did. warner bros. and dc comics looks as though they are finally ready to make amends for the past transgressions of the batman franchise after seeing how attention to detail, depth and accuracy have benefited the marvel movies in their success.

in the top ten list of best comic book movies of all-time, batman begins sits proudly at the #2 spot, with only spider-man 2 slightly ahead of it at #1. my hope and faith for this franchise has been more than restored, and i now look forward to seeing the future films in this new batman franchise, as well as the highly touted superman returns, and v for vendetta, which will be in theaters next year.

rejoice, all of you long suffering dc comics fans. our wait has ended. the monopoly of marvel is coming to an end. the batman is finally here, superman is coming back soon, and there will be others to follow. dc comics strikes back!!!

i have fond memories of tim burton's first batman picture. i saw it when i was 9 and loved it to death but like many movies i loved during my childhood it just simply hasn't aged well. it's shallow, cheesy, and with the exception of a completely over the top performance by way of jack nicholsan has little to remember in the acting department. after the initial picture the franchise plummeted into movie hell with three sequels that are some of the worst movies ever created. this franchise was in desperate need of a reboots.

well here it is ladies and gents. batman begins is quite simply one of the best comic book movies ever made. why is that you may ask; well it's because while respecting it's roots it realizes that films aren't comics and grounds the story pretty firmly in what could be reality. finally you can believe that most of this stuff is actually happening. christian bale is hands down the best batman/bruce ever put to screen and thanks to the screenwriters he is given lots to work with. finally batman's motivations for becoming the bat are fleshed out beyond the sorry joker killed my parents excuse. he is a fully realized character and christian bale delivers one of his best performances yet.

michael cain is also excellent as the loyal butler alfred. cain delivers a warmth and sincerity that the obvious alfred lacked. again he is serviced by some great writing and he runs with it. cillian murphy as scarecrow was a genuine surprise. the only thing i've seen him in was 28 days later and i wasn't prepared for how good he'd be. liam neeson has never given a bad performance and he doesn't fail us now. his character is simply one of the best villains i've seen in a comic movie. the other cast are equally excellent though they don't have much screen time. morgan freeman and gary oldman are quite good as the q-like scientist and innocent police officer respectively. kattie holmes didn't annoy me nearly as much as i thought she would, in fact she was actually pretty good and i believed in her feelings for bruce.

the one weakness this movie has is the quick cut actions scenes. some of them are fine but most of them are cut so quick in such dark scenes that it make it really hard to tell what's happening. this is really a small complaint for me because i prefer a great story over action scenes any day and boy did this movie deliver. i will draw this review to a close by saying that this is the best movie so far in 2005 and it will most likely be at the top of my top 10 end of the year list.

10outof10

it occurs to me that we never really learned the batman legend before. we never learned anything from "batman & robin" for those that unfortunately remember the film but there has never been a solid backstory about him until now. director christopher nolan creates a dark and fun filled adventure of the caped crusader that penetrates his deepest fears and shows us that he is not only just a vigilante but a real human who is vulnerable.

it's about a young child, bruce wayne (gus lewis) who loses his parents, thomas (linus roache) and martha (sara stewart) one night and bruce is taken in and raised by his butler, alfred pennyworth (michael caine). 14 years later, bruce (christian bale), is still devastated by the loss of his parents and plans to take the law into his own hands when the justice system fails. his childhood friend, rachel daws (katie holmes) berates him for thinking of such an act so bruce decides to travel the world in an attempt to overcome his fear and learn how to confront justice. after training with, henri ducard (liam neeson) and facing his fears, he returns to gotham determined to stop the crime as a caper vigilante called batman.

christian bale steps into the suit and is, arguably, the best batman to date. it opens in a prison camp where bruce is a prisoner enduring punishment as part of his journey into seeing evil for what it really is. he is rescued by henri ducard and he becomes bruce's mentor. he teaches him how to sword-fight and how to control himself in the face of danger. things go sour when wayne refuses to kill someone as a requirement for membership and ducard becomes his enemy. wayne returns to gotham city and sets his sights on carmine falcone (tom wilkinson ), a mafia boss who controls the city.

christopher nolan gives us every aspect of the bruce wayne story. we learn his fear of bats (childhood accident) and his hatred of criminals (his parent's murders) are the reason for his journey but also discovering himself and learning to face his true destiny. his family owns wayne corp. and is run by a seedy figure, william earle played by rutger hauer, who was in the meaningless and disgusting shocker called "the hitcher." he fits right in with this character. morgan freeman plays luscious fox, scientific genius, and wayne's weapons handler who gives him the tools he needs. he gives batman the batmobile and it's a juggernaut on wheels. batman's suit also has some nice upgrades as well. gary oldmen steps into the role of lt. gordon who will quickly discover batman is here to do good. in the middle of everything, wayne is torn between a love he has for rachel dawes and also keeping his identity a secret.

when wayne puts on the suit and becomes batman, the action starts and it doesn't stop. now, the plot could take a simple detour and give us some story where batman beats everyone up, finds the villain and saves the day like we have seen before but it doesn't. batman has a motive and he knows what he needs to do. when he is revealed in the second act, there is a sense of fear and darkness looming over the character that we become anxious to see what he is going to do. the main villain of the film is the scarecrow and his zany scheme spells psychotic trouble. he is played by cillian murphy and does a bang up job as a menacing presence for batman to face. he plans to poison the town's water supply and drive everyone mad. this will prove to be a challenge for batman because scarecrow is not the only person he must face. a familiar enemy in his past might come back to haunt him.

i was a little nervous when i heard they were rebooting the series. i wasn't a fan of the last four films. michael keaton was a fun batman. jack nicholson lost me when he looked like a clown from the 1966 "batman" and tommy lee jones didn't do it for me as two-face but this picture shines and finally gives us everything we want to know about batman. the special effects add a monorail in the climax of the film to keep the intensity going and it's a roller-coaster ride you can't look away from. it's clear that christopher nolan has a vision in mind for batman and i'm fine with that. i finally got the batman movie i always wanted to see and you will enjoy it. katie holmes is fantastic at batman's love interest and i hope to see more of her with the next one. i'm very excited to see what is going to happen next.

this is by far the best batman movie yet. i think the director must've been a true batman fan as a kid, because the version of batman portrayed in this movie comes closest to what i felt as i read the batman comics of my childhood (40 years ago - sigh). this batman is one bad-ass dude. one thing that made batman so dear to my brother and me was that, unlike his fellow cohorts of the justice league of america, batman had no "special" powers other than those of human genius and strength (along with a seemingly infinite supply of money), and yet was second only to superman in abilities (and he even topped superman in problems of logic and shear "sleuthdom"). we always figured that batman had to be more than just some angry super-rich guy, because that wouldn't have held up in the company of people like superman and the green lantern. batman was a very unique human - the type that comes along only once-in-a-billion times (or less). this movie gives a believable story as to how such a rare individual could come to be.

christian bale is excellent as batman/bruce wayne. finally, not some fop in a mask, but a truly complex character who can be genuinely frightening at times - the only way some guy jumping off of rooftops in tights would be able to maintain any sort of street cred! also, michael caine is the perfect alfred - of course.

i really liked the creation of lucius fox (expertly handled by morgan freeman) - batman needs a scientist/engineer as part of his "support team." i don't know why dc comics never figured this out (at least they hadn't 40 years ago...).

the actors (esp. liam neeson and cillian murphy) portraying villains are just as good at being bad guys as the actors playing heroes are at playing good guys.

this is a movie based on a child fantasy, and so some willing suspension of disbelief on the part of an adult audience is needed. however, never before has a batman movie made this so easy to do.

batman begins is inception director christopher nolan's reboot of the famous batman film franchise based on the dc comics superhero. tim burton and joel schumacher had both had their time in the batman films, and chris nolan brings a completely new feel to it, concentrating on elements such as fear and delivering quite a dark, psychological film. it stars christian bale as bruce wayne/batman, liam neeson, cillian murphy, katie holmes, gary oldman, michael caine, morgan freeman, tom wilkinson and ken watanabe. the film starts by explaining bruce's fear of bats and then travelling to bhutan after his parents death and being trained as a ninja by liam neeson's henri ducard. ducard teaches wayne to master his fear and become more than just a man, saying that if he makes himself more than a man, committing himself to an idea, he will become an immortal legend. bruce returns to the crime-struck and corrupt gotham where he transforms himself into the double personality batman, the caped crusader, to fight crime. he does this with the help of alfred, his butler played by caine who is like his father. also assisting him is sergeant gordon (oldman), one of the few cops who is not corrupt, freeman's lucius fox, who provides bruce with his equipment and childhood friend, now da, rachel (holmes). wilkinson plays crime lord falcone and murphy plays dr jonathan crane, the fear-inducing scarecrow. this film is fantastic in every aspect, with great acting, great action scene, an interesting plot and good themes. hans zimmer and james newton howard's score is amazing, one of the best film scores of all time and christopher nolan does a superb job of directing. the only minor problem i had with it was that the scarecrow seemed to be underused, and it sometimes starts to feel a little rushed in places. however, batman begins is a brilliant movie and the sequel, the dark knight, takes things to a whole new level. it is an epic start to a trilogy.

i have to be honest with you. i'm biased. i love batman.

as a kid i was a comic book person (although not a fan-boy), and i always enjoyed batman, whether as a campy 60s tv hero, or in the gritty 80s comic books. i was 14 the summer of 1989 when tim burton's "batman" came out. it blew my pubescent little mind. i saw it several times, and ate it up like it was fresh popcorn.

"batman begins" tops it. that's sacrilege to a lot of people, and understandably so. but "begins" is above and beyond the best batman film.

one of its strengths is that it seems to take cues from "spider-man": tell a fluid, sensible story, explain the origins of the character, but spend most of the screen time exploring the relationships among the primary characters. and in a way, "begins" is like a dark counterpart to the spider-man story.

but while "spider-man", with its splashy colors and frequent cgi, does a better job of making a comic book into a movie, "batman begins" succeeds in being the better film, creating a realistic world in which a bat-man, an ordinary man with no supernatural powers, could actually exist.

for example: there's a helicopter shot that sweeps over gotham city about half way through the film, in which batman is shown standing atop a tower overlooking the gotham skylineand i got chills. it's that effective. as far as i can tell, it's just a stuntman in a batsuit perched over a slightly-modified chicago, but that simple shot absolutely conveys that "this could be real; this *could* really happen". and $100 million of cgi cannot buy those chills.

and that's another of the film's strengths: throughout the movie either it uses sets and models instead of cgi, or it uses cgi so properly (that is, sparingly) and so seamlessly that everything actually looks *real*. i hate to bash george lucas when everyone else already has, but he spent countless millions making movies starring a yoda *you can't touch* when he had a perfectly tried-and-true puppet that has depth and weight and texture (not to mention an actor's---frank oz's---actual *performance*). with "batman begins", it's the other way around: this is a batman that is so realistic that he threatens to reach out and touch *you*.

yet another strength: stellar casting. christian bale is a terrific batman, hands down. sure, there will always be debate among fans as to who's the better batman, who's the better bruce wayne, etc. again, i'm biased; i love adam west. and i honestly think that every batman actor has been good in his own way, even if the particular film he was in happened to suck. but bale has both bruce and batman down in a way that is, i believe, most faithful to the true spirit of dichotomy in the character.

oddly enough, with the exception of morgan freeman, the male cast is made up entirely of brits, and they all shine. of course, when do gary oldman and tom wilkinson not? and liam neesonboy, i hate to kick lucas again, but *this* is what qui-gon jinn should have been. neeson's character is multi-layered, powerful, and compelling. take his ducard character, add morals and a few jedi mind tricks, and you'd have an excellent qui-gon. his success in this movie makes it even *more* evident what a lost opportunity "episode i" was.

my only gripe is the music. hans zimmer is a fine composer, but epic characters in epic situations deserve epic *themes*! maybe danny elfman would have been wrong for the tone of this film (although i think nothe worked in "spider-man", didn't he?), but what about williams? glass? even horner when he's in "star trek ii" mode? the music is background material in a movie that needs it to be textured for certain scenes, and thundering horns for others.

but that's the only thing that really bothers me, and even that's minor. the tone is perfect. the direction is excellent. the production design is not as immediately engrossing as that of the '89 "batman", but great nonetheless. everything that batman has, from his belt to his cape to his cowl, seems real and imminently touchable. to me, that's indispensable.

the script, while not flawless, is tight and kinetic, keeping me guessing while watching a story i already *knew*. and far from being as humorless as a few critics (notably gene shalit) have said, there are many lines that crackle with dry wit, adequately balancing---but not neutralizing---the tension the director creates.

but the triumph of the film, i believe, is in the complexity of its relationships. in the comics, alfred is not a doddering old queen (as in the films until now) but a superlative (if sometimes unwilling) partner, patching up all of batman's wounds and supporting him in both of his personae. this is reflected in "begins". in the comics, jim gordon is not a bumbling, overweight, gambling, nearly clueless police commissioner (as in the films until now), but a trusted adviser to batman, and, above all, an excellent police officer. this, too, is reflected in "begins".

my only regret is that "batman begins" will not be the cultural phenomenon of burton's '89 "batman". it hasn't been promoted as well, and it simply doesn't have the advantage of burton's film, which came out at a time when the superhero film was thought to be dead. now, because the spider-man and x-men movies are so good (and hopefully, the upcoming "superman" will be as well), it's simply *expected* that a new batman film be good, and when it *is* as good as "begins", it doesn't cause as much of a commotion.

i can only hope that this film is financially successful, and that i can spend future summers escaping the heat by watching batman---*good* batman---and eating it up like it's fresh popcorn.

i am writing this review as just having been one of the first of 200 audience members in the entire state of arizona to have viewed batman begins at an imax theater.

let me start off this review by saying, that i have been following this movie for nearly 2 years, since i first heard it was in production, and have been just as eagerly been waiting for it then, as i was 20 minutes before it began.

now then. this movie, redefines batman as a badass. no more pussyfooting batman of old, no more "chicks dig the car." b.s, this movie was explosive, when batman punched someone, the audience could feel it, it wasn't just a punch, but a punch and when you see this movie, you will understand what i am talking about. batman faces off against 2 villains in this film, ra's al ghul, and the scarecrow, suffice to say, fans of the comic book series, will not be disappointed in these villains, without giving anything away, i can't say anything further without spoiling anything. this movie follows the basic outline of the "batman, year one" series, and you never see the bat-suit, until 45 minutes into the film. in those first 45 minutes you'll be taken to many different vast, and grand locations. and when we first really see the city of gotham, it looks like an actual plausible city, not like some gothic cathedral was vomited all over new york, but an actual plausible city.

very little digital effects were used in this film (if any) and those that may have been used, i could not tell. now, my main concern with this movie was the tumbler, i.e the new batmobile. it looks bulky and cheap. but when you see this thing in action, you can definitely tell it's a batmobile bruce will eventually twist and mold into the batmobile we know and love by movie 2. (please god, let there be a sequel, and let it be directed by nolan) but, i will admit, like every movie, it has its flaws, i felt some of the humor wasn't particularly needed (don't worry its not cheesy like the last 2) but to me i felt a few comedic relief lines didn't need to really be there. i would have also liked more scenes of the underground, to really see the poverty of gotham, but some may argue there was too much of that, really it just comes down to personal taste.

anyways, to wrap this up, great visuals without ******** cgi everywhere like directors are so darned fond of doing anymore, tip top acting (bale, caine, neeson, freeman, how can you go wrong?) my rating? 5/5 stars.

batman begins is a great comic book film that brought batman back to the dark and brooding character he was. at first when i heard that warner brothers was making a new,rebooted batman film i was not to excited mainly because i loved tim burton's batman films and i thought the series should not be relaunched. but after joel shumacher's campy and candy colored films batman forever(which is not that bad)and batman & robin(no comment on that film)batman and the batman series was saved an rebooted by christopher nolan with batman begins and with this film gave us a great start to the dark knight trilogy. what separates this film from other batman films is that bb shows how bruce wayne became batman and the complexity of the character bruce wayne. nolan's film shows viewers how bruce wayne became batman with years of training and building up to becoming a crime fighter with weapons,fighting skills and striking fear in the hearts of the criminals who roam the streets of gotham city. bruce trains as batman in not only the physical and fighting advantage but also the mental advantage by using the dark and shadows. nolan also shows bruce wayne trying to balance out being batman and billionaire bruce wayne and showing that while wayne is grown up is still affected by the murders of his parents. bb also shows viewers trying to form and reform relationships because of bruce's i just returned from the midnight pre-screening of batman begins (2005) at my local theater, and the adrenaline is *still* coursing through my veins!! what a rush!!

to start, let me say that about three weeks ago, i rented batman (1989), and let me tell ya, that film is fatally flawedi'm not even sure it qualifies as a film. to me, it was like watching a comic book in real time, and while i can see the appeal of this for some of the fans of the comic books, this will not suffice when making a film.

now, that being said, batman begins (2005) is as close as you can get to a perfect film acquiring its source material from a comic book, and *this* coming from a huge fan of both the spider-man and x-men movies. granted, i love those movies and their some of my all- time favorites, but they're not even on the same playing field as this!

not knowing anything of the comic series other that it exists, this is *exactly* what i desired to see when i first saw batman (1989). and unlike that film, this movie does not intend to put on a show, but succeeds in making you *feel* the story. bruce wayne is incredibly well- written, and it's especially insightful to see flashbacks of when he was a boy.

the wry, sardonic humor is well-suited for the film, lucratively enhancing its dark atmosphere. the crowded theater housing 250 movie-loving citizens laughed simultaneously throughout the entire course of the film. the director expertly articulates his tightly-wound vision, compelling a film full of depth and personality to the big screen. christian bale was eloquent in manifesting a dark, wounded batmani don't believe anyone else could've done better. through the course of the film, i truly believed in batmanthat he was real and existedthat's how impressive his performance is. it was great to see liam neeson in another role, and he does well with the scant material he's given. morgan freeman and katie holmes fill out exceptional supporting roles, both portraying their respective characters so well, you really get a sense of who they are.

even though most of us have seen four batman movies, this film stands alone because despite that, you truly feel as if you're experiencing everything for the first time, as if the material's new and fresh, and this is primarily because it is so perfectly presented in this manner. from his first encounter with bats and how they've become a sort of demon he must continually exercise, his father's contributions to gotham city, his family history and associations, the source of the one-of-a-kind weaponryeverything is just so thoroughly intriguing and enlightening in a way that you can't quite put your finger on. we learn not only why he is who he is, but how. by the end, i left feeling oddly inspired and almost on a high of sortsit was strange and yet refreshing in a way that i've never felt before.

verdict: thoroughly engrossing and executed with precision and stylea milestone amongst all predecessors. highly recommended to all, whether you read the comics or not, whether you saw the originals or not, and even whether you like batman or not. set aside any and all notions you have, and do yourself a favor and go see this onei promise you won't be disappointed. this is not just a movieit's an experience.

"batman begins" is a movie about bruce wayne's early years and how he became the dark knight. there is an all-star cast which includes christian bale, michael cain, liam neeson, katie holmes, gary oldman, cillian murphy, and morgan freeman. as a young boy, bruce wayne watched in horror as his parents were gunned down right in front of his eyes. then bruce becomes obsessed with revenge, but his chance at revenge is taken away by fate. bruce then flees to the east and seeks the counsel of dangerous but noble ninja cult leader ra's al-ghul. bruce then returns to the now decaying gotham city, which is overrun by organized crime. meanwhile, wayne industries is slowly slipping through his fingers. bruce then sets his plan in motion to help gotham city. with the rediscovery of the cave under his family's estate and a prototype armored suit, bruce becomes batman!

i liked this movie very much because it's not like your typical comic book movie. this movie shows that maybe, just maybe, this could happen in real life.

christian bale gives a great performance as batman, not as good as michael keaton in the original "batman" but very believable. the rest of the cast is amazing in their roles; michael cain is terrific as alfred.

overall i give it 3 out of 4 stars.

batman begins was the without a doubt the perfect start to a great trilogy. i absolutely love the cast choices for each character. i love the origin story for bruce on his road to being batman. the way we saw him grow from being bruce wayne to batman was done beautifully. the way we saw him trained by ras al ghoul was a great way to see him learn the skills needed to be batman. christian bale playing batman was done better than i have ever seen anyone else as batman, liam neeson as ras al ghoul was done beautifully, michael caine is the perfect choice for alfred, gary oldman was fantastic as gordon, and morgan freeman as lucius fox is amazing. personally, i don't think they need to do the origin story again, because this movie did it to the point that it doesn't need to be done again.

i have to first admit that i avoided this movie. after experiencing the utter disappointment that was batman forever (adequate, but flawed) and batman and robin (just plain awful), despite the wonderful christopher nolan at the director's helm and gifted actor christian bale in the suit, the sentiment shared by many batman fans that what would come out of this film would be more regret was shared heavily by myself. how could i be so wrong? firstly, this movie is not a sequel or a prequel - nolan has created a new batman franchise which (arguably) betters burton's. gone are the campy villains, neon backgrounds and bat nipples. in their place are multi-layered, wonderfully acted villains, a dark, brooding gotham so reminiscent of the early batman comics, and a batman actually able to kick butt and look convincing while doing it.

the movie is wonderfully scripted and plotted. the initial scenes which describe to the viewer bruce wayne's adult fascination with bats - and the reason for his lifelong quest for justice - are done in such a way that you actually don't question how a grown, normal man could fight crime in a bat suit. the rest of the movie becomes more complex as it goes along, while still retaining several moment of humor that don't seem too forced or too campy - though i'll leave it for you to discover for yourself.

the casting is brilliant. christian bale has already proved himself as a quality actor in such films as american psycho and the machinist, and he did not disappoint in batman begins. as the quissential comic book love interest, katie holmes as assistant district attorney rachel dawes has little to do, though she does give a surprisingly spirited and engaging performance. supporting actors liam neeson, ken wantanabe, morgan freeman and michael caine are all icing on a delicious cake.

the real find in this movie, however, has to be cillian murphy, who plays dr. jonathan crane, aka the scarecrow. his performance is mind-blowingly articulate and at the same time chilling from the first moment you lay eyes on him in a courthouse. as much as i hate to use clichés such as this, murphy is truly a face to watch.

what else can i say? nolan, goyer ... thank you, from the bottom of this batman fan's heart. 10/10.

following the works of tim burton and joel schumacher, christopher nolan presents a new and improved batman movie more heavily grounded in reality (or about as real as a comic-book hero film can be), and with a strong emphasis on in-depth storytelling and style.

despite the emphasis on character development and drama, the film is entertaining. it might even be more entertaining than all the other films before it. action is frequent and impressive. some of the fights might be hard to see with the shaky cameramanship and fast editing, but the car chase, the stuntwork, the (few) special effects, and the finale are all very noteworthy. in between the major action scenes, the story moves with a fast and tight pacing. there's hardly a dull moment.

at its core though, this telling of "batman" presents a very strong story, filled with deep characters, strong themes, and detailed nuances. the story itself is pretty solid, for as the mystery unravels it proves to be cleverly sublime and tight. what is most important is the character development though; bruce wayne's origins are explored in depth and with solid reasoning behind his ascension into a masked vigilante. going hand-in-hand with this portrayal are strong themes about fear, morality, and ultimately the value of decisive action. and as the batman character comes into a fully-realized being, a lot of interesting concepts are poured into it like hot iron filling an ingot; using fear as a weapon, the principles of ninjutsu, the power of symbols, to name a few. and on top of all that, the physical genesis of the character is explored more thoroughly than ever before; we finally see where he gets all his cool gadgets from, where his costume came from, how he gained the trust of key law enforcement officers, among other things. all of these concepts work together to make the story more believable, whereas in previous movies nothing was defined and everything about the character simply existed without any basis. the movie gets high marks as it is for utilizing previously unused opportunities. i'd give it even higher marks for its strong themes.

as a film, it is interesting. photography is superb throughout, with plenty of unique imagery and camera angles. editing is very rough, with some choppy action scenes, but most of the time it works to create a unique and frenetic style. acting is excellent all around; christian bale shows both aggression and subtlety in his dual-natured role, michael caine makes for a wise and witty butler, cillian murphy and liam neeson are cool as the villains, and gary oldman is perfect as jim gordon. it's also pretty cool seeing katie holmes, morgan freeman, rutger hauer, and ken watanabe in the mix. production value is very high, with loads of excellent sets, props, costumes, weapons, cars, gear, and everything else. the music score is epic! 5/5 (entertainment: very good | story: perfect | film: very good)

batman (1989) and batman returns (1992) were visually stunning but you could feel it's cartoonish vibe. while the characters (the good and the villains) were perfect in every aspect, the experience was all about fantasy. the action sequences in both movies were great but not as spectacular as in 2005's batman. i know, the f/x were not that advanced but still. 1995's batman was a great sequel to end the franchise. it had two quality villains, a spectacular scenario, great f/x but you could say that it was all about cash. the movie had potential. batman & robin...well, what can i say? it's not even better than batman's worst comic. this is the best "batman" movie of te saga, period.

batman begins delivers for everyone! it explains every single doubt for every batman fan. the plot is as good as you can get in an action film by inserting the obligatory dramatic elements, a love story, and the basic subplot that deals with bruce's internal demons. the way christopher nolans connects all the events is simply amazing. the man demonstrated with "memento" that he could create a clever, fast-paced, visually stunning thriller-action movie. he did the same and i say better work with this movie. the plot is dark but effective, it doesn't deal with the expected cartoonish villains or something like that, it deals with believable villains (in the standards of comics) that could anytime beat easily the joker or the riddler. there were some "scary" moments in the movie. not only visually but mentally. i mean, dr. crane's technique to create panic by wearing the mask and spreading some kind of poison is an impressive technique to create tension and fear. the same goes for the panic that gotham city started feeling after the massive poison spread. batman has scenes for everyone.

acting. the acting in the movie is easily the best in the series. christian bale (of american psycho fame) portrays batman in a solid, violent, and cool way. batman was never this impotent! excellent dramatic performance. the best batman no doubt about it. michael caine delivers a great, dramatic, and tender performance as alfred. also, congratulations to morgan freeman (as always), gary oldman (as always), and liam neeson for great, convincing performances. cyllian murphy and katie holmes deliver expectations. the rest of the cast including ken watanabe and tom wilkinson are solid.

directing. christopher nolan did a great job. he created the spectacular batman movie everyone was waiting for since tim burton's batman returns. the innovative camera angles, the scenes to break (in the climatic train scene at the end, nolan makes a take of a fully illuminated gotham city with tense music) or increase tension (pair to pair scenes with explosions), the fight scenes, etc. are high quality, the best you can ask for in an action movie. mr. nolan deserves respect, a lot of it because he overpassed expectations in a way that only a few can.

f/x, soundtrack, art direction, cinematography. the movie is brilliant to look at. it has an impressive shinning yet dark cinematography beautifully done. the soundtrack is perfect for the movie and the art direction is excellent, with great details. the f/x are just great, batman is a movie that proves that cgi abuse is not the best to impress people.

as a hard core horror movie lover, i can say i'm satisfied with this movie. the same should go for fans of comics, action, and films in general. batman begins is an impressive movie recommended for anyone that wants to have a great time with a movie that mixes drama and action in a perfect way.

batman begins is an exciting and incredibly satisfying experience. the story was spot on and thrilling, the plot realistic and fulfilling. the special effect were both breathtaking and terrifying. the cast, as well, didn't fall one step short. morgan freeman and michael cane were deliciously funny and exquisitely cast. liam neeson and gary oldman alone were worth the price of admission, and cillian murphy as dr. crane was thrilling and disturbing. christian bale as bruce wayne and as batman gave a gorgeous and flawless performance: keaton and kilmer can eat their hearts out! a wonderful film for any batman aficionado as well as those just looking for a great film. it's rare for a film to achieve this much perfection.

it was on the 4th of july, 2005 i saw batman begins! it was an awesome experience to see the dark knight on the big screen once again! i have been anticipating this film and it did not disappoint. the movie is solid with an outstandingly large and famous cast, great acting, super storytelling and character development, excellent action and effects, a tremendous musical score, and great directing! there are many points in the film i want to talk about including the cast and characters, composers, and scenes. the commentary is below.christian bale as bruce wayne/batman: bale has a great performance. he is younger than michael keaton but he pulls off the charisma wanye needs. he is nearly identical as keaton when it comes to the putting on the suit. he has very good movement that makes you believe he is the batman! his voice fits the character really well. i know that there are people who think that keaton is batman. in my opinion bale comes very close being number one. michael caine as alfred: in my opinion caine was the perfect choice to play the famous butler. caine provides very good acting here. in fact its some the best i have ever seen him do!liam neeson as henri ducard: arguably his greatest role and greatest performance neeson is terrific in this film and literally steals the show! he is one of my favorite actors of all time and it was just awesome to see him as a big time villain! i love the way he looks. his goatee, hair style, clothing, fighting ability, everything! if you are a fan of his and loved how he performed in star wars: episode i - the phantom menace then you will love him here! katie holmes as rachel dawes: i was very surprised by this actress. i have read many, many comments saying how weak, dull, and boring her performance is. well i didn't see any of that! i thought that she was very good and not to mention looked the same. her character is a woman and she is very convincing as a woman! i like female characters like this! holmes is a very fine actress and i hope to see her in many other great action films in the future! gary oldman as lt. jim gordan: he is excellent as gordan. a very likable character indeed. i like the way he is and looks. another top notch performance by oldman! cillian murphy as dr. jonathan crane/scarecrow: he is something else. just by looking at him i thought that he was insane! the scarecrow character is good and scary. tom wilkinson as carmine 'the roman' falcone: one of the most talented actors performs greatly as the big time mobster. wilkinson's british accent is gone and a very good italian accent has taken its place for his role. i was really anxious to see how he would perform as someone of this stature in a comic book feature film and in my book he was great! morgan freeman: freeman is a dandy charmer here! great acting as always. rutger hauer as earle: hauer was very good. he's not his usual action hero self here as he is a business executive. ken watanabe as ra's al ghul: great performance here. he makes his character mysterious and fearful at the same time. he has an awesome sword fight and shows you why he's a master! mark boone junior as flass: a good performance by this big man! linus roache as thomas wayne: in a brief performance he is very good. musical score by hans zimmer & james newton howard: this is an extraordinary score. it fits so perfectly in it and it is completely different than the music that danny elfman and elliot goldenthal composed for the previous batman entries. i love those scores but this one is excellent as well. its just so dynamic and exciting! if there are more batman films which i hope there will be i hope that they will be chosen to score again and again! direction by christopher nolan: he really put it together here. the fight scenes and everything is just marvelous. i hope that he directs more batman movies in the future because i like his direction. fight scenes: people are talking about how bad the fight scenes are. i liked 'em! they were very exciting and some of them were long too like the wayne vs. ducard scenes. i loved those! the street chase was really cool with all of the city lights and such. so there you have it! i loved the film. there many, many things i love about it. the things above like cast, music and the fight scenes are just a few. i like the fact that all of the cast members have a decent amount of time on screen. i saw star wars: episode iii - revenge of the sith twice and i adore that movie and i just love this one! people, we have a very exciting movie year in 2005 and so far i am pleased and you should be too! i want more of the batman movies because i love the people in this film and there are limitless possibilities that can happen in them! i would love to see the return of the scarecrow! bring fourth the joker, man-bat, killer croc, the huntress, harley quinn, the spoiler, cain, egg head, mad hatter, and the rest of the gang to the big screen!

movie nuttball's note:

before the movie started the trailers of war of the worlds and the island were shown and boy do they look great! bring on more dc films like more batman, superman returns, wonder woman, the justice league of america, the legion, the green arrow, justice society of america, the death and the return of superman, i could go on! i want dc & marvel to come out with a whole bunch of films including crossovers! it'll be so awesome!

i have seen the movie again for the third time. i never see a movie more than twice. this movie is a masterpiece. magic, maturity and intelligence inhabit this film. in my opinion, it not only blows the films of the previous batman series out of the water, but every other movie of the superhero genre. i love how they made us wait to see bale in costume. the beginning half of the film was like a good meal with the second half as an unbelievable desert. the fight scenes were good and mysterious. i know some folks complain wanting to see explosive fights ala matrix, but i loved using my imagination as well as viewing it on screen.

i couldn't find anything wrong with this film except maybe the clunky romance between bruce wayne & rachel dawes. i suspect nolan & goyer were forced to put a love interest to appease the hollywood gods.

scarecrow is one of the creepiest villain to grace the thanks in part to cillian murphy. i was happy how he played the role: icy cold. add to the fact his disguise was nothing more than a burlap sack: brilliance. i'm glad that nolan did not go overboard with grandiose effect for the bad guy. i hope he does the same thing with whatever villain he uses in the sequel. it was the subtleness of crane that frightened me the most.

liam neeson is great in almost everything he's in and this is no exception. he reminded me of lex luthor. he sees himself doing some great service for humanity instead of cut-out bad guy, twirling his mustache. the plan, although seen before in films, is done pretty well here. the main focus was on establishing batman and bring his presence to gotham.

i love the relationship between batman and sgt. gordon. gordon knows from the start that gotham needs a shock to system and is happy, even with some reservation, that batman is the "shock" gotham so desperately needs. the leap of faith he takes for batman is one of a man desperately looking for an ally and more importantly: a savior.

michael caine is hands down the best alfred to grace the screen. the wit and warmth of the surrogate father role he brings is so good. i love the scenes where he gives his input on how the supply and stock the batcave and how bruce so go about his quest. another favorite is morgan freeman. the man is a class-act and lucius fox is a wonderful character. his role is perhaps one of the most important: giving batman the tools to fight crime. he was such a scene stealer.

christian bale is batman! i always felt micheal keaton was too old and too short for the role. bale brings weight and depth to this role. i love when he interrogates people and the rage that seeps out of him. and believe bale will evolve as the character does. i always had said batman's career is like a snowball effect. his parents death is the catalyst, but the drive and the obsession he feels comes each time he takes to the night against the likes of the joker, two-face, penguin. that will bring the torture at end when gordon talks about escalation. with batman jumping off rooftops its only a matter of time before criminals take the same measures. nolan & goyer are so intelligent to come up with that line.

absolute brilliance. i wait with baited breath for a sequel.

i'm really not into the whole batman comic book thing... but i thought this movie was awesome in the trailers i saw on tv. and let me tell you it was one of the best movies i've seen in a long time. christian bale was hot! hot!! hot!!! he is a gifted actor as well.... morgan freeman was fabulous as he is in all his movies!! the story of how batman became who he is...was beyond words....such a deep story of sadness & triumph. everyone else was excellent in there roles..michael caine was a treasure. do yourself a favor and go see this movie on the big screen plus cillian murphy is super hot as scarecrow....i'd love for him to intoxicate me...!!!!

best. batman. ever. at last we get a realistic superhero-movie. gritty, real and believable. i'm loving it. batman begins is menacing and dark. the action and pace is beautiful. it never drags. it grabs hold of the audience and doesn't let go before the end. that's what good movies are all about.

batman begins takes on a whole different tone than the other batman-movies. instead of going with the far-fetched cartoony style of schumaker or the gloomy, dark (and sometimes weird) burton style, this one is a much more down-to-earth and dramatic movie. it takes batman and gotham down to our level. the audience understands what's going on, because they can relate to it.

also, the impressive ensemble of actors is one of the reasons i went to see this movie. the grand old men: liam neeson, michael caine, morgan freeman and gary oldman all come to their right here. especially neeson.

the batman franchise has been reborn. i can't wait for the sequel.

"batman begins" is an excellent movie about the origin of batman. i saw this movie opening weekend with my family. we went around 9:30 at night and i'm pretty sure the theater was sold out since it was very crowded. my family and i agreed it was very well done movie full of a lot of action. in fact after the movie ended (and even during some scenes during the movie) the audience was cheering.

"batman begins" told the story of bruce wayne and how he became the gothom city superhero batman. there were many great scenes during this film including some of my favorites involving the villain "the scarecrow". i also enjoyed the special effects, especially gothom city.

the acting in the film was also very well done, including great roles played by christian bale(wayne/batman), michael caine(alfred pennyworth), morgan freeman(lucius fox), and katie holmes(rachel dawes).

overall i think everyone should see this movie. it is definitely one of the best movies this year. i give it 10/10 stars and hope to see a "batman begins 2".

bad a-- movie. chris nolan did a bad a-- job with the batman. just about as better as burton. i was a little concern because the prior two with joel s. i like how dark nolan made the movie. that is how bob kane intended it. the cast was great. morgan freeman did a excellent job as lucius fox and ken watanabe as ra al ghule and cillian murphy as scare crow. most of all...christian bale as the batman... i think he played the batman very well and he acted out bruce wayne very well. great movie.....

great job...chris nolan...thanks for bringing the batman back to us...........

batman begins was one of the best movies i have ever seen in my life. i am still shocked at what i viewed at the theaters twice since it came out. christian bale is by far the best batman and the villains were extremely creative. so many great actors in this film and they all did up to my expectations. morgan freeman, gary oldman, liam neeson, cillian murphy and tom wilkinson. i must say that the character of dr. jonathan crane/the scarecrow was the best villain i have ever seen in cinematic history. cillian murphy was absolutely brilliant portraying this psychotic, fear-obsessed villain. i am not a big fan of katie holmes, but she did a decent job in this movie. from beginning to end, this movie brings you the true comic book story of batman. i give this film 10 out of 10, and i am way too excited for the sequel.

bruce wayne(christian bale)is taken from a prison in a foreign country by henri ducard(liam neeson) to ra's al ghul's(ken wantabe) palace in the mountains to learn how to let his fear and self-doubt go. he trains with ducard and flashes back to explain how he got there constantly. he explains how he couldn't get his revenge for his parents, why he's afraid of bats, and his relationship with rachel(katie holmes). he completes his training and is told that he will lead an army into gothem to destroy it. when bruce refuses to comply, he has no choice but to kill ra's al ghul and burn down his palace, saving ducard and his own life in the process. bruce wayne returns to gotham being grated by his trusty butler alfred(michael caine). he decides to fight crime for gothem and creates the alter-persona of batman. gaining new technology from wayne enterprises employee lucius fox(morgan freeman), batman goes to work quick taking down major crime boss carminefalcone(tom wilkinson).

a psychologist by the name of dr. jonothon crane(cillian murphy) causes with a militarized hallucinogen that he uses with his scarecrow mask. batman must stop the scarecrow along with a larger twist that unravels.

the movie is the superhero movie that i have been waiting for. it is the dark and realistic batman that fans have been aching for. keeping close the story made by frank miller's(sin city)graphic novels, christopher nolan strikes as big as he did with memento. bale is a great batman and cillian murphy plays an evil scarecrow. michael caine also made a splendid alfred. overall, the movie is absolutely stunning and completely entertaining. it's the best movie of the summer!

i highly recommend this movie.

forget batman and robin which nearly ruined the batman franchise. batman begins is hard edge, gritty, and dark. christian bale is the best batman actor and michael cane is the best alfred, giving the butler more character to be bruce's guardian. liam neeson is great as ducard, putting away his role in the mediocre film star wars: the phantom menace. my props though go to cillian murphy who plays the creepy and twisted dr. crane a.k.a the scarecrow. boy can that guy act, he is far by the best batman villain in the entire franchise! katie holmes is satisfying as bruce's love girl and gary oldman was the perfect jim gordon, looking exactly like the character and playing him with good comedic relief. a new character added to the series is mr. morgan freeman playing a duplicate double of james bonds q, lucius fox. now thanks to the character of mr. fox, we finally found out where bruce got his supplies, and may i say that batmobile was wicked!we now have a real batman movie that all fans will love. and the end of this film gives a great nod to the first batman film, you'll find out when you see it. bruce wayne has never seemed more interesting, thank you mr. nolan for giving us a batman film we can all enjoy! you need to go out and see this movie, it's one of the greatest movies of 2005!

after joel schumacher destroyed the batman series with batman & robin (1997), with it's extremely camp take on the dark knight that made the 60's t.v. show look like citizen kane, warner bros. and dc comics called upon english writer/director christopher nolan (the mastermind behind following, memento and insomnia) and a mostly british cast to save the franchise. whereas tim burton's batman (1989) and batman returns (1992) went for fantasy, nolan's batman begins goes for realism and near enough achieves it.

even though this is still a superhero movie it also achieves its goal of playing like human drama. the all-star cast boasts an extremely engaging christian bale as bruce wayne/batman, gary oldman, in his best performance since leon, as lt. jim gordon, katie holmes, showing off her wonderful talent, as district attorney rachel dawes, the always fantastic michael caine as bruce's butler alfred, a wonderfully creepy cillian murphy as dr. jonathan crane/scarecrow, morgan freeman, brilliant as usual even though he is playing one of the smaller parts, as lucius fox and the always amazing liam neeson as bruce's trainer henri ducard, redeeming himself after being forced into the background in ridley scott's action - driven kingdom of heaven.

one more thing that should get a mention, and an oscar nomination, is that fantastic score by movie music giants hans zimmer and james newton howard that fits the films mood perfectly.

i absolutely loved this movie. not only did 'batman begins' did the prior batman series justice, it did the same to the entire action/comic movie genre. i don't want to sound like such a fanboy but it was so awesome how things fell together for this movie. first of all, my favorite director was christopher nolan (memento/insomnia), actor was bale(american psycho/equilibrium), and hero has always been batman.

i was worried that the movie wouldn't live up to the hype or that it could be a little campy (big budget super hero movies w/ a ton of well known actors tend to be); but it wasn't at all. the movie was very dark, sentimental, intelligent, and exciting. i felt liam neelson, morgan freeman, and michael cane all were outstanding in the roles that they played.

the only bad things about the film (if you can even call it that) is: it leaves you waiting for the sequel! in a small sort of way, but mainly because the movies so awesome you never want it to end.

i watched the batman trilogy in 2017.oh main,i could have a words to describe this trilogy.and this movie is amazing,stunning,blockbuster,brilliant,phenomenal and evergreen movie of all time.what a movie is this with great plans,policies,actions.

i am just saluting to christopher nolan for his mind upon movies.what a great plan,actions,mind-games he has put in the plot.totally amazing movie i have ever seen in my life.first of all the acting of heath ledge and his expressions are truly the beauty if movie but the thing about christian bale, i have genuine words for him for his superb and excellent acting and especially his body language as bruce wayne.the plans of joker,man what a amazed he have planned and i just can not describe the beauty and suspense of this masterpiece. i had never thought that batman could be a better character and i totally had no idea ever but when i saw this movie,i just blown up man.

and there is a alfred,let me define him as his character: a loyal,honest,wise,carer or we can say beauty of wayne family.he is one of my favorite character in movie.they way he treats bruce i loved it,and there is a fox,he is also nice,loyal and honest.all the character i loved so much and that cop jim he also has showed great acting. my favorite movies series of all time.

"what the hell are you?" "i am batman!"

this line will surely go make a mark in hollywood history! christopher nolan, the director of the critically acclaimed movie insomnia, unleashes his version of batman, which i should say is the closest to the comics after the treatment tim burton gave to the character.

after the release of the first pictures of the batman costume, (thank god it was without the bat-nipples) and the heavy duty model of the bat-mobile (which again was a refreshing change from the sleek bat-mobile) the world was pretty excited about what seemed to be a more dark, hard gritted take on the character.

fortunately, mr. nolan does not disappoint at all. we get to see a perfect origin story of bruce wayne starting from the day of his parents' death until the day he finally dons the costume. we see him working with criminals to study their mind eventually meeting alan ducard (ra's al ghul) brilliantly played by the versatile actor liam neeson who trains bruce wayne to be the dark knight with his own evil plan in mind. the training justifies the fighting methods of batman in the movie, which is actually inspired by ninja fighting skills.

returning home, we meet bruce wayne's loyal and the most trusted friend alfred portrayed by micheal caine which makes a good father figure for him with his witty advices.

we see gary oldman playing jim gordon, gotham city's police commissioner and another ally of batman. talking about the characters of the movie, all of them fit really well in the movie. be it, the scarecrow, who actually gives some jumps during his tenure in the movie, or ra's al ghul; talking about endurance to bruce wayne or alfred asking "why do we fall?", all of them are near to perfection.

the movie itself has some nice thrills, for say, the entry of batman, actually creating fear and panic for the villains. the fantastic monster bat-mobile chase scene along with the background score of hanz zimmer is one which will be played by people driving at top speeds for years to come! now that i did mention about the background score, hanz zimmer is almost half-responsible for creating this perfect image of the dark batman with the music he gave!

special mention to morgan freeman a.k.a, lucius fox, takes the mantle of the technical support for batman. we see him explaining the suits, the weapons and my god, the bat-mobile in a thunderous scene.

something that did not add up was the inclusion of katie holmes. i found her an alien being in the whole movie, though she does her best.

so, go ahead and check out the guy who is flying on rooftops and you will be left craving for more because at the end we see what's coming next!

i have seen this film last night and caught the midnight screening. this is all about the birth of batman. most of the actors are british. sir michael caine did a good job playing bruce wayne's butler, alfred pennyworth. welshman christian bale did a real good job as bruce wayne & batman. the beginning was so intense. this film also introduces us to 2 of batmans enemies: ra's al ghoul & the scarecrow. i love the weaponry. if you liked batman from 1989 & batman returns from 1992, you've gotta see this. it's kinda like james bond, because lucius fox (portrayed by morgan freeman) shows bruce wayne the car and the weapons.

wow... this movie is so good. one could never imagine a new director will do wonders to the first batman movie he would direct. i remembered when i first saw the trailer, believe me my expectations were not high. but it's phenomenal pacing just won't let you blink. the score, plot, character, dialogue everything was interesting. bale, oldman, freeman and caine did amazing job with their role so does cillian. liam neeson was as usual fantastic. the whole training scene is breathless and tumbler chase scene is edge of the seat stuff. all in all its a great, great movie. although tdk is my favorite but this have a place of its own in my heart. this movie started it all. a solid 9.5/10 in my book and maybe the best superhero movie of all time.

i was excited when i first saw batman in 1989. it was a great movie. the sequel, batman returns (1992), was also good. then, batman forever spoiled it for me, even though skillful acting by tommy lee jones and val kilmer. i walked out of batman and robin, despite george clooney being in it. then, batman begins came to theaters.

batman begins focuses on bruce wayne's childhood and early years as batman. he is guided by his friend lucius fox and butler alfred pennyworth. the movie also deals with bruce's fear of bats, and how he uses what he fears to strike fear into others. christopher nolan delivers a dark tale. he proves that fear comes in many forms.

batman begins is definitely on my top 10 list for 2005.

i must say this is a wonderfully written movie, and is even performed better than it was written. this is the true batman movie that was meant for the cinema, it is powerful, it is dark, it is fun, it it is full of action oriented scenes, it is the masterpiece of all the batman films.

to be honest, i never liked any of the batman movies. batman returns (1992, danny devito, michael keaten) was decent but not good. as for the rest (batman,batman & robin,batman forever) were horribly empty of acting, the settings seemed fake, and the acting very much like a comic book (in a bad way). the characters were to over the top to the point of annoying, and at times the whole story dragged on with a worthless plot, as well some of the worst background music i've heard in a movie franchise. as you can see, my personality does not fit the comic book type.

as for this movie, it was simply terrific. christian bale was easily the best actor in the movie, as the power of his expressions comes through flawlessly for him, a superb performance. liam neeson was a true and valiant performer, his use of the given words and vocabulary are spoken with unbelievable eloquence, rhythm, and the end result is success. morgan freeman and michael caine are wonderful supporting actors that add their experienced talent to the all ready well-made movie. katie holmes and gary oldman give even more depth to the movie. i was surprised,nevertheless happy to see cillian murphey to act on the american cinema, especially this movie. the british actor seems to have mastered his accent honorably, and follows his acting like he always does in good fashion.

this movie was definitely the darkest of all batman films;nevertheless it succeeds to be the greatest of them all. christian bale takes michael keatan's place as the greatest batman, which really surprises me because i did like keatan's performances. this film has much much depth and finally shows to every batman fan and movie-goer how bruce wayne began his voyage to become gotham city's benevolent savior.

now everybody, listen, i will go as far as to say i liked this film better than spider-man (the once only film i considered marvel produced well). you ask why? christopher nolan takes all the flaws the other directors had in the other batman films, and portrays batman the way he was always meant to be shown. superman is an a super-human alien,spiderman has spider-like senses and powers, the fantastic four and the hulk and all the other mumbo-jumbo superheroes (i don't read comics sorry) have special *powers*. batman is human. batman has human weaknesses, human strengths. notice that bruce wayne never says he is batman. nolan portrays not a superhero, but how a man lost what he thought everything his life had to offer, succumbed to anger and lust for revenge, and evolved to become a man greater than what he once was. because we all seem to forget, batman is a regular human-being, who goes through unimaginable odds to protect human life, no matter how corrupt. that is why we see him as a superhero in the movie.

that is why christopher nolan did masterfully with this film like he did with memento.

if you see this movie, you will certainly be entertained. enjoy!! 9.5/10

got to admit, i did not want to like christopher nolan's film version batman begins (2005), a retelling of the batman legend. mainly because i love tim burton's highly original, groundbreaking films batman (1989) and batman returns (1992). well, christopher nolan did well with batman begins, a strong, provocative, sprawling epic retelling of how a conflicted young man, bruce wayne, battled his inner demons and conquered his deepest fears to emerge into a crime-fighting hero batman.

christian bale is excellent as young bruce wayne and, while i still think michael keaton is the best, i can accept bale because this is the young version of bruce wayne and telling how he emerged into batman whereas in burton's films, batman was already established. also, the tone of burton's flicks were more lighthearted, even though they were still rather dark films. nolan's batman begins is more realistic and serious, but it still works. again, bale really gives a strong performance in this film displaying a variety of emotions with conviction and depth.

the early stages of batman begins are told in random fashion. the film starts showing wayne being trained in tibet by ninja warrior henri ducard (wonderfully played by the superb liam neeson). both wayne and ducard are students of ras al ghul (larger-than-life ken watanabe). wayne is being trained in all facets of martial artistry to make himself almost indestructible. flashback to wayne's childhood. as a boy, young bruce is friends with rachel dawes and while playing, he is attacked by bats. this manifests itself as extreme fear in bruce, but his father thomas wayne (solid work by linus roache) instills in him that he must fight his fear. the scenes of young bruce and his father are effectively touching without ever devolving into sappiness. and it shows how a father's guidance can help shape and mold a boy into manhood.

of course, we know what happens to bruce's parents! leaving the theatre one night, a random thug named joe chill kills bruce's parents. a distraught young wayne rebels and runs away scouring the world trying to understand the criminal mind. fourteen years later, returning briefly for the parole hearing of chill (he was caught soon after the murder), wayne is going to kill chill, but someone beats him to it. crime boss carmine falcone (deliciously played by tom wilkinson) has chill killed because he was going to testify against him. when bruce admits to rachel (excellent work by the underrated katie holmes) that he was going to kill chill, she slaps him and tells him his father would be ashamed. i found this scene to be particularly effective. holmes got way too much flack for her performance imho. she really brings a sweet innocence, yet some serious inner strength, to the role of rachel dawes. plus, bale and holmes have great chemistry in this!

now, flashforward to the present and wayne's training with ducard and al ghul. they want him to go back and destroy gotham with his newfound abilities and powers. it is then that wayne realizes that ducard and al ghul are no different than men like chill and falcone. they are all selfish, evil men who think the world is their playground. wayne refuses and in the melee, destroys al ghuls temple, killing him, but saving ducard.

upon returning to gotham after a 7-year absence, wayne re-establishes himself in the city. respectively, we meet wayne's butler alfred (michael caine), wayne foundation chairman earle (rutger hauer), wayne foundation development head lucius fox (morgan freeman), and batman's future ally police sgt. jim gordon (gary oldman). the veteran actors caine, hauer, freeman, and oldman are all superb in their roles and have an amazing rapport with the young bale. there is a kind of dignified camaraderie amongst all these characters. wayne has fox introduce him to all those "wonderful toys" that he will use in his new role as the caped crusader.

after taking down falcone, batman must contend with the scarecrow (brilliantly played by cillian murphy), who was in cahoots with falcone and, as it turns out, ducard (the real ras al ghul!), who has been plotting his revenge against wayne and gotham city.

batman begins really does good job of jumpstarting the batman story, while still having satisfying doses of action and humor along the way. the cast is uniformly excellent and the humor really emerges out of the dialogue and is not forced at all. nolan does fantastic job of having a serious, realistic tone, but yet batman begins never seems boring.

a couple of complaints:

*the action scenes, while exciting and visually arresting, are kind of difficult to discern at times, especially at the climax. in burton's films, the action was exciting while still being discernible. i know this is a function of the ninja-warrior like training of wayne, but when he fought al ghul's ninja warriors at the climax, i felt that action should have been slowed down since they all had the same abilities. i felt cheated by that scene, which should have been better.

*i think bale as the real bruce wayne (not the ineffectual playboy) is way more interesting than bale as batman! it's ok here since bruce wayne has much more screen time than batman, which is the opposite of burton's films where keaton's batman definitely had more scenes than keaton's wayne. also, i liked the fact that keaton as bruce wayne was always the real bruce wayne, a reclusive billionaire. i think they could have pulled that off with bale, too. the playboy stuff seemed kind of tacked on and didn't come across well. i find bale's batman, with his super raspy voice and cowering like a real bat to be a tad odd at times!

but, overall, this is definitely a well-executed, provocative, well acted film which happens to be about a superhero!

when i first took a glimpse of christian bale in the role of the dark knight, i was a little skeptical. american psycho was good, but i just could not picture him in the role of batman. however; that all changed within the first 30 minutes of the film. this film is one of the best of the batman series. the role of the scarecrow is portrayed very well by cillian murphy (though i would've liked to see more of him)and morgan freeman (one of my favorite actors) played an excellent role. i even liked the **spolier alert** the hint at the end of the movie for the joker. overall, this movie deserves to be in the top 250, and if you are a fan of the series, or any of the actors, i recommend this movie to any one of you.
