first off, christopher nolan's the dark knight is not a superhero movie. it has nothing to do with comic book movies really. tdk is so far beyond the limits of its supposed brethren its really in a class of its own, with comparisons to iron man, spider-man 2, and even batman begins doesn't come close to touching upon the greatness of this film. not only is tdk the best superhero movie ever made, its quite honestly one of the best movies period.

nolan has really outdone himself here. not just himself, but everyone else that has made superhero flicks. he doesn't just adapt a comic book, he has created an entire world, one that just happen to involve comic book characters. his take on batman is the most inspired i've ever seen; getting the character's inner conflicts so right and make them ring so true is incredible. christian bale is great as the caped crusader (although his harsh growl is still the lone weak spot in his performance). thankfully he has an excellent supporting cast who all get their time to shine. michael caine is perfect as alfred, who keeps bruce from falling from grace and helps him when he just doesn't know what to do, and their banter is fun to watch. morgan freeman also shines as lucius fox, a mentor of sorts to wayne who, like in freemans best roles, just radiates wisdom. aaron eckhart is simply powerful as harvey dent, a district attorney who's character arc is one of the most tragic story lines in any movie. maggie gyllenhaal gets the short stick here, as nolan just doesn't know what to do with her character.

they may all be great, but two performers here easily trump them all: gary oldman and heath ledger. oldman gets a bigger, juicier role as jim gordon, gothams lieutenant who helps batman and dent to try and stop the rise in crime thats plaguing the city. his story arc is compelling to watch. that explanation leads me to one of the most inspired and creative villains ever conceived: the joker.

heath ledger is simply incredible as the joker, a man who has no past whatsoever (which is emphasized by his contradictory explanations of the origin of his scars), who seems to live just to create destruction. he is chaos incarnate, someone who wants to burn down gotham just for the fun of it, and a part of you will want him to just see how he'll do it. he has no remorse, he is twisted in every way, and he is in short, brilliant. ledger puts everything into this role. he is the joker, he'll make you laugh at all the wrong moments, and he will make you cringe so much you're face will get stuck. his performance will stick with you for a long time. hes an instant icon. all the oscar talk is not hyperbole. give the guy an academy award, he deserves it. its the role of a lifetime, the role he was made for. saying hes the best joker ever portrayed is underselling him. hes one of the best villains ever portrayed.

in batman begins, my one big complaint was that the action, while sometimes invigorating, was handled poorly, with the close ups and shaky cam inducing a sense of nausea instead of suspense. he not only fixes these problems, he expands on the overall action. when batman fights, he takes them in quick succession, using the kind of lyrical poetry unlike nothing i've seen since bourne ultimatum. the big explosions don't matter however, as with the best of nolan's work, a lot of the action is psychological. the movies plot rises to epic status because the characters within it are so compelling. it makes the tragic story resonate more than it probably would have otherwise.

simply calling the dark knight a superhero movie is wrong. its an epic crime drama that just happens to be based on a comic book. it trumps everything and everyone that has come before to be one of the best movies ever made. when the movie ends you may find yourself applauding, as you have witnessed a masterpiece unlike anything you've ever seen.

watching the dark knight on a big screen is an experience comparable to few other pleasures one can think of immediately. i honestly can't remember the last time i felt this satisfied coming out of a film. what's genius about director christopher nolan's latest batman installment is that it's not only a spectacular comic-book movie, but also one with an intellectual heart. it's not all chases and explosions and action scenes -- although there's lots of that -- it's also a really smart film about characters with edge and a plot that actually seems to make sense.

christian bale slips into the batsuit once again to play the caped crusader who thinks of hanging up his boots when he becomes impressed with district attorney harvey dent's crime-fighting resolve. but when clown-faced psychopath the joker shows up, batman realises retirement is a long time away.

in addition to new characters like harvey dent (played superbly by aaron eckhart, by the way), all significant characters from nolan's previous film batman begins return for this new adventure. police lieutenant jim gordon (played by gary oldman), bruce wayne's faithful butler alfred (played by michael caine), wayne's go-to guy for fancy gizmos lucius fox (played by morgan freeman) and assistant da and wayne's love interest rachel dawes (played this time by maggie gylenhaal) are all back and have respectable roles to play here, but the dark knight is ultimately about batman and the joker. it's a much darker film than any of the previous batman movies, and it goes into directions that few comic-book films have taken before. much of that edginess comes from the joker and his sinister plans. not merely content at killing his enemies, the joker chooses to psychologically torment his rivals by forcing them to question what they stand for.

inheriting the character completely, delivering a text-book performance that is hard to forget even days after you've watched the film, the late heath ledger is the joker. the greasy hair, the make up-smeared face, the red scar of a grin, the tongue snaking out of his lips, and that sloshy voice - not only is this joker a complete contrast from jack nicholson's largely comic take on the same role in tim burton's 1989 batman film, but heath ledger as the joker is undoubtedly the finest, most menacing villain in any comic-book movie yet.

for those interested purely in the spectacle value of the film, there's enough to keep you excited. cars explode, jails and hospitals are blown up, bombs are put in people's mouths, even left in their stomachs. there are some fantastic chase sequences, and there's one particularly jaw-dropping scene in which a massive truck flips in the air like an olympic diver. there's also the batmobile which transforms itself into an armored tank and even a turbo motorcycle.

naturally all this means it's a long film -- 2 hours and 32 minutes to be precise -- but it's unlikely that you'll complain because you're sucked into the drama pretty early on. allowing ledger and the joker to steal this film from under his nose, christian bale as batman takes a backseat during this ride. but nolan gives him that one magnificent scene which makes up for whatever complaints batman might otherwise have. in this scene, we see batman leaping off a gotham skyscraper, swooping down into the night, his bat wings rustling in the air as he descends on the city he's here to protect. it's one of the most fantastic scenes you've seen in film for a long, long time. and this is a fantastic film.

i'm going with four out of five and two big thumbs up for the dark knight -- go with a big bucket of popcorn and prepare to have a great time. it's for the pleasure of watching films like this that reclining seats and giant screens were invented.

plot: picking up where 'batman begins' left off, batman (christian bale) and james gordon (gary oldman) join forces with gotham's new da harvey dent (aaron eckhart), dubbed "the white knight" by the press, to dismantle the remaining mob bosses in gotham. but there's a new player in the game, a sadistic criminal called the joker (the late heath ledger), and he's hellbent on destroying everyone and everything in his path, in one way or another.

to put it simply, this is a powerful, moving film far beyond any previous comic book adaptations. the film truly is nothing short of superb. the late heath ledger was undeniably creepy & terrifying as the hateful, heartless, lip-licking, cackling joker (and trust me, he does a great job of making you hate the joker), while aaron eckhart delivers a powerful performance as the doomed da harvey dent/2-face, so powerful it makes me wish eckhart was the one up for an oscar nomination. christian bale is of course perfect as batman/bruce wayne with the always welcomed gary oldman, michael caine & morgan freeman reprising their roles as gordon, alfred & fox. maggie gyllenhaal lends nice support in the rachel dawes role originated by katie holmes (who is sadly better known now as mrs. tom cruise #3).

can't wait for the next one... and it had better have catwoman/selina kyle in it.

this is one of the greatest films of all time, not to mention the greatest superhero film. everything about this movie is completely stunning.

the acting is second to none, with heath ledger's portrayal of the joker being the best villain of any movie in history. he truly deserves an oscar. christian bale does a stunning performance as batman, despite the joker, in my opinion, being the main character. morgan freeman and michael caine do good performances as bruce wayne's assistants. gary oldman plays one of my favorite characters, james gordon, and he delivers a sense of hope in all of the chaos. lastly, aaron eckhart delivers an excellent performance as harvey dent. i thought his performance was great, and his ability to play two-face was good.

the story was also great. this was the first superhero movie in which i felt a real prescence of true evil. in the spiderman films, there was never a sense of evil like this. because of this evil, it also felt like batman was a true hero, not some guy in tights. this film proves "the night it darkest just before the dawn." while there was never a dawn, this film proves that in darkness, there is always light.

best movie ever, rip heath ledger

this is not a superhero movie. it's not a comic book movie. this is a statement about the time which we live in, and how we want to see ourselves, what we could see ourselves as, and ultimately the dangers of what we can become... put simply: ledger does for the role of joker what chris reeves did for superman. this is the new gold standard and could potentially forever change joker's image in pop culture. it will be almost impossible for anybody to do a plausible follow-up-- be it illustrated, live action, or animated-- that will be as effective as this one... this performance makes nicholson's "darker" joker of 1989-- a performance raved about by bob kane himself-- as campy-looking as caesar romero's joker of the 1960's tv show. ledger's character-portrayal could be called by any other name, put it in any other movie, and it would be the talk of hollywood as one of the scariest characters in recent memory.

never mind the fact that in this movie, everything and everyone is the star getting equal screen time, including batman, joker, harvey dent-- in a poetically brilliant portrayal by eckhardt-- gotham city, jim gordon, lucius fox, and all the tertiary characters and pyrotechnics..... never mind the basic storytelling flaws (among them characters "disappear" while other characters are still, technically, looking in their direction) and completely illogical time lines.... never mind that we still don't get an accurate explanation as to how any of batman's villains convince and recruit their hired thugs to devotedly do their bidding... never mind anything and everything that you would normally want to nit-pick. this film's main flaw is that it's too good. there was always a secret joy for fans in being unsatisfied, always complaining how the director never got this or that just right-- it always gave us, the audience, a reason to want and demand more attempts.... we always seemed to love the filmmakers' efforts more than the product given to us. but now that the joy of fan-kingdom complaining has been robbed from us, all i can say is: "thanks!!!!!!" go see it-- you'll be more than glad you did..... must watch again

never will be as good a batman movie as this. nor as a good a joker. it is the ultimate batman movie that has ever been made. if only heath ledger didn't pass away, i would've liked to see him in the the dark knight rises. the only other joker that comes close to him is mark hamill's joker. that is from the arkham series so it doesn't really count. if you love batman you will love this movie. bale captures the perfect batman, michael caine plays alfred perfect as weill. i couldn't picture anyone besides morgan freeman playing lucius fox, and gary oldman also perfectly captures commissioner gordon, while heath ledger steals the show as the most insane and homicidal joker you could ever meet. out of 10 stars i give it 13.

like watchmen, the dark knight shows what superhero movies are missing. batman sets out to destroy organized crime in gotham once and for all, and to put an end to the joker's murderous chaos - but at what cost? a great thriller, and my favorite movie. to stop the joker, batman almost instead of turning into a heroic vigilante, becomes a villain to end the reign of the joker. dark and deadly, the dark knight explores the inner depths of shadows and darkness of superhero justice and with an all-star cast including: christian bale, michael caine, heath ledger, gary oldman, aaron eckhart, maggie gyllenhaal, and morgan freeman - the movie almost seems like more than one movie.

i think the crew also deserve credit for making this film and putting in a lot of hard effort to create the sound and special cgi effects including the beautiful music score for the movie and excellent directing from christopher nolan who deserves an oscar award.
