the rest of the cast, kudos to aaron eckhart, give him another good role, he is good as harvey dent/two face...

a movie to recommend, but not to the faint of heart...

the dark knight is no ordinary summer hollywood flick,it is unconventional,convoluted and most precisely brilliantafter weeks & weeks of surmounting hype with the media throwing in all possible tidbits about the movie,the movie still managed to live up to the hype.this effort by a dedicated set of actors and technicians will certainly be remembered for a long long time..

i am not going to spill the beans by giving the whole movie plot,but i sure can review it the most probable question in your mind would be 'who was the show-stealer??' .the answer to this question is a no-brainer now(thanks to all those critics who watched this movie a week ago),it is heath ledger.his final performance surely does leave an impactheath literally lived the role of the joker and everything about him was great,be it the dialogues or the body languageon a scale of 10,i give him 11,no villain in the recent past has been as menacing as the jokerit is sad that he died earlier this year.he was a great talent and he would have given us more memorable roles.big round of applause for him and i surely hope he is nominated for the oscars next year..rip!!

outwardly,just like batman begins,the whole city of gotham is made to tremble and joker brings the whole city to a standstill with multiple homicides,explosions and threats.the trio comprising of batman,lt. james gordon and the new district attorney harvey dent join hands in wiping out the skum of gotham city and they are quite successful until the city's thug mob give in to joker's terms and what follows is sheer chaos.joker goes on a killing spree demanding the batman to reveal his true identity and he almost succeeds!!the whole story involves a lot of sacrifices to counter joker's moves and as an audience,we are jolted by one twist after the other.the story surpasses the mundane superhero storyline and is just inches away from realitysee it,to believe it!!

from the acting department,everybody give their best.my favorite christian bale delivers yet again as batman and also as bruce wayne although he has very less screen time as bruce wayne.bale is very much self assured but looks a tad anemic.he reprises his role just as a day at the office.gary oldman is given more scope this time around and he looks resolute as lt. james gordon.aaron eckhart is a new member to the cast and this is the first time i have seen him in a movie.he does well as the dedicated da and also as the vengeful two-face.maggie gyllenhall,micheal caine and morgan freeman go about their roles with finesse and no one looks wasted at the end.the director nolan had a clear picture of what we wanted and his ensemble deliver just the samebravo!!

coming to the technical department,the background music was just pulsating and concise.hans zimmer and james newton howard rework on their batman begins theme and bring about an haunting experience which lasts the movie's length.this movie deserves it.cinematography by wally pfister is top notch and is award worthy.i was dazed with the camera movements .editing was jarring sometimes but very much acceptable.but do save your praise-points for christopher nolan,jonathan nolan and david s.goyer.christopher nolan is the man who made memento and the prestige and he now according to me,holds the distinction of being called the most sophisticated director in hollywood.nolan's direction is very much in keeping the movie pacy and also elaborate at the same time.screenplay is tight as usual.his brother jonathan teams up with goyer for penning the story and they sure have done their homework with the comic books .supposedly,they have read a heck lot in bringing together a serious crime epic of a movie.oscar worthy stuff!!

and now,my favorite moments from the film

1.) the start of the movie.a urban bank robbery which acts as a superlative intro for the joker.

2.) the scene where batman jumps from the top ledge of a skyscraper to gate-crash into some thugs

3.) the pre-interval chicken chase scene was just awesome with old fashioned stunts and gripping music.this is as good as the climax chase in terminator 2!!

4.) all of joker's scenes..and also his preening hehehe

in a nutshell,the movie was just great and it can be seen more than twice.by the end,we were left gasping for more,everybody was unwilling to move from their seats,such was the impact.it was 152 minutes of a thrill ride.batman and joker brawl their way into a slobberknocker and their escapades make me think by picturising the batman as a silent dark do-gooder who detests the limelight and who does everything to be within his code of ethics and the joker who is the satan or the anti-christ with absolute chaos as his solve motive,a person who is an crime artist with a love for the theatrics.together,they are yin-yang but they are fun to watch so what are you waiting for,get a load of the dark knight before your friends deliver the spoilers.

the dark knight (2008)

christopher nolan again blows our minds away with stunning effects, great writing, and a phenomenal cast of the most talented actors and actresses in the movie business, when he brings back christian bale, as bruce wayne, his alter-ego batman in the dark knight (2008) as well as michael caine, gary oldman and morgan freeman. some new faces are, heath ledger and aaron eckhart. there really is no better way to describe the dark knight (2008) than as the "holy grail" of all movies. the sequel to batman begins (2005), the dark knight has broken records of all sorts, such as becoming the second movie of all time to break 500 million in the box office, and also having the biggest weekend's total, out of any other movie made. the dark knight brings back christian bale as gotham city's billionaire man, the owner of wayne enterprises, bruce wayne.

faced with all new problems and a new villain in the mix of thugs batman must now deal with the joker (ledger). batman (bale), lt. gordon (oldman) and new district attorney harvey dent (ekhart), set out to take out the remaining crime bosses and their pawns completely from gotham city. while trying to put the rest of them behind bars, a new criminal mastermind sets foot in gotham and sets out to take over. the joker gets on a personal level with batman, forcing him to think about what really is most important in his life.

heath ledger took the role of the joker, and showed why he was the right choice for the part. this being heath ledger's last full movie with a main role, he definitely did not disappoint. as batman tries to build his symbol as a hero and protector of gotham city goons are out to destroy it and take back the city they once had. trying to decide whether or not, being batman is what he really wants, bruce wayne is also faced with the dilemma of keeping his relationship with rachel dawes close to him. aaron eckhart, plays harvey dent gotham's district attorney is also trying to fight crime and build a symbol for him while trying to avoid being assassinated and keeping a relationship with rachel dawes. christopher nolan displays batman's power and importance by choosing to shoot a broad range of close up and low shots. nolan also does this with ledger's character the joke. the dark knight is a movie of great darkness and that is why most of the movie's scenes are shot in dark, very dim lighted ways to make the movie have that eerie, scary feeling. nolan shows in great detail the massive chaos and special effects, with ingenious camera shots and lighting. this movie is great for teens and adults with its riveting screenplay, brief romance and intriguing plot. being rated pg-13, some parts and images could be too intense for some young children.

any batman lover or comic book enthusiast will greatly appreciate all the christopher nolan put into this movie. rating this movie with five stars, it should be seen by everyone. nolan is able to make it seem as if the viewer is right there going along with every punch, kick, and explosion that the dark knight has to offer.

christopher nolan has a vision. and whether you agree with it or not, he undeniably completes it in "the dark knight"--a vicious, engrossing, overwhelming, intelligent event- film that re-defines 'comic-book-flicks'. in nolan's grim, dark-depiction of gotham-city (the crime-ridden hell protected by legendary superhero batman), the director strives to make everything real (something he began in the well-received "batman begins"). he makes it plausible, possible. and yet there's more to it: just as 'begins' was a dissection of myth, the nature of symbols and heroes, 'knight' is the escalation of that notion. it's a biblical- confrontation of 'good-and-evil', yet as 'good-and-evil' really exist: a conflict of ideals, something that can't be purely-defined but that is relative to a viewpoint. in nolan's world, the line of villainy and heroism isn't crossed... it's non-existent. the bad-guys don't see themselves as bad-guys, and as such something so unnervingly-real comes across it might fly past some people's minds (no insult to anybody, it's just common that people don't look deep into 'popcorn-flicks'): the battle is a complete ambiguity.

the film runs at nearly 2.5-hours, yet never ceases to lose interest or momentum. it doesn't waste a scene or moment; every event is utilized and necessary. 'the dark knight' tells a story worth telling and it takes the proper amount of time to tell it. action-sequences are frantic, old-school, eye-grabbing stunts (vastly superior to 'begins') and in their chaotic intensity we see that they serve purpose to the story, yet more interesting are not played for pure entertainment-value: we are meant to watch, petrified, simply hoping that the outcome will go the hero's way. attention is never lost because we are immersed in a breathtaking, almost completely-unpredictable story (it packs many a shock), that makes us think and more importantly gains our emotional-investment. we come to care for the characters, because they are believable, developed, and personified fully.

everyone has great-chemistry together. maggie gyllenhal is a more mature rachel dawes than katie holmes. morgan freeman provides his authoritative presence to the role of bad- gadget-inventor/wayne-enterprise ceo lucius fox, and under anyone else's portrayal, the part would be less-memorable. gary oldman underplays his world-wearied lawman with such honest-nobility, you never feel for a second any of its forced-acting. the irreplaceable michael caine makes a gentle, reassuring, father-like presence as alfred, and the movie would surely fail without his strong-presence and interjected-moments of light-humor.

and while everyone (rightfully) pours the praise unto bale and ledger, i think most are glancing-over knight's breakout-performance. as harvey dent, aaron eckhart does more than hold himself in the company of such a renowned-cast. he makes his presence known, whether he's playing on the easy-going charisma of gotham's 'white-knight' or the broken and damaged, twisted-soul of two-face. he achieves a full-impact with the tragedy that comes unto his character, and so closely connects with dent, that he makes his pain tangible for us: we sympathize even as we become terrified. he captures both facets of each personality flawlessly.

now, some people cite that 'knight' has a potential fatal-flaw in the supposedly wooden- acting of christian bale. admittedly, his development is not as grand as in 'begins' (yet that film gave us such a good psychoanalysis of wayne, we hardly need more), yet what bale pulls off is admirable. wayne is not an eccentric personality. he is a disillusioned man who can hardly find any joy in having no family, giving up his love-interest and spending his life fighting a battle that may never end. he's dark and conflicted, and bale plays up on that brooding-mood by making wayne look as though a thousand dark-things were on his mind. he's not wooden...he's a humorless, quiet individual. even when wayne is acting as a frivolous playboy for the public, every now and then bale offers us a powerful glance that reminds us its all a façade; that deep down, something more disturbed irks him. occasionally he offers a broken-smile when exchanging banter with alfred, letting us know that beyond the dour depression of the caped-crusader lies a damaged human-being. it is only in the guise of a growling masked-man, that he can unleash his true, ferocious personality.

finally, who could forget heath ledger. now, when he was first-announced for the part, i was (along with many other people) asking myself: "why?". mr. ledger had proved with 'brokeback mountain' he could deliver a potent performance. but he hadn't before. it is only, after seeing this film, that i know the answer to 'why?': i see the significance of his loss.

when heath appears in this movie, he is completely unrecognizable. his voice is distinctly-altered; a near-whiny, pedophile-like tone that sends shivers down the spine. his face is completely splattered with makeup that renders him both freakishly-nightmarish and strangely-funny. and when you see him, you don't think it's him. in this, his final performance, ledger proved he was a chameleon. his two iconic performances in this, and 'brokeback', could not be more different. i am convinced he could have been anything in his career. he commits so intensely to character that the line of actor/portrayal dies. his every tick and gesture only further-enhances his character. heath never hams the role up or goes for something cheap: he delivers a fully-immersed display of psychotic madness...or do we just label him that to feel safer? the movie writes the character brilliantly; blending terrifying truth into his every social-accusation, and making us question why we laugh at his sick-jokes.

'the dark knight' has had an incredible-amount of hype running for it, from the get-go, mounting ever-higher, until heath ledger's too-soon death. and the finished-product does more than exceed all of the near-impossible expectations placed on it. it becomes something much richer than a super-hero-franchise-saga. christopher nolan has opened a new door in cinema: allowing action-flicks to become more serious, capable of intelligence. he has transformed this into a piece of artwork, full of beauty, terror, moral-conundrums. this movie has changed things...forever.

at 12:00 am on july 18th in my local movie theater, i saw what may possibly be(at least in my opinion) to be one of the greatest movies ever made, "the dark knight". i know, i know i'm just another person drooling over a super hero on the big screen and you think in a few weeks or months i'll forget all about this film, but no thats not it at all.

what i experienced in those two and a half hours, sitting in my seat, just gazing at the big screen, was probably the best movie experience i've ever had(next to probably my first time seeing 'the godfather'). when i tell you that this isn't your ordinary "superhero movie", this isn't your quintessential big budget, high grossing, star studded action/adventure movie, i mean it. this is art, this is poetry, this is cinema. this is how movies should be made, this is how movies used to be made(aside from the special effects and cgi of course).

let me cut as much to the chase as i can, heath ledger gives what i consider, one of the better supporting performances in the last twenty years. actually, scratch that, of all time! ledger was absolutely captivating as the joker and(no offense to jack nicholson, he's one of my favorite actors) kicks the crap out of nicholson's performance twenty years earlier. ledger without a doubt, not out of sympathy at all but out of pure talent, deserves the academy award for best supporting actor.

another awesome performance which will probably go unnoticed is gary oldman's for playing lt. gordon. oldman is a very good and very underrated actor(also one of my favorites). christian bale is amazing once again as batman.michael caine, morgan freeman, and maggie gylenhal all give excellent supporting performance as well.

while this film may or may not entice you to go see it, while most people might consider it "just another superhero movie", take it from someone who's seen thousands of films, old and new, this is one of the greatest movies i've ever seen.

highly recommended. an absolute must see! 11/10

what can i say about the dark knight that hasn't already been said? it's already rated as the 3rd best film of all time on imdb. believe me, it deserves that spot in the top 10, easily.

but let me just warn you, this is not a movie meant to be pure "fun". it is not a pure adrenaline ride, with no purpose but to give you explosions and punches. this is meant to be taken seriously, in every single aspect. where as some people may want movies only to be fun, and those movies are good sometimes, this movie does not even try that. this movie is a balance of drama, sheer creepiness, and action. the action is pretty damn good, very exciting (especially the chase sequences), but it's not the focal point. it's not gonna be the type of movie you should watch if you just want action. i would say this is an epic crime drama more than anything, with a theme of good vs evil. anyone who knows some of cristopher nolan's work knows his films have thought put behind them.

speaking of which, nolan is a great director, one of the best in recent years i now believe. during action sequences the camera work is frenetic, but you can see what you need to. every punch and kick has a sense of power behind it. on the other hand during the flights of batman the city seems large and expansive, and even batman seems minor in comparison. in my opinion nolan knows how to make a good movie.

nolan's brother jonathan has co-written a great screenplay with his brother, and i think i must say something. half of the brilliance of the joker and batman/wayne is definitely due to the writing. their respective actors just happen to be almost perfect, but you must give points to jonathan nolan. never once does a line seem truly unnatural. even the one liners have a natural wit, as if someone really could say something of that sort on the spot.

as far as acting goes, everyone is pitch perfect. not one person really seems fake, save for a few civilians who say lines a little forced once in a while. still, all characters with names in the movie are played very well, which should tell others who make movies that casting is very important, even for minor characters. from caine as alfred, freeman as lucius fox, oldman as lt. gordon, gyllenhall as rachel dawes (much better than holmes), everybody does well.

bale is very good as batman- dark and gruff voiced- but more importantly, he is able to switch characters to be bruce wayne, the playboy show off type at ease. he will hopefully get recognition with even more people now because he is a great actor. eckhart is pretty good as dent as well, and we see a gradual change in his character emotionally and on his thoughts of heroism.

and ledger, what can i say? if joker appears in the next movie, i doubt anyone can play him as well. every action, lip smack, word, everything that he does or says is the definitive joker. before this movie i always wondered what makes him batman's most popular enemy. now i understand: joker is downright evil and psychotic and he seems to be a mastermind of planning, thinking about everything before it happens. he has the exact opposite ideals (trying to bring down gotham to the criminals) of batman, who wants to bring peace. once again, credit must be given to both ledger and jonathan nolan's writing.

the music (hans zimmer and james newton howard) is brilliant at setting the mood for everything and often makes scenes super tense. there are some moments in the movie where there's just a dull vibrating bell thing sound (the scene where joker sticks his head out the car window that is in the trailer), and it was actually mesmerizing. the sounds of guns and punches feel very solid and heavy, just like they should.

joker once tells batman he doesn't want to kill him, saying "you complete me". now others in the theater started laughing, thinking that he meant it as a joke (which was one meaning possibly). but it is more than that- batman completes the joker, because no matter how much good there is in gotham, there must be someone like the joker to counter that with evil. in a way gotham represents the whole world's struggle between evil and good. and in the end, batman and joker are simply two faces of a coin- they have different faces and ideals on the outside, but in many ways, they are made of the same stuff inside, and are necessary to each other.

this review has been swirling in my mind for ages, i watched it at the cinemas and didn't know quite what to make of it...i was a big comic book fan, a great lover of batman begins, so when the trailer arrived i was in awe of heath ledger as the joker and impressed by christian's development of the batman.....

gotham city is in turmoil as the events of batman begins have thrown everything into chaos, people are dressing up as batman and fighting crime with guns, while some of arkham's inmates are still on the loose, and the leading criminals in the city are terrified of the thing that lurks in the shadows. until a man arrives who doesn't seem to be afraid of the batman, a man who dresses up as a clown...a man who calls himself the, joker.

joker unleashes hell on gotham city torturing and killing people, blowing up buildings all in the hope of catching batmans attention and he does, as well as harvey dent's, the new da.

i felt that there was too much hype building up towards this film and there were so many non-fans suddenly jumping on the band-waggon that it made it hard to distinguish if this film was truly great....

heath ledger's portrayal was truly magnificent, he went out as a great hollywood actor, he portrays a man truly lost to madness, a man who wants to understand why gotham celebrates another maniac? while aaron eckhart plays a satisfactory harvey dent, he is a man who is truly trying to change things. gary oldman is as fine as the first, michael caine takes a backseat in this film but hopefully he will return in the third with a bigger part. morgan freeman becomes a more pivotal place within batman's side, and does justice toward the end. maggie gylenhaal was okay...i felt the role needed katie holmes.... and finally erice roberts as sal maroni, eric did a tremendous job playing the mobster; he oozes with charm out of every pore...

and finally i come to christian bale. bale takes his character to a new level, his bruce wayne, is broken up into two people, the brooding 'wayne' who spends his days stitching himself back up, and staring into space with the pain he constantly feels and the bachelor 'bruce', a man totally ignorant of the things that are happening around him...

this batman is much more violent then the last, he's had enough and will throw you off a building if he has to...a creature that is losing the fear that he instilled in the hearts of his victims to the popularity.....

and finally christopher nolan, nolan focuses on the action a little more and create breathtaking sequences like the bat-pod chase, the truck flip, batman standing on top of a huge building and then leaping off... nolan shows gotham in a more brighter role, as the city gleams with happiness, almost happy at what has happened in the previous film.....i leaped out of my seat towards the end when batman takes on the swat team and the criminals in order to save the innocent, absolutely beautifully choreographed.

all in all, a great sequel...but hopefully will return to the roots in the third...

it seems to me that this film is the best of 2008. and many years to come. it is simply a masterpiece! the entire time, from the first take, to the breathtaking last, i was on the edge of my seat.

the acting, well what can i say about it. wonderful! christian bale does a great job as batman the second time. aaron echkart does a great, but disgusting harvey dent outlook. morgan freeman is always funny, along with michal caine. gary oldman does an awesome job as gordon. maggie g did a good job. (i'm glad they didn't bring back katie holmes.) but now the highlight.......the joker. heath ledger's incredible job as the joker brought out the characters dark side, with a few funny stuff thrown in! i would take heath ledger's joker over jack's any day! jack's joker has the funny clown side with his white face. while heath's brings the dark creepy side with his angry face paint covering up his violent scars.

the joker is the best part of the entire film, his evil dark character is deliciously great. the way he stands, looks, how he kills people, and of course, the smacking of the lips. in every scene with him in it, my hands shook. i noticed a few rows down, the first time you see the joker, a woman began to cry. the film made me sad as well to.

the action was one of the greatest i've seen in a while. nolan brings things out i have not seen in a film before. so many cool and disturbing action scenes. nolan i think is one of the new visionary directors. this movie brought out an intense side of the story of batman. the entire film is intense. that's why i liked it.

the film in incredible. heath ledger would deserve an oscar dead or not. i will see this a lot in the theater,and will be added to my dvd collection.

the film will make you laugh, jump, cry, and applaud at the end. i know i was.

i have waited for this film for so long and now i have had the privilege of watching it.most of this movie came to me as a surprise.the dark knight is one of,if not,the best film of the year and probably ever made.it is one of my favorite films.it was more than a action film to me,it was an epic like heat,the godfather saga and scarface among others.christopher nolan was brilliant at directing this so in my view,he should be nominated for an academy award for best director as well as the film as a whole being nominated for the academy award for best adapted screenplay as well as the academy award for best picture.

christian bale stars as batman/bruce wayne who proves that he is just as good as he was in batman begins,if not better.the cast also includes gary oldman(jim gordon),michael caine(alfred),morgan freeman(lucius) as well as william fichtner,eric roberts,aaron eckhart(harvey dent),maggie gyllenhaal(rachel dawes) and the late,great heath ledger as the joker.

the cast was magnificent but i think it was heath ledger who made me feel proud to watch this film.his performance is worthy of an academy award win for best actor as he gave it his all and more than 100% of an effort for his role as the joker.we will all miss you,heath and your character who you made iconic.rest in peace.heath ledger-1979-2008.

mark my words, the nolans brothers will be on the same level as the coens shortly. their films provide a dark and disturbing world into batman's persona and the illusion of the life he desires, bruce wayne.

simply put, this film possesses every attribute a viewer looks for in a film. it has tremendous writing, directing, acting, scenery and plot. how can you go wrong with oldman, eckhart, caine, gyllenhaal, ledger, freeman and bale. a superstar cast that doesn't disappoint.

i won't spoil the film for anyone, but i urge all to see it. it is my own selfish need, but i feel robbed that cinema will never again see such a disturbing and entertaining character personified in ledgers performance. rip...

for the faint of heart be warned--here be spoilers.

let me start off with, yes; i have been looking up every small piece of info about this movie for a year, yes; i ordered my tickets 12 years in advance, yes; i counted down the hours and minutes till the movie opened and yes; i stood at the theater 2 hours early to make sure i got a really good seat. i'm a fan of batman, always have been always will be, through the good and batman and robin.

but this bat movie had so much hype that even if you're not a fan you are drawn to see it, if only to see heath ledgers last movie. and after seeing it i can only say one word....holy crap. take everything you know about movies and throw it out the window people, this movie is so full of twist and turns that the 2 hour 45 min run time seems like 10 minutes and once the last frame of the movie is over, you'll find yourself asking "when is the third one now?"

the dark knight picks up right where batman begins left off, and the caped crusader could not be in better form. new gizmo's and gadgets make the capture of the joker look good.

which brings me to, the joker. i personally have never been a fan of heath ledger (my daughter thinks hes dreamy) but this role made me a fan at once. this is the joker! forget cesar romero and jack nicholson, while good versions, they fell far from who the joker really was, a sadistic serial killer with no morals or guilt. this joker is scary, and believe me, you would not want him at your birthday party. my wife (who is a shrink) is watching this trying to diagnose his mental illnesses, and i'm laughing because i'm watching a comic book literally come to life. we've come a long way from the 60's batman series and its about time we saw the characters for who they really are.

we have the usual players: bale, caine, freeman, oldman (except katie holmes, but oh well, her loss) two face even makes an appearance here, and he reminds me of shadow of the bat comics, a very good look for him, way way better than tommy lee jones' two face.

however, a few things did bother me, and i thought i'd share them with you, like:

1: gordons wife, her name is barbara....you mean like batgirl? isn't barbara gordon commissioner gordons daughter? ewwww.

2: two faces 'transformation'. it seemed really rushed, a big lead up just to have a small 'poof' and hes twoface. seemed a silly way to have it happen if you ask me, which no one did.

3: with two face, the eye on his scarred side, how does it stay moist? he has no eye lids to blink with. does he use special eye drops or something?

4: ok, so some dweeb guy at wayne enterprises discovers 'hmmm, a lot of stuff is missing', why did it take so long for this to be discovered? you'd think with a huge business like that there would be more checks and balances.

5: on the same note with the dweeb guy, how did the guy decide 'bruce wayne is batman' why not fox? fox had access to all that stuff and was obviously the one who lied about the stuff going missing? why would he go after wayne of all people first?

6: maggie gyllenhaal....what is the deal? every line she had seemed like she was whining through it. thank god we didn't have to put up with much of her in this role.

7: what is with batmans voice? take a cough drop already.

but even with my nonsense complaining, this is the best i have seen in a long time. best film i have seen ever if i may be so bold. the hype was well met and this one is even better than the first. if this is any indication of what to expect from this new batman franchise, we are in good hands.

long live batman!

i had been looking forward to the dark knight since the middle of 2007, and the death of heath ledger increased the already growing hype surrounding the film. approaching the cinema, i decided to forget the hype, forget my own desire to watch, so i could do the film justice in my own way. i'm glad i did, as i think this is the 21st century's best film so far, it surpasses the hype magnificently.

the film centres around batman, james gordon and harvey dent's struggle against the joker, a new criminal in gotham city who is running riot. as the city begins to descend into chaos, our heroes begin to see what they must become in order to stop him.

from the opening scene, it is clear that the dark knight is more about the villain than the hero. heath ledger is simply unbelievable as the joker, he bristles with psychotic energy in every scene. his body language and vocal range are an inspiration and he is a truly terrifying character. as a heath ledger fan, my expectations were exceeded beyond belief. the real surprise was aaron eckheart, who was at times even more chilling as two-face than ledger. watching him slowly turn from gotham city's white knight into an evil, vengeful monster is brilliant. christian bale is as good as he was in batman begins, and it was nice to see maggie gyllenhall surpass katie holmes. michael caine and morgan freeman's performances were several levels above what they were in batman begins. each actor complemented each other, and shares a common plus point with anchorman in that it was as near as can be to perfectly cast.

i think this film's main strength is it's writing. the script delivers constant high quality dialogue and some of the best twists and turns since fight club, and i love fight club. i love how nolan adapted the characters into what worked the best, in particular the villains. the campness of the joker and two-face's previous incarnations is non-existent, and would be out of place in this version of gotham city. the two-face character is visceral and graphic, and harvey dent's fall from grace is handled brilliantly. the origins of the joker are not shown, merely referenced by the joker himself in some horrifyingly genius dialogue.

i was blown away by the dark knight, it was almost perfect. the only niggle i had was that i would have liked to have seen more of cillian murphy as scarecrow. this film was a fitting end to heath ledger's career, and the joker is definitely the role he will be most remembered for. the must-see film of 2008.

the dark knight is the best comic book film and one of the best films ever made. it is a dark, and gripping tale of crime, psychopaths, and the city of gotham. it can't be said enough that heath ledger's performance as the joker is stunning. his last role will be known as his best and is oscar worthy. this joker is a terrifying sociopath which will be remembered for years to come. christin bale is once again a great bruce wayne/ batman. the viewer really feels for his character and his struggles. michael caine, gary oldman and morgan freemen are also great as usual. maggie glyhanall adds depth to the character of rachael dawes and is much better than katie holmes. aaron eckhart is a fantastic harvey dent and has an impressive and gruesome alter ego. the action scenes are spectacular especially since there was little cgi. the villains and mob bosses are all greatly casted and used. the music and score are great especially joker's theme song. the dark knight has broken several box office records and currently is rated #1 on imdb. it truly deserves all the honors.

the dark knight was 100% astounding. the first time i think i've ever walked out of a theater and not had a least one complaint. the perfect superhero movie. i'll remember the movie for its top notch performances. every scene ledger is in is pure magic. he doesn't steal the scenes hes in, he takes them. eckhart is absolutely insane as dent. you really feel for this guy. he is completely controlled throughout the entire movie. even as two-face. nolan took the screen time to make us believe in dent and at the end it shows. bale is perfect as batman again. alfred, fox, gordon, etc all get there due. i will remember this film mainly for how spread out everything is. every character is used. the story is complex, but perfect for the particular movie. visuals are also excellent. i really can't think of one thing i disliked about the film.

i'll remember this film for ledger's and eckhart's performances, the character development, and the overall fantastic directing on the part of nolan. the perfect superhero movie. 10 out of a possible 10.

when heath ledger was first cast as the joker, i, like many others, had raised my eyebrows to say the least, as he was on very few of the multitudes of lists of actors that people were saying who should play the joker.

i'm happy to say that i didn't bash the choice, like many others did. having been a huge fan of batman begins, i had faith in christopher nolan and the vision he had for the dark knight. i was quite curious to see how ledger would do. i wasn't surprised he did well. i was surprised at how he hit a grand slam with this performance. wow! i did not see ledger at all in this movie - i only saw the joker. i doubt i will be able to ever watch the 89 batman with jack nicholson again. ledger's joker puts all the rest of the joker incarnations to shame. he hits all the right notes of the character - his insanity, his twisted view on life, his doing things for no real reason, but just to do it. his relationship with batman is extremely true to the comics thanks to the brilliance of the screenplay and ledger. the interrogation scene in the police station and the dialogue between batman and the joker near the end are highlights. this was a very well defined rendition of the joker that will be extremely difficult to top. ledger's performance alone will make this movie extremely rewatchable.

then there's aaron eckhart and the character of harvey dent/two-face, a character that had yet to be fully realized in a batman movie (batman forever did not do the character justice, no pun intended, at all). finally, we get a very well realized character arc, a tragic tale of the white knight, harvey dent, an honorable man destined for a tragic downfall. thank you christopher nolan for finally delivering a worthy tale of the tragic character dent. aaron eckhart was fabulous. i always liked him as an actor, but i think this has been his finest performance yet. he makes dent a very likable person who you hate seeing go through what he goes through over the course of the movie. his transition into two-face is very well done, very believable. they establish many of the traits that would go into that personality very well at the beginning. the way they incorporate the coin was well executed.

christian bale is good once again as batman. morgan freeman and michael caine are their usually reliable selves, bringing nice comic relief at points. a welcome cameo by cillian murphy adds a nice touch and i thought eric roberts actually did quite well as mob boss sal maroni, who deals with the joker, but not completely happy about having to do so.

this was a two and a half hour movie, but it moves fast. the interweaving of the story lines, particularly with the joker and dent was impressively done. the strength of the movie is the strong story and memorable characters. i'd highly recommend it. one of the movies that actually lives up to the hype.

this year was flooded with top-notch movies that surpassed my expectations - the dead-pan but utterly hilarious (in a dark way) there will be blood to the summer-loving iron-man and everything in between. however, when the dark knight first hit the cinemas, i took pride in witnessing what i would humbly deem as the greatest movie of the decade.

let me first get pass the obvious. its batman! and then there is joker! yes,christian bale and christopher nolan are on top of their game as usual,but heath ledger made me believe that there is a god. oh, and then there was the supporting cast which includes the ever soulful aaron eckhart, the relatively brilliant (as compared to katie holmes) maggie gyllenhaal and some unknowns (morgan freeman, michael caine and anyone knows gary oldman?).

nolan's controlled directing has orchestrated a sombre piece of crime drama in which the stand-off between batman and joker is worth the price of admission alone. the movie is visually stunning and the soundtrack is the best i have heard in years. certainly, this is a movie micheal mann would be proud of.

without giving too much away, the movie goes to explore the central theme of anarchy and the sacrifices one have to make in this fabricated society. it highlights the burden of being a superhero and the liberty of being a villain. it also ties some loose ends in terms of the development of some characters. the depth of the movie may skip pass a casual viewer but the action set pieces is in every respect of the word, adrenaline-pumping.

some critics have bemoaned the movie to be anti-climatic and bringing together several stories into one 2 and 1/2 hours of drama. i say if it is done right, who cares? heath ledger's performance is almost certain of an oscar and i give credit to everyone who has their name on the credits.

this movie mind you is not iron-man or wanted. if i ever were to be asked to sum up this movie: it's heat on crack done right.

little more can be said... the dark knight was simply brilliant. never have i seen a comic book movie explore the metaphysical depths of morality, bad conscience, resentment, vigilantism, and justice to the extent that nolan does here. the story takes so many abrupt left turns and on-a-dime twist that it leaves you as dizzy as the breathtaking action sequences are themselves.

if there were any flawed traces left in those tautly edited reels they are erased by mesmerizing performances from the entire cast. freeman and caine's chops ranged well beyond just being two clever and witty old men. bale surpassed what he did for begins. eckhart is able to take a somewhat clichéd character (thematically and in appearance) and generate it into someone complex, brooding, and yet seemingly fragile.

ledger's performance alone should and will haunt you for years to come. he truly becomes what he proclaims himself to be, and agent of chaos, a juggernaut that fuels anarchy and tragedy like an all consuming fire. despite how disturbing and unnerving his humor becomes, you can not help but give a macabre chuckle. the sequence where the joker appears in a nurse's dress becoming frustrated with an explosives detonator while bangs and fire surround him is a riot.

believe the hype! this is may be one of the best movies of the year, let alone the best movie of its kind.

seeing "the dark knight" for the first time took me back to my childhood. that magical time when you could get excited about something. imagine this: 8:00 pm on july 18th 2008, a theater full of people, full to the point where some people sat on the floor. the curtain falls. the batman logo appears on screen and the room goes silent for almost an entire two and a half hours, except for a few laughs and gasps. it ends with the loudest applause ever heard in a theater with a hundred people. that's the power an epic has. what is an epic? it's a movie that sets out to be the greatest of all time and comes close. "the dark knight" comes dangerously close.

at the end of "batman begins" commissioner gordon warns batman about his impact on crime. the harder he fights crime the harder the criminals will fight him. "the dark knight" takes this idea to the next level. enter the joker, a run of the mill thug who steals millions from gotham's top criminals, insults them, and then offers his services to exterminate batman. the joker manipulates the fears of gotham city and publicly asks the batman to reveal his identity to prevent the joker from killing innocent people. this makes bruce wayne question if has the inner strength to face a villain as sadistic as the joker. alfred tells him that batman because batman is incorruptible he must make the choices no one else can. he has to be the one to stand up to the joker. but bruce wayne is not as strong. many times he contemplates giving up on his quest. this bruce wayne is the most layered and interesting of all the bruce wayne's.

gotham has a new district attorney: harvey dent. he's a hero that the people need. a man working within the law. a man not hidden beneath a mask. he's the opposite, always out in the open no matter what criminal threatens him. dent, commissioner gordon, and batman team up to put crime away for good. the joker challenges them and forces each of them to make hard choices that will have a devastating impact on their lives no matter what they choose to do.

that's what the dark knight is about. heroism. what it truly means to be a hero and the consequences it brings. the hard choices that normal people can not make, and the results those choices bring. dent, gordon and batman each face consequences for their courageous actions, some more severe then others. by the end of the film they're never the same.

harvey dent has the same convictions as batman but he's not a strong. through tragic circumstances the joker twists his mind and turns him into a villain in the second half of the film. he becomes the key component in the jokers master plan to create chaos. the people look up to dent for protection and seeing him turn to the dark side would frighten the citizens to the point of madness. the joker is truly the devil. he finds weakness and human error and morphs it into evil. there has rarely been a villain this frightening.

the cast is an ensemble. and with the talents of christian bale, michael caine, morgan freeman, and gary oldman why not? everyone gets a chance to shine, including maggie gyllenhaal a beautiful and supremely gifted actress. her portrayal of rachel dawes makes katie holmes's last credible role nearly obsolete. no actor in this movie ,or any movie, is better than heath ledger. thanks to the cosmetic team he is unrecognizable, an oscar nod could be coming for them. he speaks with an thick chicago accent and never breaks it. he walks with a strange limp. he sucks on his cheeks because his face has been sliced open. his performance is a total performance: mind, body and soul. he was the joker, and his portrayal will be the definitive version of the character, sorry jack. if he doesn't win best supporting actor the academy should stop giving the award. god bless the actor brave enough to fill his shoes an a sequel.

"the dark knight" is easily the greatest comic book/super hero movie ever made. this is all because of the fearless direction of christopher nolan. there is no boundary he wont cross, and no idea he isn't willing to explore. he takes batman from the confined realm of comic books and brings him into reality. gotham city exists and it exists within us. we are the people of gotham, so frightened with threats, through fear so easily corruptible. christopher nolan lets us see our own human emotions at their very lowest, and fully explains why we need heroes, because heroes give us hope and take our fears away. hope is the movies key plot device and its an emotion worth fighting for.

"the dark knight" comes close to being one of the greatest movies ever made. i can only hope the stiffs at the academy recognize its brilliance. a comic book movie has never been this close to getting in the best picture race, and that's because none of them have been this good. the joker tells batman that they've changed gotham city forever and they can never go back. the dark knight has changed comic book movies forever, and i can only hope we never go back to the way it wasin 1997.

the dark knight is on a whole other level...its more of a crime style movie than comic book. much darker with the added cast member, the late, heath ledger portraying the joker. the beginning goes by a lil quick but for good reason. batmans new costume and batpod adds more to the action. we see a more mobile batman than its rubber constricted batman begins costume. harvey dent(aaron eckhart) does a great job but seems corny at certain scenes. eventually we see eckharts great acting skills towards the end. gary oldman does an amazing job as does morgan freeman and michael caine. finally there is a rachel dawes(maggie gyllenhaal) worth watching. but even though christian bale does a superb job as bruce wayne/batman, heath ledgers joker steals the show. he does get over the top screen time like nicholsons joker and it works better and with how terrifying he is in this movie...im glad we didn't see so much screen time(scratch that...every scene he was in left me smiled, amazed and terrified) saying he deserves an oscar isn't a far fetch thing. i may seem over praising but i was honestly skeptical on the hype for this...but for all the huge batman fans that enjoyed batman begins and yet wanted more...you get your wish...this is brilliant...i wont say its a "masterpiece" because thats an overplayed word...seems like everything is a masterpiece...this is just plain brilliant and one of the best movies i've seen in a very long time. aw heck...its a masterpiece ;)

the way it was filmed was brilliant. the cast was amazing! i loved every minute of it! simply the best super hero/comic hero movie ever made. nolan did a wonderful job. bale continued his role perfectly. gylenhal(spelling) was way better than holmes. ledger was amazing, probably his best movie. freeman added great humor. cane plays alfred perfectly. in fact everyone did an amazing acting job. the visuals were amazing and the action scenes were awesome. this was definitely the best movie of 2008 and one of the best movies of all time. i have already seen the movie twice and plan on seeing it a third time. it is that good. everyone should take time out of their busy schedules and go see this movie you wont be disappointed.

after several outstanding actions movies this year, we get the idea that filmmakers have finally started doing justice to the original sources, the stories of heroes that are flawed, strive to conquer evil and maybe eventually better themselves and the world. we had the joy of traveling the road with "ironman", with its flawed protagonist who tries very hard to use technology to defeat his nemesis. then indiana jones makes a return appearance, showing how age is taking its toll on his armor, giving us a couple of surprises and quite an ending for its installment. the much improved "hulk" benefits from a leaner screenplay and a great performance by norton, but nothing prepared for us the magnificent achievement that the sequel to "batman begins" turned out to be.

"the dark knight" is almost a perfect film. its sole blemish is a bit of miscasting, taking away a bit of the believability of the main character. leaving that aside, we welcome back michael caine's alfred, with his blend of sarcasm and fondness for his protégé. then morgan freeman's imposing technological wizardry, still works very well, as he must now decide whether he should follow bruce wayne in his new path. oldman's commissioner takes on more responsibilities and makes more dangerous choices, some of which will shock the audience.

it's the new arrivals that add the punch to this film, first eckart's two face is a wonder to behold in his transformation from the ultimate knight in shining armor to the tormented villain who descends into madness as the film reaches its conclusion. however, it is the wonderful and bewitching ledger who has the winning hand and turns what could be a regular drama into a powerful epic where evil has no reason and knows no fear. his joker is a perverse, demented, and killing machine, a creature that knows no boundaries, doesn't know the meaning of remorse or probably listens to his conscience anymore, if he ever had one.

his series of crimes begins with an assault on a local bank, and the execution of the heist is explosive and unforgiving, and if the audience is still catching his breath from the explosive happening, this sets the stage for worse things to come. soon this metropolis will have turned into hell and the joker is king, with batman soon struggling to find ways to control the chaos and realizing this might be the challenge of his life.

ledger's performance has many shades, incorporating a range of emotions hardly seen in any movies before. his madness is a very cool act, a performance for those who want to pay attention to the repulsive actions of a criminal who wants to test the mettle of a society that is slowly thinking into something more horrible than they want to believe. he knows this and grabs them by the throat, soon having them confront their fears and their natures. words like unbelievable will come to mind as we seen him do his joyful, demented celebratory dance, telling others that the world is about to end. if the film is not perfect, ledger is, a force to behold, and an intensity to match, and this where bale comes.

bale doesn't disappoint, and he delivers his most solid performance, as his caped crusader must use his wit, physical stamina, and his sense of morale to vanquish his biggest challenges. bale is now tormented by guilt and pain, like he has never seen before, and he might soon discover that he is someone he didn't know.

"the dark knight" is indeed a masterpiece, a film that weaves many elements, rarely seen in escapist entertainment, such as the superhero genre. we have a story dealing with human duality, with political and social ethics, with the fine line that separates sanity and madness, and what each might be. there are many floating metaphors in this film, such as the coin, the choice, the colors, the meaning of what truth really is. it is a fantastic achievement, and it should be honored and recognized by everyone who sees it.

last year i browsed this website and found the dark knight. i saw batman begins and loved it, which made me want more. i saw that there was going to be a sequel to it, called the dark knight. i waited and waited, finally a trailer came out and it made me more anxious. finally the day came. i bought tickets 2 weeks ahead of time online of course. i sat in the theater and waited anxiously. the film started and just from the beginning to the end credits was hard to find words for. in my review right now i don't want to talk about the plot or who plays who i will just tell you all this. acting is amazing and spot on for all actors but no one else tops the man of the 2 hours and 30 minutes that this film rolled... heath ledger. with his iconic and extraordinary performance as the joker... he blows jack nicholson's 1989 clown make-up completely off (no disrespect intended). i mean ledger was amazing. scary & funny. every time he came on screen i couldn't help but smile in amazement at his acting. but he couldn't have done it without christoper nolan. the joker's tone was set perfectly with the beginning scene (aka the pencil scene). also one of my favorite scenes was the hospital scene which will be a famous scene forever. but the joker wasn't the only thing that was great just everything was perfect.the acting was amazing. bale as the batman, freeman as fox, caine as alfred, and of course oldman as gordan. also the music throughout the whole movie set the tone for everything. if you have not seen this movie i recommend you do asap. oscars should be very abundant in this film ledger for best supporting actor as the joker. nolan for best director. maybe even best picture but its very rare for an action film to be nominated. that wont change my opinion though. overall 10/10

let me start off by saying this movie was nothing short of amazing best superhero movie ever. however, this movie is not and never will be worthy of being number one on that list. top 25? definitely. top 10? pushing it but i would say so. heath ledger's performance as the joker was without a doubt oscar worthy, one of if not the best villain and superhero movie performances, and a straight up amazing acting job. heath ledger was captivating throughout the entire movie, in all honesty i didn't really care if batman wasn't in the movie or not as long as the joker was. but don't get me wrong everybody else in the movie was great bale (best batman ever) freeman and caine (two of the best of all time) and eckhart ( second best in the film) and gyllenhall was terrible. the action sequences were perfect as well and not over done at all. the overall theme or idea of the film being anarchy and revenge i definitely enjoyed, reminded me a lot of v for vendetta. there were few problems with the dark knight but if u have one problem to me your not the best. it was a little dragged out, the scarecrow scene was unnecessary. maggie gyllenhall was awful, they're 0 for 2 casting that role and finally it didn't have that surprise ending that people including me love, thats why fight club, the prestige, memento, the usual suspects are all so great. so all in all fantastic movie top 10 worthy just not number one.

just to let everyone know, you must go see this movie. it is by far the best batman movie ever made. in fact, it is the greatest superhero movie ever made. before watching this movie, i thought that spiderman 2 was the greatest superhero movie of all time. the casting for that movie was great, but the casting in the dark knight exceeded my high expectations and deserves all the praise that they receive. christopher nolan (director and writer) made me want to be a superhero again. his direction of the script and the casting of ledger as the joker made going to the movies fun again. especially after watching two scenes in this movie. 1) erasing the pencil and 2) walking out of the hospital.

just to let everyone know, heath ledger was not in this movie. i constantly looked for him and couldn't find him. his role of the joker was so fascinating that i couldn't even see him under the makeup. he played the joker how the joker should be played, an evil, chaotic person that will kill someone off the whim just to get his point across. i would go as far as saying that he made jack nicholsons' joker look like a clown. the best thing about the joker was that he was not a wimp, he took on batman, fists to fists, and held his own. to me, that is the joker, he is crazy, insane, intelligent, and understands he wouldn't be anything without batman, because they complete one another.

harvey "two-face" dent was played by aaron eckhart and he put tommy lee jones to shame because he had one goal in mind and that was to clean up the city of gotham, but he was willing to either do it the right way, or the wrong way as long as the job was done. as harvey dent, eckhart made him a character that would go to extremes to clean up gotham. but as two-face, his role changed into a man that wanted revenge for the loss of a loved one. the thing i loved the most about two-face this time around is that he looked just like two-face in the comics, his face was burnt to a crisp on one side, while keeping his original look on the other side. there were not high amounts of color in this movie, unlike batman forever.

as far as batman, played by christian bale, there is not much to say except that he is by far the greatest batman ever. michael keaton held that post for so long, but we all knew in 2005 after batman begins that keaton's version was never as good as bale's. in this film we start to understand what it actually takes to be batman. he is torn apart by the actions of the people of gotham, some of them love him, while others believe he is part of the problem. this dramatic pull from both sides make bruce wayne want to turn himself in as the vigilante some thinks he is. then there is rachal dawes (played by maggie gyllenhaal) that is brucie's long time love. she is dating the new white knight of gotham harvey dent. this relationship makes bruce wayne to realize that as long he is the batman, he could never have that love from her. ultimately the movie twists and turns to help bruce wayne/batman make the decision to save the city, in turn letting the audience know who is the dark knight.

lt. james gordan, played by gary oldman was a superb performance. as you are watching the movie, like the joker you tend to forget who playing this role. oldman makes a perfect gordan, a clean cop that will do whatever it takes to make the city of gotham a great place again.

lucius fox played by morgan freeman brings more sly comments to this film like he did in batman begins. fox, the maker of the high-tech toys that batman uses has some tough decisions to make in this movie that relate to how he believes technology should not be able to view people's private lives.

alfred pennyworth, played by michael caine is as impressive in this film as the last. while in this film we truly understand how he is bruce wayne's second father in so many ways. he desires to protect him from pain while encouraging him to do the right thing.

as for the rest of the cast, they play very good roles that included good cops, bad cops, dead cops, mob bosses, mayors, and the public. the cast as a whole deserve more credit than i could give them, in fact some of them should win many awards, starting with the late heath ledger.

as for me, i dressed up in my best joker gear (no green hair or purple coat) and went to the midnight showing with a group of friends. i had a blast and the kids at the theater loved me. i did all of this dressing up and writing because in my life there has never been a movie more hyped and as great as this one. that is why i will continue to watch movies and hope that one day there may be a movie as great as the dark knight.

comic book movies are just getting better and better aren't they? recently we've had iron man, the incredible hulk, and the less recent spider man 2 which add depth and characters as strong as the superheros are. i'm sick of these special effects extravaganzas that ignore the human factors behind the superpowers. with some of these movies it's all about actiony explosions and cartoonish villains. these movies look pristine, but they're pretty weak at the core. yes special effects look pretty, and they fully entertain some simplistic audiences, but i need something a little more complex. the dark knight does just that. not only did it have excellent special effects and action, it had one hell of a brilliant story for a summer blockbuster.

batman is back but not too adored by the citizens and police of gotham. he is gaining a rep as a villainous criminal in a mask. one of the only people in law enforcement who does believe in him is commissioner gordon (gary oldman). behind the mask, bruce wayne isn't doing too well either. he really wants to help gotham get back on solid ground, but until then he still needs to be batman. and the longer he stays batman the longer his love rachel dawes (maggie gyllenhaal) distances herself from him. she is even dating the strong willed new district attorney harvey dent (aaron eckhart), who believes in helping the people of gotham and stopping the mob and crime in the city once and for all. however it is here that a new villain shows up, who starts up with armed robbery and tangles with the mob, and soon starts his own reign of absolute chaos. his name is the joker (heath ledger), wearing white makeup and a carved grin on his face. without any desire for money or fame, all he wants is to terrify people and cause chaos until the heart of gotham cracks in half, and people start to turn on each other just like he wants. out of control and unrestrained, the joker only gets increasingly more dangerous and powerful, and it's up to batman to stop him. or gotham is going to literally crumble.

i've been waiting for this movie since i saw the ending of batman begins in theaters. i remember the second the joker card appeared, people in the crowd started clapping with joy. and i thought to myself, oh this is gonna be good! a few years later, after lots of anticipation, i finally saw the dark knight in imax about a week ago. "good" doesn't justify this movie. "one of the best movies of the decade", and "one of the best villains of the decade" ought to do the trick! this movie contains some of the strongest performances and storytelling i've ever seen in a comic book adaptation. christian bale is excellent at both bruce wayne and batman, although his "bat" voice is a little over the top. however the character of bruce wayne gets a little undershadowed here because of the joker, but his character is still developed well. and the ending truly breaks new ground. his character was done better in batman begins, but that's because it was an origin story. gary oldman, michael caine, and morgan freeman all have their captivating moments in this film. although the rachel dawes character is still a little dull, maggie gyllenhaal is a far better actress than katie holmes. however the two best performances come from aaron eckhart and heath ledger, who truly provide the light and the darkness of this movie. eckhart is charming and powerful as harvey dent, and as the infamous two face is nothing short of excellent, especially for his screen time. two face looked wonderfully gruesome, and comparing the great tommy lee jones to aaron eckhart. tommy boy barely even comes close, surprising right? but the real buzz of the dark knight comes from the late heath ledger, who damn well deserves a post-humus oscar for this role.

the joker is far more sinister and threatening here than he was in batman 89'. first off heath looks pretty creepy in the makeup, second off the character is just creepy in general. in batman 89' the joker tried to poison the streets of gotham, and ended up failing miserably. in the dark knight the joker just randomly decides to blow up a hospital, making everyone rush to the exits to barely get out in time. the joker is very unrestrained, random, and downright twisted in his decision making. "i'm a dog chasing cars", he tells harvey dent, "i wouldn't know what to do if i caught one." he goes on to say that he just does things without any plan, because people don't panic under a plan. but with chaos "everyone just loses their minds!" he's absolutely right, and this is what makes the dark knight's joker one of the greatest movie villains in a long time. heath ledger plays him so well that you completely forget it's him, and even if he hadn't died i wouldn't praise his performance any less.

the dark knight is deeply disturbing, riveting, and chaotic experience. your eyes feast on the visuals of batpods, truck-flips, and "pencil tricks" (wink wink). while your brain is treated to powerful, mind blowing storytelling and performances. there are very few disappointments in the dark knight, but those few never overcome the great. the director christopher nolan tells his story with both breathtaking visuals, and disturbingly unforgettable emotion. i give the dark knight a 5 out of 5. can you believe we graduated from batman & robin to this? neither can i.

this is the best film of 2008 (a lot of people says that and it's true).

i finished the film with satisfaction, some unsolved questions and wanting more more of batman, joker and two face.

the first film i saw from ledger was a knight's tale, an achronic and funny middle age film. people thought that he was going to turn into a new teen star that would make girls shouting but then came ang lee's brokeback mountain about a love story between two cowboys. critics and people acclaimed this film and ledger turned (along with his partner in the film jake gyllenhaal) into a new promise of acting. he was also a great and funny casanova. it's a shame because he was a great joker and he did it psychotically awesome. we'll miss ledger but we won't forget that joker (more different than nicholson's). the most curious thing is that he worked with the two gyllenhaal brothers before dying.

aaron eckhart was always a secondary role actor and a usual indie film actor. i saw him in the black dahlia and he did right as a mysterious detective and boxer. i was hoping that his harvey dent will be better than tommy lee jones ' cartoonish character. and it was better, much better. he put soul and sense to the gotham city d.a. a very complex character, full of wrath and letting the chances to the destiny. aaron eckhart can make a real two-faced character.

the rest of the cast is also great. christian bale is definitely the best batman, gary oldman is also brilliant (as always) and maggie gyllenhaal (since i saw her in stranger than fiction) made a rachel dawes different than katie holmes. everything has been said about morgan freeman and michael caine. they are gods. their short presence are charming.

the action scenes are really correct and, of course, the epic soundtrack by two 'big guys': james newton howard and hans zimmer.

i also don't forget the participation of the rest of the cast (william fichtner, cillian murphy, eric roberts, anthony m. hall, nestor carbonell, etc).

" ladies & gentlemen , we are tonight's entertainment " proclaims the joker , perhaps he should have said " our time's entertainment " ! the dark knight is a complex puzzle , which truly reminds us "what movies are really all about" 70 years ago in the month of may , mr.bob kane imagined & gave us a caped crusader , bruce wayne. hollywood was then entering it's golden age. 4 movies & 6 decades later, christoper nolan captured the imagination of our childhood hero in batman begins. but with this installment he has moved the genre to it's rightful place why is it the perfect movie of this genre ? knockout performances by every casted actor.

christian bale & aaron eckhart take the cake , but heath ledger , bless his soul , was actually in a state where he couldn't possibly do anything wrong. i have never seen a performance so eccentric , powerful & yet at the same time so convincing. nicholson , mr.kane felt , was born to play the joker but i wonder what he would have said now. but as they say "to each time , it's own".

michael caine ,maggie gyllenhaal ,gary oldman & morgan freeman were also very important & i feel they did more than just justice to their characters.

this is a story of a man trying to solve the complex puzzle of life , heroism , rejection , hatred & most crucially the moral ethics & dilemmas posed by his nemesis. this movie is actually a psychological horror. so be prepared ! & also , there are surprises which you might have never thought existed! the background score by hans zimmer & james newton howard is amazing . this movie is a perfect example where the special effects doesn't effect human emotions at all . which is , honestly , rare these days .

the success of this movie also lies tenderly on christopher nolan dedication to his work not only as a director but with jonathan nolan on the screenplay & david s. goyer on the story . they created characters we come to care about ,which is lacking in so many movies nowadays . their screenplay is very poetic.

the movie is brilliant on so many levels that it should only be experienced rather than just commented upon. it's really hard to find fault with the dark knight !!! most importantly , in this movie , heath created for us a man we'll never forget . like the terminator , jack sparrow , indiana jones & so many others , they are born because those actors believed that they could truly give us someone we'll love , no matter how bad or silly they were . they are the one's we'll remember & cherish forever . that is how the become legends . they are the one's who teach us the magic touch of commitment.

heath , you truly put a smile on my face ! thank you . . . god bless ! p.s. - if at all there is a chance of bringing the joker back , johnny depp should give it a shot , though , as of now , it's hard to imagine anyone come close to heath's legendary performance , but depp's eccentricity could ,or nearly, match ledger's . . . hopefully .

let me start by saying i have been looking forward to this movie since i first saw batman begins. the character development of batman by showing his beginning allowed us to understand him and truly believe his virtues. chris nolan's batman isn't like any other batman or any superhero we've come to know through film for that matter; he's deep down just a person. of course there are special effects and some unrealistic elements, but nolan's batman leaves out all of the typical overly fantastic elements that make superhero movies nothing more than some cheap entertainment. because of this tdk already had a lot going for it. for the hardcore fans and regular movie-goers alike, we are able feel true compassion for bruce, rachel, and the remaining uncorrupted souls of gotham and feel true fear of the joker and gotham's villains. we're not accustomed to seeing such depth and overwhelming emotion in such a film.

while the story, intense action, and message in this film make tdk a gem by themselves, the real reason this movie is so incredibly good is because of the phenomenal acting talent of the cast. christian bale was perfect in batman begins and continues to perform at the highest level here. ever since his first major role in empire of the sun, bale has been turning heads. if you haven't seen empire of the sun, the machinist, american psycho, or the prestige, i recommend them all. he's just brilliant. i probably needn't mention ledger, but wow, what a performance. heath's transformation into the joker is perhaps one of the most sinister and terrifying things i've ever seen. many have been talking of a posthumous academy award for ledger and i wasn't sure if i bought it, but after seeing his truly inspiring work in tdk, i don't see any reason why he shouldn't be given such an honor. i could go on for hours about ledger, but so much of the greatness in the film comes from the others as well. gary oldman is hands down regarded as one of the best actors in hollywood. he's the eastern terrorist in air force one, the alcoholic irish mobster in state of grace, the psychotic and corrupt dea agent in leon, and zorg in the fifth element. this man has no bounds and remains one of the best character actors ever, giving another top performance here, showing once again his amazing ability to become almost unrecognizable from one role to the next. michael caine (one of my favorite actors), morgan freeman, and maggie gyllenhaal (who i wasn't so sure about at first) are all at there prime here in tdk. i wasn't sure if aaron eckhart would do the trick after seeing the core and some other mediocre films of his, but he shows plenty of talent as well playing the gotham da harvey dent and of course his more sinister role later in the film. the bottom line is that the acting in the film is easily some of the best i've ever had the privilege to seen.

in short, this film is pure excellence. after seeing it twice, i'm still thinking nothing but oscar gold. do yourself a favor and go see this in theaters. it's an experience that will put you on the edge of your seat for all of its glorious 150-some minute runtime. 10/10 for this one, a movie that will undoubtedly become one of the greatest movies of our time.

uhmmm how do i start. this latest batman movie is everything a batman fan wants to watch in a movie. but it isn't the typical superhero movie, it's a dark drama and a mind blowing thriller that will leave you breathless. the film is great, its exciting, spectacular, full of action and adventure, suspense and mystery to the fullest and some nice black humor in selected moments, it will keep on the edge of your seat the whole time. the story is excellent, it is one of the best adaptations from a comic book, of course with some changes but only for the benefit of the movie. the plot is very well developed, batman and gordon find alliance with a newly appointed da harvey dent to stop a vicious killer with a warped sense of humor known only as the joker, a threat to both the good, and the evil of gotham city but some circumstances will change everything. the cast is one of the best ones in a move, christian bale is very good as batman, he is a great actor and confirms that is one of the best batman's ever. heath ledger steals the show, his performance is flawless, you really can see a demented person whose only joy is to kill and create chaos, with this role, his final one, he stops being a great actor to become one of the greatest. aaron eckhart has a superb performance as harvey dent/two face, michael caine, morgan freeman and gary oldman as great actors, their performances were really convincing and maybe the weakest one in her acting was maggie gyllenhaal but still very good and decent. well my conclusion is that the dark knight is the best movie of the summer, the best batman movie maybe just behind tim burton's batman and a movie that will be remembered for a very long time.

i saw it this weekend and i think the entire first hour was filled with anticipation as i watched things begin to unfold. the clearest reason i can give for that is because i was definitely enjoying it already, and since i knew there was much more to come i could only hope that the movie kept up the pacing and tension, i wasn't let down either. the ending was much better than the previous batman movie too for me, there's much much more tension to it than just a near miss on "guy gets girl". this one also had less mystical overtones and more relevant social commentary with the portrayal of harvey dent as a great political hope for gotham...

******spoiler******** also, bruce wayne's use of technology to tap several million cell phones, and morgan freeman/lucius fox's response to that was an excellent poke in the eye of the current administration's policies (imo), especially in light of the most recent fisa bill.

the contrast between the white knight and the dark knight was well done, especially in light of the fact that these are purely iconic symbols that don't actually reflect the person that embodies each symbol. in the earlier scene where harvey dent was threatening the schizophrenic and bruce showed up to tell him that the people couldn't have their one true hope be seen like that was excellent foreshadowing and painted dent's willingness to give way to psychopathic behavior quite well.

harvey dent's characterization of two face was great, though that aspect of the story was much smaller than the overarching joker storyline. i personally like the gritty realism that his character had so much better than earlier portrayals of him as just some comical side-kick. the use of the two-headed coin as a symbol of rachel's death and his newfound two-faced persona played out nicely.

the focus of the emotional tole on christian bale didn't come out as well as it possibly could have, but there is room for that in future movies. ******/spoiler********

incidentally i'm not sure i can recall the last movie to have a score that high on imdb after 45,000 votes. usually movies start out with high scores (obviously due to studio's gaming the imdb voting system at movie release) but after a few thousand the initial attempts at swaying a score are more normalized. people seem to have enjoyed this one, and it's definitely worth it. very happy at the length of the movie too though i did notice that some people were squirming shortly before the 2 hour mark.

this movie has left deep repercussions to my mind. this is a masterpiece of epic proportions , one which will certainly define this era. i feel privileged to be a part of the dark knight era .

this movie is one of the best ever. it has redefined cinema, everything from the cast, acting, cinematography, background score, sound effects, storyline was just perfect, i could not believe at first, that how can everything about a movie be so perfect at the same time.
