i have seen the movie many times like more than 50 times and i loved the acting skills of christian bale and heath ledger.heath ledger plays the role of iconic villain this world has ever seen.a must watch movie. also the roles of morgan freeman has been as usual one of the best in the movie.the concept of multi-millionaires looking after the world and its prosperity is one of the best concept ever.christopher nolan as the director has done a great job and his visions are clearly one of the best and his direction is as good as anything.but to wrap up heath ledger is the one who raised the level of the movie many folds.this is one of those movies where even though villain loses at end but still wins the heart of the audience through his attitude and acting skills in the movie.overall the movie is must watch and one of the best movies ever made.please do watch the movie and share your reviews.

many critics and fans thought jack nicholson would flop as the joker in the 1989 "batman" movie. they were surprised to be proved wrong. many critics and fans thought john candy's last film, a western-spoof called "wagons east," would be hilarious. they were disappointed at being proved wrong.

many critics and fans prayed that the dark knight would prove to be worthy of heath ledger's considerable talents. their prayers were answered.

i have seen this movie twice, now. partly, because of one theater's lousy sound system. but, mostly, because i just plain liked it.

ledger's joker has a more gothic-look than nicholson's. more similar to brandon lee's version of the crow. and, the maniacal laugh sounds like an angrier, edgier version of the one used by mark hamill for the 1990's cartoon version!

add to that, some truly frightening actions (i literally jumped in my seat when that hanged corpse came crashing against the window!), and you have a new kind of joker. one you would have no trouble believing when he professes to being an agent of chaos. in fact, i would be willing to go one step further and call this joker the personification of chaos!!!

because, as played by the late, great heath ledger, this joker is waging a one-man war against order. never mind the law!

as for the rest of the cast? maggie gyllenhaal reminded me more of a brunette kirsten dunst, rather than katie holmes. but, she still put in a masterfully poignant performance as ada rachel dawes. and, aaron eckhart, who i remember only from the romantic comedy "no reservations," surprised me with the convincingness with which he played harvey dent.

tommy lee jones and billy dee williams, eat your hearts out!

as for christian bale, michael caine, and morgan freeman? chances are good they'll be back for the next sequel. and, i can only hope that a slight quip made by mr. freeman--during the scene where lucius fox and bruce wayne discuss the lighter-weight batman costume--proves to be an accurate portent of who will be the next bat-foe to appear opposite mr. bale.

in summation, then (as harvey dent might've said): this movie is a fitting feather to posthumously put in heath ledger's proverbial cap. and, for that reason alone, you should all see this movie.

this movie will be remembered as one of the best superhero films ever made. christopher nolan's vision and style created a modern action- packed dark toned batman film, containing the best acting from many brilliant actors / actresses like christian bale who portrayed bruce wayne brilliantly, he created a sense of power and responsibly towards his character but also a taste of sadness from bruce's past. heath ledger shall be forever known as the best joker in film history. he established terrifying aspects on screen and psychological elements to the joker which makes him dangerous and evil. i love heath so much in this movie and no actor could of done it better than mr. ledger himself but of course there are many others, morgan freeman who played the smart lucius fox, maggie gyllenhaal and aaron eckhart; the casting director did an amazing job for this movie. seeing the joker and two face together made me so happy. the cinematography is stunning, so many well known move quotes like 'where is she?" if you haven't seem this movie, i would rush to your nearest movie store like hmv and get it quick, your in for a treat.

i have never written comments on movies before, but this one was so good in all aspects that i could not help it.

the story could not be written or told better, and the effects were so real, there was no feeling of being robbed by cgi. the score and cinematography were flawless.

all that being said, the absolute best piece of this masterful film, was the acting. christian bale performed to his regular brilliance, aaron eckhart did great justice in his portrayal of a "white night", that gets caught up in a moment of weakness and anger, and oldman, freeman, and caine rounded out a stellar cast.

but we have to set all of these performances aside, as it was heath ledger's portrayal of the joker, that stole the show. never has such a sadistic and utterly insane character been played in such a way that you can't help but be hypnotized by it. he had such a presence, that even while he was not in a scene, you could not wait for him to make his entrance. he played this role so convincingly that up until i left the theater, i completely forgot that an actor was playing the part. i am still in awe of the fact that heath ledger was so talented, that when you saw the joker, you did not see heath ledger, but instead a madman that had no rules and no boundaries, and of course a few scars and face paint.

it is truly sad that we lost such a talented human being, with the ability to play a part in a way that no one could ever emulate. he saved his best performance for last (not to mention the best villain portrayal ever), and my sympathy and best wishes go out to his family and friends.

the dark knight is dark, intriguing, and immensely entertaining. the best part of the movie is probably of course heath ledger's above-professional performance as the legendary batman villain the joker. ledger totally nailed the role by providing a dark, twisted performance that stays true to the comics while giving off a sinister, gripping atmosphere. christian bale, michael caine, and morgan freeman were great as well, while gary oldman and newcomer aaron eckhart delivered very enjoyable performances. i also like the fact that the film doesn't heavily rely on cgi, as do most other superhero films. it also has more realistic characters, weapons, and perception of the world. and while being completely dark isn't necessarily a good thing, the dark knight cleverly balances its tonal pacing, supplying humor when it is needed and being serious when it needs to be. the action is as good as ever, of course, and the final act was just mind-blowing as well as actually quite shocking (batman letting the public believe he murdered harvey dent when he was just protecting gordon's family). unfortunately, we don't really know what happened to the joker, though that is because of the unfortunate death of the actor who played the iconic character. overall, the film was incredible and breathtaking, and i personally brand it as one of the best comic book movies ever made as well as all time. for the people who never saw this film, start with batman begins, then see this film, and finish with the greatly enjoyable the dark knight rises. after you've seen the whole trilogy, you will want to see it again and again. unless you're not a fan of christopher nolan.

the dark knight exceeded my expectations completely. i thought batman begins was the greatest and that nothing could beat it but this one... there are no words. it is not superior than batman begins but batman begins isn't better either. they are exactly the same. the difference with this one is that it's darker and it has an all time iconic villain, the joker (heath ledger). the soundtrack was 10/10 thanks to the one and only hans zimmer. christopher nolan's writing and directing just keeps on getting better and better. his mind and his knowledge is from another world that no one can understand how well he uses it and how he maintains it intact. and of course, the cast. morgan freeman as lucius fox is just perfect. maggie gyllenhaal did a pretty good job even though we all wanted katie. gary oldman is the best james gordon that fits perfectly. michael caine is stupendous as being the best alfred pennyworth of all time! two face's character development was so well written and thanks to aaron eckhart, it was splendid to watch. the one and only heath ledger, may his soul rest in peace, shall be remembered as performing one of the best acting performances of all time and as portraying the best villain of all time. i just couldn't take his eyes off of him and it was just a joy to watch. and now.. the heart of everything... christian bale as batman. now, i don't care what people say about michael keaton and robert pattinson, none of them did what christian bale did. he is just in another level. a level that no one can quite comprehend. he is the best batman of all time and no one can tell me he isn't, otherwise. his performance is remarkable, his character is unforgettable. his batman voice is only him and the cape crusader shall always be him. with the soundtrack, christopher nolan, the cast, the sounds, editing, and everything else, this is truly an unforgettable masterpiece. now... why so serious?

in the modern era, we finally get the ultimate batman movie. the one that most fans have been waiting for since roughly the early eighties. christopher nolan, who rebooted the franchise with batman begins, gives us the excellent follow-up the dark knight. christian bale returns as the haunted bruce wayne and his caped alter ego batman, as do michael caine (as loyal butler alfred), morgan freeman (lucius fox, financial adviser and inventor), and gary oldman (lt. james gordon, who's about to get a big promotion). maggie gyllenhaal takes over for katie holmes in the role of d.a. rachel dawes, a much better trade, in my opinion. as in batman begins, chicago once again stands in for gotham city and the city looks even more nightmarish than it did in the previous film.

batman now has to contend with a town that has gone over the edge with both imitators (like a chubby, shotgun-toting batman) and a new criminal: the joker (the late heath ledger). unlike the previous men who have played the clown prince of crime, ledger's joker isn't interested so much in making a profit from his crimes, just the kick that he gets from causing havoc. i still wish that they had gone the route of the comic books and had joker actually have white skin instead of wearing make-up, but they do a good job with what ledger does with the character. he practically transforms the joker into his own. meanwhile, rachel, after breaking up with bruce, is now dating the new chief d.a., harvey dent (aaron eckhart), who we know is doomed to become the coin-flipping two-face. batman wants dent to be the white knight that he feels gotham needs in order to combat villains on the order of the joker while he is the dark knight of the title.

as dark as this movie is, i certainly hope that this isn't the last we see of certain characters that were shown in this movie.

wow! just stunned me away. this film was so incredible! the music, the takes, the shots, the acting! all of it! just stunning! but the greatest part of the movie was heath ledger and how he played the joker. the moves, the way he talked.. just the way he acted. he truly deserves to get the oscar for this performance. he just completely stole this movie from all the other actors. christian bale, michael caine, aaron eckhaart, morgan freeman.. all great actors, but they all fell in the shadow in this movie, because heath ledger just owned it! "want to see a magic trick. i'm going to let this pencil.. disappear! and then boom into the guys head! "and it's gone!".. wow.. heath ledger truly was a great actor and would probably have got even better if he wouldn't have passed away so young. but yeah.. like i said.. heath ledger owned this movie, and made this movie the best movie i've ever seen. 10 out of 10 for sure! r.i.p.

fans of the caped crusader got more than they bargained for when they flocked to theaters to see the long-awaited sequel to batman begins. the new franchise had ushered in a more violent but cerebral batman by focusing on the character development of bruce wayne (christian bale) and his psychological motivation to fight crime. with such a strong reboot to the series, expectations were very high for the dark knight and director christopher nolan delivered. the sequel fully realizes the potential of its superhero and villain arc with harrowing sequences of violence and chaos constantly erupting. the film's narrative explores the meaning of leadership and what it takes to fight evil in the modern world. the extended scope is necessary to capture the criminal mastermind joker (heath ledger), and focus on the more complex story of district attorney harvey dent (aaron eckhart). heath ledger's untimely death and glimpses of his makeup and performance created part of a box office draw rarely equaled in motion picture history. but not even the trailers and tv ads could prepare audiences for ledger's inspired and disturbing performance. ledger nailed the real essence of the joker and bore no resemblance to nicholson's caricature. the joker of the dark knight is not a simple murderer and bank robber. his goal is to inspire evil in others so that even the most law abiding citizen will be driven to commit acts of crime or murder.

at any opportunity, the joker tries to drive crime fighters toward crime by sowing the seeds of terror and chaos. he allows himself to fall into a police trap so that he can spring a more diabolical plot. he arranges to have two ferries full of passengers forced into committing mass murder against one another. he dresses restrained civilians as criminals so police will be responsible for murdering innocents. the combination of nihilism and violent eruption that defined the joker was achieved purely by ledger's own artistry and for that he should be considered for a posthumous academy award. despite christian bale getting top billing, ledger played a more important, challenging role in the film. wayne is well defined from batman begins and the joker is firmly established in the prologue, a bank heist in which all the accomplices are shot and the joker issues his tenet, which is a twist on nietzsche: "what doesn't kill you makes you stranger." but the central character in the dark knight is neither the joker nor batman. it's harvey dent. the film follows the major changes that transform him from the public attorney into dc comic book villain two-face. the bulk of the character development focuses on dent's complicated descent from a dedicated, fearless political figure, passionate about defeating criminals using the rule of law. this white knight of gotham lives by his tenet, "you either die a hero or you live long enough to see yourself become the villain." dent is able to achieve popularity and make good on his promise to put violent mafia figures behind bars mainly because batman is willing to do the dirty work and get no credit for it. as batman's success in the streets and dent's success in the courtroom push the mob organizations into an increasingly small corner, the joker appeals to the mob bosses and rallies them against batman. in the ensuing chaos, it becomes clear that dent lacks ethical principles. when he loses his girlfriend, rachel dawes (maggie gyllenhaal), and damages half his face in one of the joker's vicious schemes, dent turns his back on the law altogether. with some words of inspiration from the joker, dent transforms himself into two-face. dent had gone after criminals. but two-face preys upon cops, including lt. jim gordon (gary oldman), using a two-headed coin similar to the one nolan and bale used in the prestige. instead of magic tricks, however, two-face uses the coin to determine the fate of his victims.

the significance of the coin and of dent's prophetic quote about becoming a villain is to show how easy it is to succumb to chance and chaos in the absence of real principles. one of the themes of the dark knight is to evaluate how different characters respond to the pressures of leadership and of fighting evil. nolan hits upon a truth seemingly missed by the entire press corps: leaders must be willing to sacrifice their popularity to do what's right. this core message of the dark knight is demonstrated in a subplot about telecommunications surveillance taken right from the front pages of newspapers during the us debate about the homeland security act of 2007. bruce wayne uses government contractors to build an advanced telecom technology that taps into ordinary cellphones to triangulate and illuminate the location of anyone in gotham. the technology is the only way to locate and catch the joker. but when wayne enterprises' most trusted official, lucius fox (morgan freeman), finds out what wayne is up to, he says that no man should have that much power and tenders his resignation.

faced with an adversary who is threatening countless lives and the future of gotham, wayne understands the consequences if he doesn't do what's necessary to end the joker's campaign of terror. dent proves to be an unprincipled politician with a rotten core and no one but wayne/batman is willing to sacrifice popularity to win the fight against evil. ultimately, batman decides he must take the blame for the actions of two-face in order to defeat the joker and restore faith to the people of gotham. the decision has major consequences. gordon ultimately describes batman as, "not a hero. he's a silent guardian, a watchful protector...a dark knight." public perception is always secondary to batman. his principles guide him to defeat evil and save lives, but the result is his loss of popularity and respect. some things are more important than public perception.

the dark knight is the second installment in the re-imagining of the batman movie mythos. chris nolan along with sibling screenwriter jonah nolan and most of the returning cast and a few additions(one of which is no longer with us, sadly), created what could be essentially the greatest superhero movie of all times. many people can look at this movie and see it as either: a) an action packed superhero movie b)a crime drama c)a case-study on human morality d)all of the above. there are a lot of layers to this film. it starts with batman, harvey dent and jim gordon team up to take down the remaining crime bosses, but not all goes well when a new criminal mastermind wearing clown make-up starts to wreck havoc in gotham city, which ultimately leads to the big issue of this movie: no one is safe. as a superhero movie, we are told that everyone's safe, nobody gets hurt, the hero will save the day, good always thriumps over evil 100% percent. but no, the dark knight enters a realm of darkness, something we haven't seen since the empire strikes back. i can't think of any superhero movie, save for that piece of trash daredevil, where the hero's main squeeze gets taken out of the picture. it's simply scary, even more terrifying because it's real, it's plausible. the main villain in this film is perhaps the greatest evil of them all. it's more than his disfigured look, mannerisms and twisted sense of humor, he is crime's logical response to someone like batman, of course, the joker is someone that nobody understands. but somehow, his train of thought makes some sense in some creepy way, that's what scares me. the joker is perhaps the most terrifying incarnation of evil and it lies mostly on his nihilism, his complete and utter disregard for human life and rules, we can thank heath ledger's performance for this. to the joker nobody is pure. everybody has a price, even batman. the dark knight's greatest challenge is fighting this monster without crossing the line himself. batman ultimately in the face of apparent defeat near the end, sacrifices all he accomplished for the greater good, albeit in a slightly unclear manner. the rest of the cast does their job well. michael caine and morgan freeman never go beyond their mentor/assistant roles, though alfred continues to be the voice of reason and bruce's father figure. rachel dawes, by maggie gyllenhall certainly washes off the bad taste brought in by katie holmes and aaron eckhart plays a little like what you expect, but he too reaches the heart of darkness and can be at times as disturbing as the film's main nemesis. it's a shame the dark knight was snubbed at the oscars, this movie as well as the watchmen prove that comic book movies can be serious, intelligent and still be fun to watch.

wow. i've just come from a midnight screening of this movie and that's the only word i can come up with. this latest batman film really outdid the last one and i think all other comic book films ever made. christopher nolan is a genius! the way he uses the camera to give the feeling that gotham city is nothing but a barren land of skyscrapers is fantastic.

the special effects were amazing. but the real genius of this movie come from the fact that there are great actors working with a great script. christian bale has given another fine performance and it's really gotten to the point where i can't tell if he's an amazingly talented actor that can do mediocre work which everyone else perceives to be fantastic or whether he has actually consistently been working hard to come out with one fine performance after another. the rest of the cast, oldman, freeman, caine, and eckhart all give fantastic performances as always. and maggie gyllenhall also holds her own against some of hollywoods finest. but it's heath ledgers turn as the joker that is going to be talked about for years to come. i know i can't forget it. the writing for the joker in this film is a notch above the rest. this words that come out of the jokers mouth are at times so haunting that you get chills. and heath ledgers brings a madness to the character that will make this one of the all time great performances. this movie is fantastic in every aspect. i know it won't be considered for a best picture oscar probably but i think it is far more deserving than some art-house flick being released in the last five days of the year:) bloody fantastic movie!! i will be back in the theater for a second viewing this weekend

i know the joker is a comic book villain, but heath ledger played with it with same amount of creepiness that anthony hopkins did with hannibal lecter in the silence of the lambs. ledger really stole this movie from everybody, he even tops jack nicholson from the 1989 movie. his performance is enough to gave kids under 10 nightmares. christian bale give quite a humanity performance as bruce wayne/batman, so does gary oldman as lt. gordon. aaron eckhart is also quite appealing as harvey dent, so is maggie gyllenhaal as rachel dawes(replacing katie holmes), and michael caine and morgan freeman are also great. the action scenes will have you on the edge of your seat, and it surpasses batman begins(2005). my hats off too director christopher nolan, cause he took a comic book story, and made it very gritty and real, and it proves to be more then just a superhero movie. but heath ledger as the joker, is really what kept this movie on it's toes, he was really great, i hope he get's nominated. it's a real shame that heath ledger is not here to enjoy the success of it. he died in january at the 28, it is a real tragic loss, he was such a great actor, it's sad that his life was short, but he made quite an impact on the hollywood scene, this film is the best way we can remember heath ledgers talent. we'll always remember you heath ledger 1979-2008.

usually the superhero movies mostly show the fights and visual effects, but the batman is different, he started as normal human with fear in himself, but time after time, he started to explore the world, to know what himself become, until he become a batman, gotham's hero behind the shadows. not only fighting scenes, but also amazing plot and story, the actors are perfect and excellent. christ bale as batman, show his skill as batman actor, i also like morgan freeman, his talking style is always cool, michael caine with morgan freeman duet in many movies. gary old man as gordon is nice, believe the batman although he doesn't know who is behind the mask. and the best, heath ledger is perfectly to become the joker, his acting and improvised acting are very amazing. although many characters show only as complementary figures. but the dark knight is a amazing movie made by nolan. batman is the "real" superhero for me.

the dark knight is much more than a comic book film, a summer blockbuster or a high-sprawling action film. it is quite simply, a masterpiece.

story: the dark knight depicts a city that has gained faith for the eradication of crime under batman's stewardship while newly introduced harvey dent, has given the city hope for justice. but this quickly changes with the arrival of the joker who turns everything upside down. the story is magnificent in every way. from the mafia to the police; from the characterization of batman to the persona of the joker; all of the finer details in the script that are easily missed from a first viewing, become all the more apparent the more times you watch it. the story does have it's problems. at times, some sequences are left hanging with no explanation as to what happens next. moreover, upon increased viewings, there are plot holes that take away from the overall cohesion of the story while the resolution that batman and gordon come to at the end leaves one questioning its necessity. nevertheless, the story as a whole is still likely one of the best that have been told in a comic book film.

action: the action sequences are where this film really excels. the opening sequence that depicts a typical bank robbery is turned into a thrilling heist due to stunning cinematography, and a fantastic combination of hans zimmer's thrilling score, great dialogue and heart thumping action. the swat action sequence in the middle of the film may be one of the best vehicle action sequences on film in recent memory and certainly one of the best action sequences ever displayed in a comic book film. christopher nolan's commitment to real world stunts make these sequences even more thrilling as its realism draws you in. while all of the vehicle sequences (particularly those involving the batpod), are consistently fantastic, the combat scenes are sometime inconsistent. indeed, while the final fight sequence that pits batman against a swat team and joker's henchmen represents one of the most beautifully directed fight scenes put together in a comic book film, the first combat scene where batman appears for the first time, is remarkable incoherent. nevertheless the vast majority of the action scenes fall in line with brilliance rather than incoherence and together bring about a well- crafted action film overall.

cinematography/score: as noted above, the cinematography in the film is beautiful and majestic with many of the imax scenes bringing together jaw dropping visuals. the score is also fantastic with zimmer adding a couple beautiful new tracks to the already great batman begins soundtrack, including a special joker theme. however, the score in this film doesn't have that one theme that will ring in your ears long after you leave the theatre like ones from star wars, indiana jones or even to some extent the avengers. nevertheless, the score acts as an ensemble piece with each individual piece acting as a beautiful part to an overall majestic whole.

acting performances: it's hard to discuss acting without giving a nod to heath ledger's legendary performance as the joker. his performance in this film (so great that he received an oscar for it), may be one of the best performances in recent memory and is certainly the best performance ever brought forth in a comic book film. in fact, his performance is so great that he sometimes shines the light away from the other fantastic performances in this film. aaron eckart in particular is incredible as harvey dent as we see his character take a macbeth-like turn away from heroism. while, christian bale delivers a fantastic performance as bruce wayne, it is probably his worst in the trilogy simply because he isn't given as much to work with in this film. on the other hand, michael caine, morgan freeman and gary oldman prove that great ensemble casts can help to push a film over the edge of greatness.

favorite aspects & problems: while the action sequences (particularly the vehicle sequences), are in my opinion the best ever displayed in a comic book film, my favourite aspects are undoubtedly the long dialogue scenes of the joker. whether its his first appearance with the mob, his discussion about rules with batman in the interrogation room or his pep talk to dent in the hospital room, every scene is enthralling and entertaining no matter how many times you watch it. as you have seen from this review i have very few negatives which can be narrowed down to two. the first being the plot holes, which as i noted in the story category, are annoying and disruptive but don't take away too much from my overall experience. and the second would be the first action sequence with batman where he stops scarecrow and the mob. while the batman stopping the minivan was rather neat, the combat bits made it look like the henchmen were going down without a fight. better choreography would have helped in this case.

summary and rating: with some of the best action sequences, acting performances, dialogue, music, and cinematography, the dark knight is a revelation in filmmaking and a symbol for what directors should aspire to accomplish. it's accomplishments have become a spark to the passion of many aspiring filmmakers and have left many like me in awe of its brilliance. it seems the dark knight has in some ways, done to this generation what star wars did to the last so many years ago. the film is a masterpiece, and while some poor combat choreography and plot holes may cause it to be a flawed one, it is undoubtedly a must see and the best comic book film ever made.

this movie surpasses the hype. it is incredible. phenomenal. breathtaking. near-perfect. ok, i'm done.

christopher nolan has given us the batman film we've been waiting for (though "batman begins" was pretty darn good too). from the acting, to the story, the action, the sets, the score (love it) to the sheer quotability of the joker, this film blows your socks off. it grabs you and never lets go. i could watch this movie a thousand times and never tire of it.

the opening scene, the bank robbery, was a fantastic scene, and one of the best openings to a film ever. the score is chilling and the fact that the robbers are taking each out really adds to it. plus, when the bank manager, played by william fitchner (my favorite cameo in a film) comes out with his shotgun, shooting at the remaining robbers, you really see the chaos involved with the whole robbery. then you finally see....the joker. though brief, it sends chills down your spine.

the interrogation scene, the chase scene through the streets of gotham, and the final confrontation between batman and joker all really stand out.

christian bale, though criticized by some, gives what i believe is the best portrayal of bruce wayne. he's not supposed to be the happy, billionaire playboy like his character from the 1940s. he's a dark, unhappy man who is the only one capable of doing what he does. bale is great in this film. and if you still doubt bale as an actor, go watch "equilibrium" and "3:10 to yuma".

gary oldman, my gosh, how many roles can this man play? he's been commissioner gordon, a russian terrorist, dracula, sirius black, whoever the heck he was supposed to be in "the fifth element". this man is versatile! he brings a lot of heart to an otherwise one-dimensional character. i might even say oldman does the best job in the film, even better than ledger, eckhart, caine, and freeman.

michail caine and morgan freeman are both great, as usual, and provide good father-like figures for bruce wayne.

aaron eckhart does a fantastic job as harvey dent. i love how nolan makes you care for the character, then tries to turn you against him. eckhart gives a stellar performance.

maggie gyllenhaal should be banned from making movies. she can't act at all. she was horrible. she was laughing during a dramatic scene! this isn't "die hard" or "face/off". this is "the dark knight"! get with the program.

and finally, heath ledger. ledger had already done some impressive work with "the patriot" and "a knight's tale". this role has immortalized him in the film industry. he owned every single scene he was in. i've never seen a character like him. the voice alone was enough to frighten you, but add his ghoulish appearance and trigger-happy, knife-wielding, cackling attitude, and you got one scary dude. love it.

this film scared the crap out of me when i saw it, and i still get chills watching it. this is what movies should aspire to be.

the dark knight brings us batman as never seen before. finally a comic-based movie which not for little kids, the isn't afraid to show us batman as we want to see, the movie isn't afraid to unveil the joker's madness at it's full "madnessity". you get to see batman making life depending choices, his greatest dilemmas. this movie will actually make you think, what would you do? how would you act? commissioner gordon's amazing words on batman, harvey dent's amazing acts of heroism, luscious fox's bright mind, alfred pennyworth's life experience, bruce wayne's great manipulation of batman, the joker's sick- minded perception of the world and the people around, all the rich characters in this movie, the way that you actually see the world from everybody's point of view, you hear about their stories, will make you sit silently and be fascinated by it's amazing way it has been done. this movie is way more than just a batman movie, this movie is about all who is around him, this is story of gotham.

i just can't believe how great this movie was... i went in to the theater with the same expectations i had with spiderman sequels, and lotr sequels...and for the most part i was satisfied with both series...but the dark knight is different animal...all of my expectations were fulfilled and than some...what a great movie...all the actors gave top notch performances...and christian bale was excellent so was aaron eckhart...morgan freeman, maggy g., gary oldmen and michael caine did their parts flawlessly....and last but not least heath ledger..if he doesn't win an oscar for his performance i would loose all the respect i have for the academy..i couldn't believe how great this actor was...its a tragic that we have lost such a talent...the joker music is still ringing in my ears...chris nolan did a wonderful job with his brother writing script and directing. and if you haven't seen this movie in theater...please go check it out...this is what makes hollywood great, masterpieces like this. unbelievable movie making and tremendous acting performances!!

this film can be described using one word: epic. the film itself encompasses not only the archetypes and themes necessary for a good 'batman' film, but utilizes techniques and characters that make this film an overall outstanding piece of art. christopher nolan's impeccable vision for this film would have been daunting for another director of less clout (i.e. joel schumacher). not only has this film included a storyline evident in many 'batman' comic books: the outlaw vigilante; but this film also provided alternate perspectives and characteristics for the caped crusader. the replacement of katie holmes as rachel dawes (maggie gyllenhaal) was a great call. also, christian bale, michael cain, and morgan freeman had great performances. the run-away award winning performance by heath ledger was not only hauntingly amazing, but technically profound. heath ledger's joker was point on, it was what tim burton's and jack nicholson's tried to achieve but lacked. the joker is an agent of chaos, and this was perfectly portrayed in this film. another great performance given was aaron eckhart's portrayal of harvey dent/two face. his character provided another dimension to this timeless film. all in all, this film was fantastic. the only are for critique was that it ended! i was on the edge of my seat the entire film. the only painful thing to accept is that the joker will not be in the third installment. rest in peace heath ledger.

christian, bale that is, is back as batman. there is no reason to "bale" him out in the batman persona because undoubtedly christian bale continues to prove that he is the best batman thespian to put
